title: WIP: Initial Commit for the GPU Operator new home
body: This is reference implementation how to handle GPUs in a k8s/openshift cluster. Please see the README on how this operator works.

title: Same resource kind in one state
body:
In the `init` part, what we are doing currently in the `addResourcesControls` function (https://github.com/Ethyling/gpu-operator/blob/master/pkg/controller/specialresource/specialresource_resources.go#L70) is to find all yaml files from the state directory and fill a `Resources` structure with the objects found in them.

When there are two resources of the same kind in the same state directory, I think we are losing the information of the first one and we are only checking the second one. I think we should have a list for each type and iterate over it while the reconcile loop.

Am I missing something?
@zvonkok @rajatchopra

title: Namespaces and CRD naming
body:
Currently the CRD kind for the partitioning is `SpecialRessource`. I think we need to change that as it's really confusing. I think something like `SchedulingType` could be better. Any other ideas?

On another side, the namespaces names are `openshift-sro` and `openshift-sro-operator`. We need to change this. I don't know exactly which namespace is for what kind of resource. @zvonkok could you give us some details about this?

cc @RenaudWasTaken @guptaNswati @rajatchopra

body: Fix imports to point to the new GPU Operator repository

title: special-resource-operator fails to restart
body:
### 1. Quick Debug Checklist
- [x ] Are you running on an Ubuntu 18.04 node?

### 1. Issue or feature description
Running gpu-operator-1.0.0-techpreview.8 via helm, the `special-resource-operator` automatically deploy the gpu specialresource on initial run. If the pod restarts it enters a restart loop and errors out because the gpu resource already exists.

```
{"level":"error","ts":1580478272.0765631,"logger":"cmd","msg":"","error":"specialresources.sro.openshift.io \"gpu\" already exists","stacktrace":"github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/vendor/github.com/go-logr/zapr.(*zapLogger).Error\n\t/go/src/github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/vendor/github.com/go-logr/zapr/zapr.go:128\nmain.main\n\t/go/src/github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/cmd/manager/main.go:107\nruntime.main\n\t/usr/local/go/src/runtime/proc.go:203"}
```

### 2. Steps to reproduce the issue
- Deploy gpu-operator via helm: 
```
helm install --devel nvidia/gpu-operator -n gpu-operator --wait
```
- Wait for `special-resource-operator` to start and validate it's running 
```
kubectl -n gpu-operator get pods
```
- Simulate a restart of it by scaling to zero, then back to 1. 
```
kubectl -n gpu-operator scale --replicas=0 deployment/special-resource-operator 
kubectl -n gpu-operator scale --replicas=1 deployment/special-resource-operator
```
- Check that `special-resource-operator` went into a  `CrashLoopBackOff`
- Delete `gpu` to fix it. `kubectl -n gpu-operator-resources delete SpecialResource gpu`

title: nvidia driver image tag issue if you are using a nightly build of OCP 4.4 - rhcos4-4
body:
_The template below is mostly useful for bug reports and support questions. Feel free to remove anything which doesn't apply to you and add more information where it makes sense._

### 1. Quick Debug Checklist
- [ ] Are you running on an Ubuntu 18.04 node?
- [ X] Are you running Kubernetes v1.13+? 1.17.1
- [ x] Are you running Docker (>= 18.06) or CRIO (>= 1.13+)? 
crio version 1.17.0-4.dev.rhaos4.4.gitc3436cc.el8
- [ ] Do you have `i2c_core` and `ipmi_msghandler` loaded on the nodes?
- [ ] Did you apply the CRD (`kubectl describe specialresources --all-namespaces`)

### 1. Issue or feature description

### 2. Steps to reproduce the issue
Install an OCP 4.4 cluster on AWS (nightly build). Here we are using openshift-install-linux-**4.4.0-0.nightly-2020-02-17-103442**.tar.gz
 using this helm command :
```
 helm install --devel https://nvidia.github.io/gpu-operator/gpu-operator-1.0.0-beta.0.tgz --set platform.openshift=true,operator.defaultRuntime=crio,nfd.enabled=false -n openshift-operators --generate-name --wait
NAME: gpu-operator-1-1581954405
LAST DEPLOYED: Mon Feb 17 15:46:45 2020
NAMESPACE: openshift-operators
STATUS: deployed
REVISION: 1
TEST SUITE: None
```
We can find that the operator is installed but once it tries to deploy the resources they fail because it’s trying to use an image that does not exist in the docker.io/nvidia repository: 440.33.01-**rhcos4.4**. In the repository, at this moment, only **440.33.01-rhcos4.3** is published. 

We tried to change the values for the helm chart, we untar the helm chart and checking the image variable we can see in gpu-operator/templates/0320_configmap.yaml that it comes from some variables:

driver: "{{ .Values.driver.repository }}/{{ .Values.driver.image }}:{{ .Values.driver.version }}" 

We tried to change that value in gpu-operator/values.yaml but the operator include a fixed sufix “**-rhcos4.4**”, so even changing it to  440.33.01-rhcos4.3 the image that the operator uses will be 440.33.01-rhcos4.3-rhcos4.4.



### 3. Information to [attach](https://help.github.com/articles/file-attachments-on-issues-and-pull-requests/) (optional if deemed irrelevant)

 - [ ] kubernetes pods status: `kubectl get pods --all-namespaces`
 - [ ] kubernetes daemonset status: `kubectl get ds --all-namespaces`
 - [ ] If a pod/ds is in an error state or pending state `kubectl describe pod -n NAMESPACE POD_NAME`
 - [ ] If a pod/ds is in an error state or pending state `kubectl logs -n NAMESPACE POD_NAME`

 - [ ] Output of running a container on the GPU machine: `docker run -it alpine echo foo`
 - [ ] Docker configuration file: `cat /etc/docker/daemon.json`
 - [ ] Docker runtime configuration: `docker info | grep runtime`

 - [ ] NVIDIA shared directory: `ls -la /run/nvidia`
 - [ ] NVIDIA packages directory: `ls -la /run/nvidia/toolkit`
 - [ ] NVIDIA driver directory: `ls -la /run/nvidia/driver`
 - [ ] kubelet logs `journalctl -u kubelet > kubelet.logs`


Workaround found 
So what we did is to pull the image from dockerhub and push it in our private repo (making it public) changing the “repository” key in the values file (values.yaml):

driver:
  repository: luisarizmendi
  image: driver
  version: "440.33.01"

Once it’s done the pod can get the image and continue with the installation.
Image is available here : https://hub.docker.com/r/luisarizmendi/driver/tags
the image is just the same binary as the : docker pull nvidia/driver:440.33.01-rhcos4.3

maybe having the image version inside the "version" like version: "440.33.01-rhcos4.3" and not only "440.33.01" or having an additional field like platform  with platform : rhcos4.3 and not to identify the platform automatically because in our case we are using a 4.3 driver on top of rhcos4.4. And it works. 

I identified the line of code where the concatenation is done 
https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/9fdae4d499ab21457cb37f5e9cecbe6e65d27eac/pkg/controller/specialresource/specialresource_controls.go#L323
and the values is coming from the NFD annotation 
    feature.node.kubernetes.io/system-os_release.ID: rhcos
    feature.node.kubernetes.io/system-os_release.VERSION_ID: "4.4"

We can understand you can't change the code because you are responsible of the driver version and you will build a driver image for each os_release. VERSION_ID . Not sure it's needed for each RHCOS minor version.  Or just offering the flexibility to decide which image we want to use.

### 3. Information to [attach](https://help.github.com/articles/file-attachments-on-issues-and-pull-requests/) (optional if deemed irrelevant)

 - [ ] kubernetes pods status: `kubectl get pods --all-namespaces`

 - [ ] NVIDIA driver directory: `ls -la /run/nvidia/driver`
 - [ ] kubelet logs `journalctl -u kubelet > kubelet.logs`

Workaround 
Temporary driver fix workaround 
NVIDIA containers are contained and not privileged with an SELinux policy. The policy creates a new SELinux type: **nvidia_container_t** with which the container should run.

The used SELinux type “**container_runtime_tmpfs_t**” is not correct because of a bug with this beta code;
```
$ oc get pod
NAME                                       READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
nvidia-container-toolkit-daemonset-rcmnb   1/1     Running   0          19m
nvidia-driver-daemonset-2jw2k              1/1     Running   0          19m
nvidia-driver-validation                   1/1     Running   4          19m

$ oc exec -it nvidia-driver-daemonset-2jw2k bash -n gpu-operator-resources

[root@nvidia-driver-daemonset-p8dkp dev]# ls -Z /dev/nvidia*
system_u:object_r:container_runtime_tmpfs_t:s0 /dev/nvidia-modeset  system_u:object_r:container_runtime_tmpfs_t:s0 /dev/nvidia-uvm-tools  system_u:object_r:container_runtime_tmpfs_t:s0 /dev/nvidiactl
system_u:object_r:container_runtime_tmpfs_t:s0 /dev/nvidia-uvm      system_u:object_r:containe
```

Fix the SELinux type:
```
$ oc get pod
NAME                                       READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
nvidia-container-toolkit-daemonset-rcmnb   1/1     Running   0          19m
nvidia-driver-daemonset-2jw2k              1/1     Running   0          19m
nvidia-driver-validation                   1/1     Running   4          19m
$ oc exec -it nvidia-driver-daemonset-2jw2k bash -n gpu-operator-resources
[root@nvidia-driver-daemonset-2jw2k nvidia-440.33.01]# ls -Z /dev/nvidia*
system_u:object_r:container_runtime_tmpfs_t:s0 /dev/nvidia-modeset    system_u:object_r:container_runtime_tmpfs_t:s0 /dev/nvidia0
system_u:object_r:container_runtime_tmpfs_t:s0 /dev/nvidia-uvm        system_u:object_r:container_runtime_tmpfs_t:s0 /dev/nvidiactl
system_u:object_r:container_runtime_tmpfs_t:s0 /dev/nvidia-uvm-tools
[root@nvidia-driver-daemonset-2jw2k nvidia-440.33.01]# chcon -t container_file_t  /dev/nvidia*
[root@nvidia-driver-daemonset-2jw2k nvidia-440.33.01]#
```

```
$  oc get pod nvidia-driver-validation -o yaml -n gpu-operator-resources | oc replace --force -f -
pod "nvidia-driver-validation" deleted
pod/nvidia-driver-validation replaced
```


Check again the SELinux context, “**container_runtime_tmpfs_t**” is replaced by “**container_file_t**”:
```
$ oc exec -it nvidia-driver-daemonset-2jw2k bash -n gpu-operator-resources
[root@nvidia-driver-daemonset-2jw2k nvidia-440.33.01]# ls -Z /dev/nvidia*
system_u:object_r:container_file_t:s0 /dev/nvidia-modeset    system_u:object_r:container_file_t:s0 /dev/nvidia0
system_u:object_r:container_file_t:s0 /dev/nvidia-uvm        system_u:object_r:container_file_t:s0 /dev/nvidiactl
system_u:object_r:container_file_t:s0 /dev/nvidia-uvm-tools
```


Success, validation is passed (pod nvidia-driver-validation completed):

```
$ oc get pod -w
NAME                                       READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
nvidia-container-toolkit-daemonset-rcmnb   1/1     Running   0          27m
nvidia-driver-daemonset-2jw2k              1/1     Running   0          27m
nvidia-driver-validation                   1/1     Running   0          3m8s
nvidia-driver-validation                   0/1     Completed   0          3m39s
.......

body:
Hi guys,

we are using the GPU operator successfully in our clusters but noticed one problem after reinstalling a single host of the Kubernetes cluster causing it to have a more recent kernel version than the other nodes.

The reason is that the `nvidia-driver-daemonset` has a `nodeSelector` for the kernel version of the host it runs on (and yes I saw https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/issues/21 :)): https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/27d1dc5863d5eb68d0b95e3bfe8b025e7a8787b6/pkg/controller/specialresource/specialresource_controls.go#L236-L238

After removing the kernel version nodeSelector the driver-daemonset pod ran fine, or is there still a reason to keep this after the 1.0.0 release?
The other ticket linked above also says that it should be removed in Feb-March - was it maybe _missed_ before the 1.0.0 release?

I could also try to do a PR if this helps with getting it done quicker.

Thanks,
Vincent

title: Docker unusable after reboot due to missing /run/nvidia directory
body:
Hi,

we noticed another IMO really critical issue with the GPU operator that happens after rebooting a system, we are using the 1.0.0 version.

### Issue Description
The GPU operator missuses the `/run` mount as per the [Linux Filesystem Hierarchy Standard](https://refspecs.linuxfoundation.org/FHS_3.0/fhs/ch03s15.html):

> This directory contains system information data describing the system since it was booted. **Files under this directory must be cleared (removed or truncated as appropriate) at the beginning of the boot process.**

If this directory is missing you are not able to start any docker container as the container-runtime configured for docker in the `/etc/docker/daemon.json` is not available as `/run` and the contained symlink to the `nvidia-container-runtime` are missing after reboot.

### Further Explanation
This prevents docker and thus also all Kubernetes components on that node from starting with the following error:
```
$ sudo docker run --rm -it alpine
Unable to find image 'alpine:latest' locally
latest: Pulling from library/alpine
c9b1b535fdd9: Already exists 
Digest: sha256:ab00606a42621fb68f2ed6ad3c88be54397f981a7b70a79db3d1172b11c4367d
Status: Downloaded newer image for alpine:latest
docker: Error response from daemon: OCI runtime create failed: unable to retrieve OCI runtime error (open /run/containerd/io.containerd.runtime.v1.linux/moby/115fc504d4d2f9dcfbf1b801ba3d32ec1923c7bda96477c936fca27bb6553045/log.json: no such file or directory): fork/exec /run/nvidia/toolkit/nvidia-container-runtime: no such file or directory: : unknown.
```
If you check the `/etc/docker/daemon.json` you see the reason, the path for the default runtime does not exist.
```
cat /etc/docker/daemon.json
{
  "runtimes": {
    "nvidia": {
      "path": "/run/nvidia/toolkit/nvidia-container-runtime"
    }
  },
  "default-runtime": "nvidia"
}
```
The operator creates the directory `/run/nvidia` with the following content during the driver installation (IIRC):
```
$ ll /run/nvidia/
total 4
drwxr-xr-x  2 root root   80 Mar  9 15:31 ./
drwxr-xr-x 30 root root 1080 Mar  9 15:31 ../
lrwxrwxrwx  1 root root   25 Mar  9 15:31 toolkit -> /usr/local/nvidia/toolkit/
-rw-r--r--  1 root root    6 Mar  9 15:31 toolkit.pid
```
If this is missing there is also no valid symlink to the `nvidia-container-runtime` located in:
```
$ realpath /run/nvidia/toolkit/nvidia-container-runtime
/usr/local/nvidia/toolkit/nvidia-container-runtime
```

Why is `/run` being used and why don't you just use the realpath instead of the symlink going through `/run/nvidia`?

BR, Vincent

title: Documentation should call out that Openshift doesnt support multiple 'roles' on nodes
body:
https://github.com/openshift/machine-config-operator/issues/269

Ran into an issue were i couldnt get the entitlement MC to roll out on my Openshift 4.4 RC1 pre-release.  I also observed the issue on 4.3.8.  Basically, you cant have nodes with two roles.  The MCP/MC doesnt handle it at all and your entitlement rollout will get stuck.  I ended up just boiling down to a single role for every node and creating an MCP for 'infra' and 'nvidia' nodes.  Creating this issue so others dont spend days pulling their hair out like i did.

title: Helm chart v1.0.0 is actually a nightly version
body:
Hi,

it seems that a nightly gpu-operator version was incorrectly tagged as v1.0.0, see the last line:
https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/0328060705f5f8c73a030fdd4f66776f7707739a/index.yaml#L4-L19

Proof:
```
 $ helm template --version "v1.0.0" nvidia/gpu-operator | grep nightly -B2
      containers:
      - name: special-resource-operator
        image: nvidia/gpu-operator:1.0.0-nightly-64ae160d
```

I guess this is unintended as the old v1.0.0 is still there and you probably don't plan to retag versions.

BR, Vincent

title: Nvidia container toolkit build for RHEL 7 https://hub.docker.com/r/nvidia/container-toolkit
body:
_The template below is mostly useful for bug reports and support questions. Feel free to remove anything which doesn't apply to you and add more information where it makes sense._

### 1. Quick Debug Checklist
- [ ] Are you running on an Ubuntu 18.04 node?
- [x ] Are you running Kubernetes v1.13+?
- [x ] Are you running Docker (>= 18.06) or CRIO (>= 1.13+)?
- [x ] Do you have `i2c_core` and `ipmi_msghandler` loaded on the nodes?
- [ x] Did you apply the CRD (`kubectl describe clusterpolicies --all-namespaces`)

### 1. Issue or feature description
I am noticing when trying to set GPUs up on a RHEL worker that the nvidia-container-toolkit compiles the nvidia-container-cli with a GLIBC version that is not compatible with RHEL 7. This leads to the following errors when deploying either the gpu-operator or the https://github.com/openshift-psap/special-resource-operator (this is an Openshift 4.3 environment).

```
Events:

  Type     Reason     Age        From                    Message

  ----     ------     ----       ----                    -------

  Normal   Scheduled  <unknown>  default-scheduler       Successfully assigned nvidia-gpu/nvidia-gpu-device-plugin-qdfmn to 10.177.155.99

  Warning  Failed     7m55s      kubelet, 10.177.155.99  Error: container create failed: time="2020-04-27T19:53:10-05:00" level=warning msg="signal: killed"

time="2020-04-27T19:53:10-05:00" level=error msg="container_linux.go:349: starting container process caused \"process_linux.go:449: container init caused \\\"process_linux.go:432: running prestart hook 0 caused \\\\\\\"error running hook: exit status 1, stdout: , stderr: /run/nvidia/toolkit/nvidia-container-cli.real: /lib64/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.27' not found (required by /run/nvidia/toolkit/libnvidia-container.so.1)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\"\\\"\""

container_linux.go:349: starting container process caused "process_linux.go:449: container init caused \"process_linux.go:432: running prestart hook 0 caused \\\"error running hook: exit status 1, stdout: , stderr: /run/nvidia/toolkit/nvidia-container-cli.real: /lib64/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.27' not found (required by /run/nvidia/toolkit/libnvidia-container.so.1)\\\\n\\\"\""
```

It appears there needs to be a new version built of this image to support RHEL 7: https://hub.docker.com/r/nvidia/container-toolkit/tags. Are there any plans for that? Would you mind pointing me to the upstream repo that actually has the docker files that build those images?

### 2. Steps to reproduce the issue
Deploy GPU operator or SRO https://github.com/openshift-psap/special-resource-operator in an Openshift 4.3 cluster with RHEL 7 workers. Once the prestart hook is set: all new containers will fail with the above error

### 3. Information to [attach](https://help.github.com/articles/file-attachments-on-issues-and-pull-requests/) (optional if deemed irrelevant)

Basically the runtime hook that is created with the runtime-enablement container `nvidia/container-toolkit:1.0.0-alpha.3` has it's nvidia logic compiled with the glibc version that corresponds to Ubuntu 18.04. Do I potentially need a different container for the RHEL 7.8 kernel? I tried `nvidia/container-toolkit:1.0.0-beta.1-ubi8` as well but that want into a crash loop.

title: NVIDIA GPU-Operator does not work on Openshift 4.3 or Openshift 4.4
body:
There is a lot of existing documentation out there that points to the NVIDIA GPU Operator being GA. Documentation below:
https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/kubernetes/openshift-on-gpu-install-guide/index.html
https://devblogs.nvidia.com/nvidia-gpu-operator-simplifying-gpu-management-in-kubernetes/
https://www.openshift.com/blog/creating-a-gpu-enabled-node-with-openshift-4-2-in-amazon-ec2
https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4908611

However, none of these result in a functioning GPU system or deploy properly. Following the docs directly you end up not having the Node Feature Discovery Daemonset deployed and the GPU Operator errors with the following:
![Screen Shot 2020-05-29 at 11 19 25 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7716924/83319293-db3c0700-a202-11ea-9035-28615241020a.png)

This was also on an Openshift 4.3 cluster and it ended up deploying the 4.4 version of the Node Feature Discovery Daemonset
![Screen Shot 2020-05-29 at 11 19 01 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7716924/83319308-00307a00-a203-11ea-8339-f5edc8d0261f.png)


Even when I fill out the CRD appropriately the gpu operator sits in crashloop state (was able to piece it together from the helm chart repo). The operator errors since the Node Feature Discovery daemonset doesn't get deployed.

If you manually deploy the Node Feature Discovery Daemonset, you end up getting glibc mismatch issues because the containers are built for Ubuntu 18.04's GLIBC version and not RHCOS or RHEL's GLIBC version. (noted in the openshift-psap comment here: https://github.com/openshift-psap/special-resource-operator/issues/22#issue-610308684)


I was able to get further deploying the PSAP operator (documented my journey with it here: https://github.com/openshift-psap/special-resource-operator/issues/22). However, I was told by the Openshift team that that operator will not be supported and that NVIDIA owns building the functionality that that operator provides in this repo. 

I have tried to get support through multiple avenues (listed below):
https://developer.nvidia.com/nvidia_bug/2997565
https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/02665306
https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/issues/58
https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/issues/32

title: Use ISO 8601 format for datetime stamps in logs
body:
Not a bug but an improvement:
Please switch to logging with the standardized ISO 8601 date time stamp which is human and machine readable in opposite to the current painful unix timestamps used in the logs.

I understand that a central logging system would help but find it really hard to quickly check the logs and pinpoint the time when the issue happened, with lines as the following:
```
{"level":"info","ts":1591777763.3031344,"logger":"controller_clusterpolicy","msg":"ClusterPolicy","ResourceStatus":"NotReady"}
``` 
instead of something like:
```
{"level":"info","ts":2020-06-01T18:43:26.000Z,"logger":"controller_clusterpolicy","msg":"ClusterPolicy","ResourceStatus":"NotReady"}
```

There seems to be an easy way how this could be done in a kubernetes operator, see https://github.com/elastic/cloud-on-k8s/issues/1587

Thanks

title: Problems running the GPU operator on k3s
body:
Our product is IBM Edge Application Manager (IEAM). It manages containerized workloads on small devices, like the NVIDIA nano, and TX2. It also manages containerized workloads on Kubernetes clusters. We support OCP kubernetes clusters and k3s kubernetes clusters (among others) for IEAM. We would like to be able to support NVIDIA GPUs on all of our supported platforms. However, we are currently trying to run the NVIDIA GPU operator on k3s and we are running into problems.

Hardware: 96 core Xeon, 200GB RAM
OS/Distro: Linux 5.3, ubuntu 18.04.04
Docker 19.03.12
Fresh install of the latest k3s

We followed the instructions ([https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator#install-helm](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator#install-helm)) on the installation **but 3 of the pods do not come up**.  Note, as per the preqs, that we invoked the helm install as follows as I saw that nfd pods existed:
    `sudo helm install --devel --set nfd.enabled=false nvidia/gpu-operator --wait --generate-name`

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20863968/88228440-06037400-cc24-11ea-8cce-09d935898a3d.png)

For the pod logs of the two that have the CrashLoopBackOff error show:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20863968/88228507-1fa4bb80-cc24-11ea-8ea3-8d016c3b8ccd.png)

Attached are the pod descriptions for the three pods. 

This seems to be a similar issue to https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5089121.

Here is our platform configuration info:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20863968/88228673-5b3f8580-cc24-11ea-8ad5-77a6e548549d.png)

(Please see the 2 attached files).
[pods.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/files/4962629/pods.txt)
[log-nvidia-dcgm-exporter-48rqg.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/files/4962632/log-nvidia-dcgm-exporter-48rqg.txt)

We received some help on this from Anurag Guda and Anudeep Nallamothu but we remain blocked and they suggested I should raise a github issue for this.

title: NVIDIA driver installed by GPU operator fails on reboot
body:
We are trying to use the NVIDIA GPU operator to install NVIDIA driver/compiler/libs/runtime etc. on open-source kubernetes and we are running into a problem. This problem is very easy to reproduce.
 
Hardware: 96 core Xeon, 200GB RAM
OS/Distro: Linux  4.15.0, ubuntu 18.04.03
Docker 19.03.12

Steps to reproduce:
- Fresh install of the 18.04.03
- Used the GPU operator ansible playbook
- everything comes up beautifully (so nice! thanks for this great way to install)
- verified the driver/libs/runtime are working by running a container that uses the CUDA libraries to exercise the GPU

At that point all is good.

Then we rebooted.

After reboot the NVIDIA driver container goes into a crash/backoff loop. It seems to be trying to reinstall the driver, but since it is already there it is failing.

Anurag Guda helped us on this so he knows some more details.

title: GPU Operator crashes if no GPU nodes present
body:
### 1. Issue or feature description

GPU Operator crashes when GPU nodes are not present, as is the case when GPU nodes are temporarily scaled down to save operational costs. By extension, this means that a GPU node must be idling while the NVIDIA kernel module is built.

### 2. Steps to reproduce the issue

* Create machineset using GPU instance type
* Scale replica for said machineset to 1
* Install GPU operator, create ClusterPolicy (a truly ominous CRD name)
* Scale replica for machineset to 0
* `oc get po -n gpu-operator-resources`

### 3. More Information

https://gist.github.com/mmgaggle/27a847e0ed8a7a347dfd026471c67a9b

title: CentOS 7.8 Support - GLIBC_2.27

### 1. Issue or feature description

I'm trying to run on CentOS 7.8 with a single-node kubernetes cluster that I set up with kubeadm (no openshift).

I'm getting errors on the nvidia-driver-validation, nvidia-device-plugin-daemon-set, and nvidia-dcgm-exporter pods - each complaining that "GLIBC_2.27 not found". It seems like it is trying to use the host glibc which on centos 7 is GLIBC_2.17. 

From looking at the commits it seems that CentOS support is a recent development and perhaps there is some flag or configuration that I need to provide to run on CentOS 7 that hasn't been documented yet.

Any ideas? Thank you!

title: Remove close dependence on NFD
body:
GPU Operator uses the `feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-10de.present` label created by NFD to determine GPU nodes, which cannot be changed. To remove the dependency on NFD, I suggest extending the ClusterPolicy CR as follows:

```yaml
apiVersion: nvidia.com/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: cluster-policy
spec:
  nodeSelector:     # <-- Here
    matchLabels:
      feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-10de.present: "true"
  dcgmExporter:
    ...
```

The ability to customize GPU node decisions also makes it possible to set up different versions of components in different node groups.

---

I think it's good to use `feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-10de.present` label by default as it is now.

title: Label feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-10de.present=true is missing, but my node has T4 GPU
body:
I encountered this error:
https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/592c2d10a604e4262aaec42a4c6cb9efb4b90254/pkg/controller/clusterpolicy/object_controls.go#L168

But after checking my node labels, I actually had this label on my GPU node.

I started investigating the source code and I found this line:
https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/592c2d10a604e4262aaec42a4c6cb9efb4b90254/pkg/controller/clusterpolicy/object_controls.go#L155
I realized my node has to be labeled with `feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-10de.present=true` for the operator to work correctly,
So I manually labeled the node with `feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-10de.present=true` and the operator continued it's work to deploy the runtime, driver, plugin and validation containers as expected.

NFD automatically labeled my node with the following labels:
`feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-0300_1d0f.present=true,feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-0302_10de.present=true`
But as you can see, `feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-10de.present=true` is missing.

I am running Ubuntu 18.04 on AWS g4dn.xlarge node.

title: New GPU nodes do not get labeled with nvidia.com/gpu resources without restart of device-plugin pods
body:
_The template below is mostly useful for bug reports and support questions. Feel free to remove anything which doesn't apply to you and add more information where it makes sense._

### 1. Quick Debug Checklist
- [n] Are you running on an Ubuntu 18.04 node?
- [y] Are you running Kubernetes v1.13+?

- [?] Do you have `i2c_core` and `ipmi_msghandler` loaded on the nodes?

### 1. Issue or feature description
Issue: when adding a new node to a cluster with the GPU operator running, they never get labelled as nvidia.com/gpu nodes. An easy work around is to delete the device plugin daemonset pods, however this makes scaling up GPU nodes hard to automate (for instance using the cluster autoscaler). I believe this is because of a race condition between the driver container and the device plugin.

### 2. Steps to reproduce the issue
- Install the GPU operator
- Add a GPU node to the cluster

title: Support for OpenShift 4.5
body:
### 1. Issue or feature description

Per the Installation documentation[1] OpenShift 4.5 is not supported by the gpu-operator. What needs to happen to get OpenShift 4.5 supported?

[2] https://access.redhat.com/support/policy/updates/openshift

OpenShift 4.5.15

apiVersion: nvidia.com/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: cluster-policy
spec:
  dcgmExporter:
    image: dcgm-exporter
    repository: nvidia
    version: 1.7.2-2.0.0-rc.9-ubi8

    defaultRuntime: crio
  toolkit:
    image: container-toolkit
    repository: nvidia
    version: 1.0.2-ubi8
```

### 3. Information to [attach](https://help.github.com/articles/file-attachments-on-issues-and-pull-requests/) (optional if deemed irrelevant)

The problem can be worked around by adding the following env variables to the driver daemonset definition:

          env:
            - name: OPENSHIFT_VERSION
              value: '4.5'
            - name: RHEL_VERSION
              value: '8.2'
```

It appears the [driver image repo](https://ngc.nvidia.com/catalog/containers/nvidia:driver/tags) only has images tagged for REHL & Ubuntu. *Is it possible to use the REHL tagged images on Amazon Linux 2 as they both use the `yum` package manager?

title: state-device-plugin-validation schedules on wrong node in multi-node cluster
body:
### 1. Quick Debug Checklist
- [x] Are you running on an Ubuntu 18.04 node?
- [x] Are you running Kubernetes v1.13+?
- [x] Are you running Docker (>= 18.06) or CRIO (>= 1.13+)?
- [x] Do you have `i2c_core` and `ipmi_msghandler` loaded on the nodes?
- [x] Did you apply the CRD (`kubectl describe clusterpolicies --all-namespaces`)

### 1. Issue or feature description

We noticed state-device-plugin-validation pod could schedule on the wrong node in a multi-node cluster

### 2. Steps to reproduce the issue

1. spin up one gpu node A and wait for it to become ready
2. spin up another gpu node B
3. if node A is not being used, state-device-plugin-validation from node B could be scheduled on node A and then report gpu status for the wrong node
4. both node A, B are ready but B was never truly validated (both state-device-plugin-validation pods are shown completed on node A).

This normally doesn't cause any user-facing error since plugin-validation rarely notice failure.
However, this introduces a huge operation challenge for clusters equipped with autoscaler

autoscaling problem we saw:
1. the above process happens, state-device-plugin-validation pods are both on node A.
2. Some user gpu workload gets scheduled on node B, while node A remains unused.
3. Cluster autoscaler scale down node A due to inactivity. Both state-device-plugin-validation for A and B gets removed
5. gpu-operator notices node B's plugin-validation no longer exist and tries to recreate it, node B cannot fit plugin-validation pod because it's used by user workload
6. autoscaler gets in to infinite scale-up -> scale-down loop because from this point on node B will always have broken state until the user workload gets removed.
 


 could fix this by adding podAffinity to validation pods or make it a daemonset.

title: clusterpolicy_controller: watch Nodes' GPU labels to support scale-up
body:
This patch adds a custom Watch to the controller. The GPU operator
watches for Node events. When it happens, it checks if the GPU common
label is correctly applied and synchronized with the NFD labels.

When a mismatch is detected, the custom mapping function looks up all
the existing ClusterPolicy objects and requests a reconciliation.

Without this patch, when new nodes joined the cluster, they would
not load the Nvidia driver & toolkit until a GPU operator
reconciliation would be triggered (for instance by deleting an object
controlled by the operator).

Fixes #81

Signed-off-by: Kevin Pouget <kpouget@redhat.com>

title: Documentation: set operator.version in Helm charts
body:
Currently, [NVidia GPU-operator documentation](https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/kubernetes/openshift-on-gpu-install-guide/index.html#openshift-gpu-install-gpu-operator-via-helmv3) gives the following command to install the GPU operator on OpenShift:

```
$  helm install gpu-operator nvidia/gpu-operator --set platform.openshift=true,operator.validator.version=vectoradd-cuda10.2-ubi8,operator.defaultRuntime=crio,nfd.enabled=false,devicePlugin.version=v0.7.0-ubi8,dcgmExporter.version=2.0.13-2.1.0-ubi8,toolkit.version=1.3.0-ubi8 --wait
```

However, it can lead to deployment crashes when the command is used with the wrong GPU-operator version (ie, using an outdated command).

I would suggest setting the [GPU-operator version](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/2caaf94/deployments/gpu-operator/values.yaml#L15) (`--set operator.version=1.4.0`) in the command-line, so that it works regardless of the current operator release:

```
$  helm install gpu-operator nvidia/gpu-operator --set platform.openshift=true,operator.validator.version=vectoradd-cuda10.2-ubi8,operator.defaultRuntime=crio,nfd.enabled=false,devicePlugin.version=v0.7.0-ubi8,dcgmExporter.version=2.0.13-2.1.0-ubi8,toolkit.version=1.3.0-ubi8,operator.version=1.4.0 --wait
```

title: Wrong node pci labels when using NFD
body:
_The template below is mostly useful for bug reports and support questions. Feel free to remove anything which doesn't apply to you and add more information where it makes sense._

### 1. Quick Debug Checklist
- [x] Are you running Kubernetes v1.13+?
- [x] Are you running Docker (>= 18.06) or CRIO (>= 1.13+)?
- [x] Did you apply the CRD (`kubectl describe clusterpolicies --all-namespaces`)

### 1. Issue or feature description

Node labels added by the NFD have unexpected values for the pci.vendors labels

### 2. Steps to reproduce the issue

Deploy GPU operator 1.3 or higher using default helm chart values

### 3. nodes labels
                    ...
                    feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-0300_102b.present=true
                    feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-0302_10de.present=true
                    feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-0302_10de.sriov.capable=true
                    ...
### 4. Expected Labels
                    ...
                    feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-102b.present=true
                    feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-10de.present=true
                    feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-10de.sriov.capable=true
                    ...
### 5. cause
The node feature discovery values found at the [main chart](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/master/deployments/gpu-operator/values.yaml#L155-L159) use `worker.options` to configure the labels, but the node feature discovery [values](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/master/deployments/gpu-operator/charts/node-feature-discovery/values.yaml#L43-L128) uses a `config` field to do that, which causes the node feature discovery to use its default values to label the nodes.

title: New MIG slicing not visible outside of Pod
body:
While working on the MIG slicing for the GPU operator, I observed that if I launch a Pod and reconfigure the MIG slicing:

```
      nvidia-smi mig -dci 
      nvidia-smi mig -dgi
      nvidia-smi mig -cgi "$DRV_MIG_MODE" -cgi 1 -C
      nvidia-smi -L
```

the new slicing is correctly reported by `nvidia-smi -L` inside this Pod, but the other Pods do not see it.

A workaround to propagate the MIG slicing is to call `nvidia-smi -L` inside the `driver-daemonset` local Pod. This will have the side effect to propagate the MIG reconfiguration and make it visible to all the existing and new Pods.

title: nvidia-persistenced keeps a handle on the GPU and blocks --gpu-reset
body:
While working on the support of MIG slicing in the GPU-operator, I noticed that `--gpu-reset` doesn't work even when no Pod is consuming GPU resources.

After further investigations, it turned out that the `driver-daemonset` Pods spawns `nvidia-persistenced --persistence-mode` daemon, which keeps a handle on the GPU.

Killing this process and calling `nvidia-smi --gpu-reset` subsequently works correctly:

```
$ nvidia-smi -mig DISABLED
Warning: MIG mode is in pending disable state for GPU 00000000:C1:00.0:In use by another client
00000000:C1:00.0 is currently being used by one or more other processes (e.g. CUDA application or a monitoring application such as another instance of nvidia-smi). Please first kill all processes using the device and retry the command or reboot the system to make MIG mode effective.
All done.

$ nvidia-smi --gpu-reset
GPU 00000000:C1:00.0 is currently in use by another process.

1 device is currently being used by one or more other processes (e.g., Fabric Manager, CUDA application, graphics application such as an X server, or a monitoring application such as another instance of nvidia-smi). Please first kill all processes using this device and all compute applications running in the system.

$ killall nvidia-persistenced

$ nvidia-smi --gpu-reset
GPU 00000000:C1:00.0 was successfully reset.
```

title: Auto-updating nvidia_com_gfd_timestamp label issue with prometheus
body:
### 1. Issue or feature description

The *nvidia_com_gfd_timestamp*  node label seems to update every minute. This causes issues with our prometheus aggregations, as every time it changes, it creates an entirely new series (because node labels are appended to the series automatically), which contributes to the sum in our aggregations. 

If you happen to know to deal with this issue in promql (which I assume many k8s users will be using), please let me know.

Otherwise, I hope you can take this into account and possibly reconsider your use of dynamic values in node labels.

title: ClusterServiceVersion missing required 'displayName' field
body:
### 1. Issue or feature description

The ClusterServiceVersion definition located [here](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/c937c68a5f8469cdedea4c78fc8d681ad5d7c62c/bundle/manifests/gpu-operator.clusterserviceversion.yaml#L146) is missing the displayName field required under `spec.customresourcedefinitions[0].owned.displayName`.

Documentation on the required fields for the owned object can be found [here](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.4/operators/operator_sdk/osdk-generating-csvs.html#osdk-crds-owned_osdk-generating-csvs).

title: Operator breaks on hosts that already have drivers installed
body:
For context, we're hoping to use the operator with MicroK8s, in order to remove the need to package the nvidia-container-toolkit and template the containerd config file.

The issue we see is that, when the host already have the nvidia drivers installed, the `nvidia-driver-daemonset` pod fails to start.  The logs contain:

```
========== NVIDIA Software Installer ==========

Starting installation of NVIDIA driver version 450.80.02 for Linux kernel version 5.4.0-1034-aws

Stopping NVIDIA persistence daemon...
Unloading NVIDIA driver kernel modules...
Could not unload NVIDIA driver kernel modules, driver is in use
Stopping NVIDIA persistence daemon...
Unloading NVIDIA driver kernel modules...
Could not unload NVIDIA driver kernel modules, driver is in use

```

Would it be possible for the operator to check for the presence of existing drivers and use them instead of trying to re-install them?

title: Cannot deploy GPU operator on OpenShift following the documentation
body:
The documentation in [this page](https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/kubernetes/openshift-on-gpu-install-guide/index.html#openshift-gpu-install-gpu-operator-via-helmv3) for deploying the GPU Operator on OpenShift still mentions the broken `DevicePlugin ` image (`v0.7.0-ubi8`):
```
$  helm install gpu-operator nvidia/gpu-operator --set platform.openshift=true,operator.validator.version=vectoradd-cuda10.2-ubi8,operator.defaultRuntime=crio,nfd.enabled=false,devicePlugin.version=v0.7.0-ubi8,dcgmExporter.version=2.0.13-2.1.0-ubi8,toolkit.version=1.3.0-ubi8 --wait
```

as fixed images have been published (`v0.7.3-ubi8`), the documentation should be updated accordingly.

With the GPU operator v1.5.0, the `nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset` and `nvidia-dcgm-exporter` are stuck in `Init:0/1` state and GPUs are not available after a node restart.

After a manual restart of `nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset` with `kubectl delete` it starts successfully and the GPUs become available on the node.

The restart was working on the same nodes (Ubuntu 18.04) with the v1.4.0 version.

title: documentation: cannot deploy the operator on a MIG-enabled GPU

When the MIG mode of A100 GPU is enabled, the GPU operator cannot deploy successfully. 
I don't think this is properly documented.

```
# query the current MIG mode
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=mig.mode.current --format=csv,noheader
# disable the MIG mode
nvidia-smi -mig "0"
# reset the GPU if necessary
nvidia-smi --gpu-reset
```

See also https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/issues/129

title: crashLoopBack on finding kernel version
add the ability to define tolerations for validation pods
body:
gpu-enabled nodes may be defined with taints to prevent normal workload from landing on them. The gpu-operator addresses this use case by allowing to specify toleration for several of its components. But it is not possible to specify toleration for the validation pods.
These prevents these pods from being scheduled in the gpu-enabled nodes.

title: dcgm-exporter can be scheduled and run on a non-GPU node which will end with failure.
body:
### 1. Quick Debug Checklist
- [x] Are you running on an Ubuntu 18.04 node?
- [x] Are you running Docker (>= 18.06) or CRIO (>= 1.13+)?
- [ ] Are you running Kubernetes v1.13+? No, K3S version v1.20.2+k3s1
- [ ] Do you have `i2c_core` and `ipmi_msghandler` loaded on the nodes?
- [ ] Did you apply the CRD (`kubectl describe clusterpolicies --all-namespaces`)

### 1. Issue or feature description

All components that need to run on GPU nodes are labeled with `nodeSelector: nvidia.com/gpu.present: "true"` except `node-feature-discovery`,  `operator` and `dcgm-exporter`.  

https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/565ea353fec1a434a59a3e1eceae21dd3dd2cacb/deployments/gpu-operator/values.yaml#L122

so I moved `dcgm-exporter` to a non-GPU node and it failed to run with the following error messages. 

```
kubectl logs --namespace gpu-operator-resources nvidia-dcgm-exporter-l75sj -c toolkit-validation | head

Failed to allocate device vector A (error code CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version)!
[Vector addition of 50000 elements]
waiting for nvidia drivers to be loaded
Failed to allocate device vector A (error code CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version)!
[Vector addition of 50000 elements]
waiting for nvidia drivers to be loaded
Failed to allocate device vector A (error code CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version)!
[Vector addition of 50000 elements]
waiting for nvidia drivers to be loaded
Failed to allocate device vector A (error code CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version)!
```

The scheduler did run the `dcgmExporter` on a non-GPU node and there is no explicit declaration of `nodeSelector: nvidia.com/gpu.present: "true"`, therefore the scheduler can put `dcgmExporter` on any node and this can create a problem. 

### 2. Steps to reproduce the issue

Install the operator with the following `values.yaml`
**note**: master does not have GPU
 
```yaml
node-feature-discovery:
  master:
    nodeSelector:
      kubernetes.io/hostname: master

dcgmExporter:
  nodeSelector:
    kubernetes.io/hostname: master

operator:
  nodeSelector:
    kubernetes.io/hostname: master
```

body:
_The template below is mostly useful for bug reports and support questions. Feel free to remove anything which doesn't apply to you and add more information where it makes sense._

### 1. Quick Debug Checklist
- [NO ] Are you running on an Ubuntu 18.04 node? coreos 4.6
- [ YES] Are you running Kubernetes v1.13+?
- [ CRIO] Are you running Docker (>= 18.06) or CRIO (>= 1.13+)?
- [no ] Do you have `i2c_core` and `ipmi_msghandler` loaded on the nodes?
- [yes ] Did you apply the CRD (`kubectl describe clusterpolicies --all-namespaces`)

### 1. Issue or feature description
When installing GPU-operator, nvidia-driver-daemonsets fail because they can't reach external repos

### 2. Steps to reproduce the issue
Install GPU-operator from OpenShift web console

### 3. Information to [attach](https://help.github.com/articles/file-attachments-on-issues-and-pull-requests/) (optional if deemed irrelevant)

 - [ ] kubernetes pods status: `kubectl get pods --all-namespaces`
 - [ ] kubernetes daemonset status: `kubectl get ds --all-namespaces`
 - [ ] If a pod/ds is in an error state or pending state `kubectl describe pod -n NAMESPACE POD_NAME`
 - [ ] If a pod/ds is in an error state or pending state `kubectl logs -n NAMESPACE POD_NAME`

 - [ ] Output of running a container on the GPU machine: `docker run -it alpine echo foo`
 - [ ] Docker configuration file: `cat /etc/docker/daemon.json`
 - [ ] Docker runtime configuration: `docker info | grep runtime`

 - [ ] NVIDIA shared directory: `ls -la /run/nvidia`
 - [ ] NVIDIA packages directory: `ls -la /usr/local/nvidia/toolkit`
 - [ ] NVIDIA driver directory: `ls -la /run/nvidia/driver`
 - [ ] kubelet logs `journalctl -u kubelet > kubelet.logs`
 
### 4. Fixing the problem:

CoreOS is running on the worker nodes and as such does not have entitlement keys in /etc/pki/entitlement or the /etc/rhsm/rhsm.conf file that is required to access the repositories where kernel-devel source is located in the event that the Nvidia drivers need to be rebuilt against a newer kernel. I do not think there is an automated update of the machineconfigs on the worker nodes with the entitlement keys during operator install - maybe there is but it is not working.

Until the machineconfigs with new entitlement keys are applied to the worker nodes, the nvidia-driver-daemonsets can not successfully transition to RUN state.

title: GPU Monitoring not working on OpenShift OperatorHub
body:
When deploying the GPU Operator from OpenShift OperatorHub, the Prometheus DCGM monitoring is not working.

This can be confirmed by checking that there is no `dcgm` target in Prometheus:
```
https://prometheus-k8s-openshift-monitoring.apps.$CLUSTER_ADDR/targets
```

or programmatically, by checking prometheus configuration file:

```
oc get secret prometheus-k8s -n openshift-monitoring -ojson | jq -r '.data["prometheus.yaml.gz"]' | base64 -d | gunzip | grep dcgm
# (empty)
```
---

The issue comes from the labeling of the `namespace/gpu-operator-resources`, which is missing the label `openshift.io/cluster-monitoring=true`, so this should be included in the deployment documentation.

```
oc label ns/gpu-operator-resources openshift.io/cluster-monitoring=true
```

This command ^^^ solves the issue, after a few minutes Prometheus notices the DCGM `ServiceMonitor` and starts exposing the GPU metrics.

    repository: nvcr.io/nvidia

    version: 450.80.02
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    tolerations:
    - effect: NoSchedule
      key: nvidia.com/gpu
      operator: Exists
    nodeSelector:
      nvidia.com/gpu.present: "true"
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
      seLinuxOptions:
        level: s0
  toolkit:
    repository: nvcr.io/nvidia/k8s
    image: container-toolkit
    version: 1.4.4-ubuntu18.04
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    tolerations:
    - key: CriticalAddonsOnly
      operator: Exists
    - effect: NoSchedule
      key: nvidia.com/gpu
      operator: Exists
    nodeSelector:
      nvidia.com/gpu.present: "true"
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
      seLinuxOptions:
        level: s0
  devicePlugin:
    repository: nvcr.io/nvidia
    image: k8s-device-plugin
    version: v0.8.1
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    nodeSelector:
      nvidia.com/gpu.present: "true"
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
    args:
    - --mig-strategy=single
    - --pass-device-specs=false
    - --fail-on-init-error=true
    - --device-list-strategy=envvar
    - --nvidia-driver-root=/run/nvidia/driver
  dcgmExporter:
    repository: nvcr.io/nvidia/k8s
    image: dcgm-exporter
    version: 2.0.13-2.1.2-ubuntu20.04
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    args:
    - -f
    - /etc/dcgm-exporter/dcp-metrics-included.csv
  gfd:
    repository: nvcr.io/nvidia
    image: gpu-feature-discovery
    version: v0.4.0
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    nodeSelector:
      nvidia.com/gpu.present: "true"
    migStrategy: single
    discoveryIntervalSeconds: 60
```

Now specifically looking at:
```
    repository: nvcr.io/nvidia
    image: gpu-feature-discovery
    version: v0.4.0
```

While this definitely follows a common pattern seen in most Helm charts, at a pure Kubernetes level this format of separating repository, image, and version makes it very hard to inject a sha256 hashed image.  When trying to use resolution and relocation tooling like [kbld](https://carvel.dev/kbld/) you'll actually get errors as using `image` is triggering its auto-discovery in unintended ways:

```
kbld: Error: 
- Resolving image 'driver': GET https://index.docker.io/v2/library/driver/manifests/latest: UNAUTHORIZED: authentication required; [map[Action:pull Class: Name:library/driver Type:repository]]
- Resolving image 'cuda-sample': GET https://index.docker.io/v2/library/cuda-sample/manifests/latest: UNAUTHORIZED: authentication required; [map[Action:pull Class: Name:library/cuda-sample Type:repository]]
- Resolving image 'container-toolkit': GET https://index.docker.io/v2/library/container-toolkit/manifests/latest: UNAUTHORIZED: authentication required; [map[Action:pull Class: Name:library/container-toolkit Type:repository]]
- Resolving image 'dcgm-exporter': GET https://index.docker.io/v2/library/dcgm-exporter/manifests/latest: UNAUTHORIZED: authentication required; [map[Action:pull Class: Name:library/dcgm-exporter Type:repository]]
- Resolving image 'gpu-feature-discovery': GET https://index.docker.io/v2/library/gpu-feature-discovery/manifests/latest: UNAUTHORIZED: authentication required; [map[Action:pull Class: Name:library/gpu-feature-discovery Type:repository]]
- Resolving image 'k8s-device-plugin': GET https://index.docker.io/v2/library/k8s-device-plugin/manifests/latest: UNAUTHORIZED: authentication required; [map[Action:pull Class: Name:library/k8s-device-plugin Type:repository]]
```

Is there an optional way to provide the full image name rather than dissecting it into 3 parts?

So instead of:
```
  devicePlugin:
    repository: nvcr.io/nvidia
    image: k8s-device-plugin
    version: v0.8.1
```
You could have:
```
  devicePlugin:
    fullImage: nvcr.io/nvidia/k8s-device-plugin:v0.8.1
```
which could then be properly handled for resolution and relocation?

Also, how do you override the `nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda@sha256:ed723a1339cddd75eb9f2be2f3476edf497a1b189c10c9bf9eb8da4a16a51a59` reference in the init containers?

title: Documentation: helm install command from docs.nvidia.com is broken
body:
This [documentation](https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/kubernetes/openshift-on-gpu-install-guide/index.html) page still indicates this command to install the GPU Operator on OpenShift from Helm:

```
$  helm install gpu-operator nvidia/gpu-operator --set platform.openshift=true,operator.validator.version=vectoradd-cuda10.2-ubi8,operator.defaultRuntime=crio,nfd.enabled=false,devicePlugin.version=v0.7.3-ubi8,dcgmExporter.version=2.0.13-2.1.2-ubi8,toolkit.version=1.4.0-ubi8 --wait
```

but this configuration is invalid, the `DevicePlugin` crashes with this error:
```
flag provided but not defined: -nvidia-driver-root
Usage of nvidia-device-plugin:
  -device-list-strategy string
    	the desired strategy for passing the device list to the underlying runtime
    	[envvar | volume-mounts] (default "envvar")
  -fail-on-init-error
    	fail the plugin if an error is encountered during initialization, otherwise block indefinitely [default: true]
    	 (default true)
  -mig-strategy string
    	the desired strategy for exposing MIG devices on GPUs that support it
    	[none | single | mixed] (default "none")
  -pass-device-specs
    	pass the list of DeviceSpecs to the kubelet on Allocate()
```
---
This is due to fact that the helm deployment doesn't specify the version of the Operator, so the latest version is used:
```
Pod: gpu-operator-86db95c4b5-f8629
nvcr.io/nvidia/gpu-operator:1.6.1
```

Remember this issue https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/issues/113 ?
`--set operator.version=1.4.0` should really be mentioned along with the `helm install` command

title: Docs: CRI-O runtime hook location
body:
The most recent release of the GPU Operator (v1.6.2) changed the location of the CRI-O runtime hook to `/run/containers/oci/hooks.d`.
After doing a fresh install of the GPU Operator on a vanilla k8s cluster, running the most recent CRI-O v1.20.1 with the default configuration, I had the `nvidia-device-plugin` pods stuck in a crash loop. It took me some time to figure out, that I had to edit the default CRI-O settings at `/etc/crio/crio.conf` to include the new (non standard?) location of the runtime hook in order to get it working.

```diff
 hooks_dir = [
        "/usr/share/containers/oci/hooks.d",
+        "/run/containers/oci/hooks.d",
 ]
```

This step wasn't necessary before v1.6.2 and I couldn't find any explanation regarding this in the docs. Shouldn't this be mentioned in the installation manual? Maybe somewhere [around here](https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/cloud-native/gpu-operator/getting-started.html#install-the-gpu-operator)?

Or is there something wrong with my setup and this should work out of the box?

title: Support for Nvidia Drivers Version 460.32.03+ on RHEL 7.9
body:
### 1. Issue or feature description
Seem to be running into issues when trying to install Nvidia Drivers 460.32.03+ on RHEL 7.9. The only possible GPU node type on ROKS (IBM Cloud hosted Redhat Openshift) is a bare metal node, with RHEL 7 installed. 

When trying to install Nvidia GPU Operator version `1.6.2` the `nvidia-driver-daemonset` pod, the image that is trying to be pulled is `460.32.03-rhel7.9` which does not exist. Seems the operator itself will append the "os" to the image automatically.

Is there support for  460.32.03+ Driver Version on RHEL 7.9? The current work around is to use 1.5.2 of the GPU Operator, which pulls `450.80.02-rhel7.9` which does exist. 

Please see the images tags available [here](https://ngc.nvidia.com/catalog/containers/nvidia:driver/tags)

### 2. Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Obtain RHEL 7.9 node with GPU hardware 
2. Try install Nvidia Operator through Operator Hub or Helm 
3. Here is helm install command from documentation
```
helm install gpu-operator nvidia/gpu-operator --version=1.6.2 --set platform.openshift=true,operator.validator.version=vectoradd-cuda10.2-ubi8,operator.defaultRuntime=crio,nfd.enabled=false,devicePlugin.version=v0.8.2-ubi8,dcgmExporter.version=2.1.4-2.2.0-ubi8,toolkit.version=1.4.7-ubi8 --wait
```
4. This will try pull `460.32.03-rhel7.9` for the `nvidia-driver-daemonset` deployment

Thank you in advance!

After deploying the gpu-operator Helm chart on a cluster with pod security policies enabled, adding a GPU instance to the cluster results in the following events:

```bash
$ kubectl get events -n gpu-operator-resources                                                                                                                                                         
LAST SEEN   TYPE      REASON         OBJECT                              MESSAGE
81s         Warning   FailedCreate   daemonset/nvidia-driver-daemonset   Error creating: pods "nvidia-driver-daemonset-" is forbidden: PodSecurityPolicy: unable to admit pod: [spec.securityContext.hostPID: Invalid value: true: Host PID is not allowed to be used spec.volumes[0]: Invalid value: "hostPath": hostPath volumes are not allowed to be used spec.volumes[1]: Invalid value: "hostPath": hostPath volumes are not allowed to be used spec.volumes[2]: Invalid value: "hostPath": hostPath volumes are not allowed to be used spec.containers[0].securityContext.privileged: Invalid value: true: Privileged containers are not allowed]
```

Adding a `PodSecurityPolicy` with these permissions and associated `Role` and `RoleBinding` for the `nvidia-driver` service account fixes the issue.

title: Uninstall persists `containerd-template.toml` changes
body:
### Issue or feature description
After uninstalling the helm chart, my `containerd-template.toml` remained altered. Specifically the `default_runtime_name` was yet `nvidia`. In my particular case this caused Emby pods to fail to start with the following:
```
Error: failed to create containerd task: OCI runtime create failed: container_linux.go:370: starting container process caused: process_linux.go:459: container init caused: Running hook #0:: error running hook: exit status 1, stdout: , stderr: nvidia-container-cli.real: initialization error: driver error: failed to process request: unknown
Back-off restarting failed container
```

Manually resetting the `containerd-template.toml` resolved the issue, though this is something that I would expect to be managed by a standard uninstall process or documented in the [uninstall section](https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/cloud-native/gpu-operator/getting-started.html#uninstalling-gpu-operator).

title: Airgap Install Help
body:
Hello,

Sorry I did not use your issue template because I have some questions with the installation. My situation is a little unique. I’m training AI on an isolated LAN running k3s 1.17. Because we’re using an offline network, we completely air gapped the entire k3s rancher install — not even using helm. We have an NVIDIA DGX running Ubuntu 18.04 with CUDA 11.2 and nvidia-container-toolkit (instead of nvidia-docker2). Our other nodes are basically in charge of running our environment, and those are running rhel 7.8, CUDA 10.2, and container-toolkit as well.

We’re not having an issues getting the containers to access the GPU, but the functionality we’re trying to achieve is adding the GPU limit. If an AI workload is scheduled on GPU-0 of the DGX, we want other workloads that are scheduled to go to a different GPU instead of GPU-0 that’s occupied.

I tried creating a Daemonset of just the k8s-device-plugin, but it was looking for our “manifests” directory, which I think is created by kubelet or kubeadm (?), which we don’t have.

I’ve been following the instructions on your site [here](https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/cloud-native/gpu-operator/getting-started.html).

My questions are: can I just create a Daemonset of all of the containers that gpu-operator requires?

If so, since the DGX is running a different OS, driver version, and cuda version, would I need two Daemonsets or can i just disregard the version verification containers?

Will I need to remove nvidia-container-toolkit and replace with nvidia-docker2?

We have multiple AI agents training on 300+ containers, so ruining our k3s cluster would be a huge burden. Let me know what you guys think! Thanks in advance. We could really use the help

title: nvidia-driver-daemonset cannot pull image on Ubuntu 21.04
body:
_The template below is mostly useful for bug reports and support questions. Feel free to remove anything which doesn't apply to you and add more information where it makes sense._

### 1. Quick Debug Checklist
- [ ] Are you running on an Ubuntu 18.04 node?
- [x] Are you running Kubernetes v1.13+?
- [ ] Are you running Docker (>= 18.06) or CRIO (>= 1.13+)?
- [ ] Do you have `i2c_core` and `ipmi_msghandler` loaded on the nodes?
- [ ] Did you apply the CRD (`kubectl describe clusterpolicies --all-namespaces`)

I'm running:
1. Ubuntu 21.04
2. Microk8s 1.21/stable
3. Kubernetes 1.21

I currently have 460.80 version of the driver installed on the host machine if it makes any difference.
The GPU in use is GeForce RTX 2080 Ti.

### 1. Issue or feature description
I need to enable the gpu-operator inside the microk8s deployment
```
microk8s enable gpu
```

It creates the `nvidia-driver-daemonset` daemonset in the `gpu-operator-resources` namespace. Pods of this daemonset cannot pull the image:

```
olokshyn@neptune-linux:~$ mk -n gpu-operator-resources get events --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp

This image does not exist on [NGC](https://ngc.nvidia.com/catalog/containers/nvidia:driver/tags). I guess the tag that it should be using is `460.32.03-ubuntu20.04`.

This daemonset deployment is controlled by the helm chart. 

**How can I change the image tag?**

The helm chart doesn't seem to explicitly specify it anywhere (maybe that's my lack of experience with helm).


### 2. Steps to reproduce the issue
On Ubuntu 21.04 with a NVidia GPU:

```
sudo snap install microk8s --channel 1.21/stable --classic
sudo usermod -a -G microk8s olokshyn
sudo chown -f -R olokshyn ~/.kube
# reboot
microk8s enable dns dashboard storage
microk8s enable gpu
```

title: The CustomResourceDefinition "clusterpolicies.nvidia.com" is invalid: metadata.annotations: Too long: must have at most 262144 bytes
body:
I get the following error when applying the custom resource definition for clusterpolicy objects:

```bash
$ kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/master/deployments/gpu-operator/crds/nvidia.com_clusterpolicies_crd.yaml
The CustomResourceDefinition "clusterpolicies.nvidia.com" is invalid: metadata.annotations: Too long: must have at most 262144 bytes                                                                                                                                    
```

After researching some, it seems like this is due to the annotations placed on the CRD resource when using `kubectl apply` (see https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kubebuilder/issues/1140#issuecomment-561729237). I verified that using `kubectl create` works, however I'm concerned that updating the CRD with `kubectl replace` going forward may cause issues with deployed cluster policy objects by deleting and recreating the CRD.

title: Changing provided DCGM-exporter metrics
body:
Hello Team,

For our GPU monitoring solution we would like to expose some additional metrics provided by the DCGM API. For this purpose, I changed the file /etc/dcgm-exporter/dcp-metrics-included.csv to also include those metrics by creating a config map and adding my custom file to the dcgm-exporter daemonset. This work as expected but my problem is the dcgm-exporter daemonset and the dcgm-exporter configmap (which includes my custom dcp-metrics-included.csv file) are managed by the GPU operator which means if it includes a reconciliation loop in the future my changes will be gone.

Do you have any concerns about the way I am changing this file or will there be no reconciliation loop / updates of the managed resources after creation? If this is a problem do you have any recommended way to change the included metrics or any plans to make this configurable via the cluster policy?

title: containerd config.toml
body: when setting default runtime to containerd, the nvidia-toolkit from container-toolkit overrides containerd/config.toml and restarts the daemon. Is there an option for the toolkit to not alter config.toml. Use case is that the containerd has already been configured and includes a number of other changes and we cannot restart it.

title: Validation Pod failing to do its job when the driver failed to be removed
body:
Hello,

we noticed that if for any reason, the kernel driver cannot be removed when the GPU Operator is uninstalled,
the validation Pod will lift the `driver` barrier right away (`nvidia-smi` works), allowing the other operands to run.

Because of these operands keeping the driver busy, the driver-container will not be able to remove the old driver, and thus will fail forever to load the new one.

---

here is what the validation pod reports (1.6.2 driver):
```
$ oc logs nvidia-operator-validator-z94hz --all-containers
all validations are successful
running command chroot with args [/run/nvidia/driver nvidia-smi]
Thu Jun 17 19:15:50 2021
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 460.32.03    Driver Version: 460.32.03    CUDA Version: 11.2     |
|-------------------------------+----------------------+----------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| Fan  Temp  Perf  Pwr:Usage/Cap|         Memory-Usage | GPU-Util  Compute M. |
|                               |                      |               MIG M. |
|===============================+======================+======================|
|   0  Tesla T4            Off  | 00000000:00:1E.0 Off |                    0 |
| N/A   34C    P0    26W /  70W |      0MiB / 15109MiB |      0%      Default |
|                               |                      |                  N/A |
+-------------------------------+----------------------+----------------------+

```
and the driver contains fails on this:
```
Starting installation of NVIDIA driver version 460.73.01 for Linux kernel version 4.18.0-240.22.1.el8_3.x86_64
...
+ nvidia_refs=47
+ rmmod_args+=("nvidia")
+ '[' 47 -gt 2 ']'
+ echo 'Could not unload NVIDIA driver kernel modules, driver is in use'
Could not unload NVIDIA driver kernel modules, driver is in use
+ return 1
+ exit 1
```

---

I guess the validation pod should ensure that the right version of the driver is loaded before lifting its barrier.

title: compat32 libs do not work
body:
as of driver nvcr.io/nvidia/driver:460.73.01-ubuntu20.04, compat32 option does not work as libs are all taken from ld.so.cache from the container. However, the container does not instruct linker to search also /usr/lib32, no 32bit libs are cached and thus not mounted to containers.

this is easy fix to add search for 32bit to the driver container:
echo "/usr/lib32" > /etc/ld.so.conf.d/i386-linux-gnu.conf

one more thing remains. nvidia-installer does not provide libGL.so.1 for 32bit libs, so container-cli should link libGL.so.1 to libGLX_nvidia.so.

title: Upgrade/reboot issue related to the container-toolkit
body:
Hello,

in a recent cluster upgrade (4.7 -> 4.8) CI test, using the GPU Operator `master` branch ([commit](https://gcsweb-ci.apps.ci.l2s4.p1.openshiftapps.com/gcs/origin-ci-test/logs/periodic-ci-openshift-psap-ci-artifacts-release-4.7-upgrade-gpu-operator-e2e-upgrade/1420353446782963712/artifacts/gpu-operator-e2e-upgrade/0-preupgrade-gpu-operator-test-master-branch/artifacts/009__gpu_operator__bundle_from_commit/operator-image-builder-pod.log) 8188766aac0b280b90332248430d540d79653a62), we [observed](https://gcsweb-ci.apps.ci.l2s4.p1.openshiftapps.com/gcs/origin-ci-test/logs/periodic-ci-openshift-psap-ci-artifacts-release-4.7-upgrade-gpu-operator-e2e-upgrade/1420353446782963712/artifacts/gpu-operator-e2e-upgrade/2-postupgrade-gpu-operator-validate-deployment/artifacts/001__gpu-operator__must-gather/004__gpu_operator__capture_deployment_state/gpu_operator_pods.list) a failure with the Pods unable to start:
```
NAME                                       READY   STATUS                      RESTARTS   AGE    IP            NODE                          NOMINATED NODE   READINESS GATES
gpu-feature-discovery-9xbmz                0/1     CreateContainerError        0          43m    10.130.2.13   ip-10-0-164-90.ec2.internal   <none>           <none>
nvidia-container-toolkit-daemonset-x6rkr   1/1     Running                     0          43m    10.130.2.2    ip-10-0-164-90.ec2.internal   <none>           <none>

From the `events`, we [see](https://gcsweb-ci.apps.ci.l2s4.p1.openshiftapps.com/gcs/origin-ci-test/logs/periodic-ci-openshift-psap-ci-artifacts-release-4.7-upgrade-gpu-operator-e2e-upgrade/1420353446782963712/artifacts/gpu-operator-e2e-upgrade/gather-extra/artifacts/events.json) that they are failing because of the container toolkit:

"message": "Error: container create failed: time=\"2021-07-28T14:17:45Z\" level=error msg=\"container_linux.go:367: starting container process caused: process_linux.go:495: container init caused: Running hook #0:: error running hook: exit status 1, stdout: , stderr: nvidia-container-cli.real: initialization error: driver error: failed to process request\\n\"\n",

title: WITH_REBOOT variable - not clear how to set it
body:
This is a documentation issue, but a quick reply here could help a lot.

Reading this page...

https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/cloud-native/gpu-operator/gpu-operator-mig.html

...I've found this quote:

> In a CSP IaaS environment such as Google Cloud, ensure that the mig-manager variable WITH_REBOOT is set to “true”. Refer to the note in the MIG User Guide for more information on the constraints with enabling MIG mode.

There is no mention anywhere else in the document about that variable. The linked page makes no mention of it either. A google search has not revealed anything mentioning that variable.

So, how to set that variable? Is it enough to declare it as an environment variable before running `helm install gpu-operator`?

Thanks!

title: Report images not found when deploy GPU Operator on openshift 4.9 using helm
body:
_The template below is mostly useful for bug reports and support questions. Feel free to remove anything which doesn't apply to you and add more information where it makes sense._

### 1. Quick Debug Checklist
- [ ] Are you running on an Ubuntu 18.04 node?
- [ ] Are you running Kubernetes v1.13+?
- [ ] Are you running Docker (>= 18.06) or CRIO (>= 1.13+)?
- [ ] Do you have `i2c_core` and `ipmi_msghandler` loaded on the nodes?
- [ ] Did you apply the CRD (`kubectl describe clusterpolicies --all-namespaces`)

### 1. Issue or feature description
Deploy GPU Operator on openshift4.9(Not official released), the gpu driver images version will automatically add a tag rhcos4.9 for driver images, for example, 
nvcr.io/nvidia/driver:470.57.02-rhcos4.9, only nvcr.io/nvidia/driver:470.57.02-rhcos4.9470.57.02-rhcos4.8 exist 
nvidia-driver-daemonset-72jqc will report the error
Warning  Failed          19s               kubelet            Error: ImagePullBackOff
  Normal   Pulling         6s (x2 over 21s)  kubelet            Pulling image "nvcr.io/nvidia/driver:470.57.02-rhcos4.9"
  Warning  Failed          4s (x2 over 20s)  kubelet            Failed to pull image "nvcr.io/nvidia/driver:470.57.02-rhcos4.9": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = Error reading manifest 470.57.02-rhcos4.9 in nvcr.io/nvidia/driver: manifest unknown: manifest unknown
  Warning  Failed          4s (x2 over 20s)  kubelet            Error: ErrImagePull

### 2. Steps to reproduce the issue
1. Setup Openshift 4.9 cluster
2. #Support version, v1.7.1, v1.8.0
export HELM_VERSION=v1.8.0
export JUMP_HOST=ec2-18-118-164-13.us-east-2.compute.amazonaws.com
cp values-${HELM_VERSION}.yaml values.yaml
oc create ns gpu-operator-resources
helm fetch https://helm.ngc.nvidia.com/nvidia/charts/gpu-operator-${HELM_VERSION}.tgz
helm install  gpu-operator gpu-operator-${HELM_VERSION}.tgz -f values.yaml -n gpu-operator-resources

Suggested:
Don't use the current rhcos version as images tag, the tag can be the same with gpu operator version, for example, v1.8.0, so we can deploy gpu operator to an un-released openshift cluster.

title: Pods do not wait for nvidia-driver to be ready
body:
Hey there,

we are running the GPU-Operator on AWS EKS and since we also deploy spot instances, GPU nodes will come and go frequently. The issue is that the pods that run ML models on the GPUs won't wait for the nvidia driver to be ready. As soon as the node is up, they will spawn on it, but by that time the nvidia-driver pod hasn't finished, so the ML applications will instead run on the CPU, which is quite problematic. 

Currently, we solve this by having an initContainer with a sleep timer. I was wondering if there is a better solution to this, as the other pods like validator or dcgm-exporter also wait for the driver. They seem to mount /run/nvidia and a secret, so I'm not sure if this is a valid option for my own pods. Perhaps it could be done with readiness probes but I don't see any in the nvidia pods. 

Has anyone else experienced this issue and if yes, do you have any solution for this? Thanks!

title: Multiple issues with dcgm and dcgm-exporter in latest release (v1.8.2)
body:
### Platform
Platform EKS 1.21 + AMI [AMI v20210722](https://github.com/awslabs/amazon-eks-ami/releases/tag/v20210722)

###  Issue or feature description
Multiple issues with latest release v1.8.2

#### Problem 1
Breaking change introduced in 1.8.0. Upgrading from 1.7.1 is not possible due to changed selector label - which is immutable. Release notes for 1.8.0+ did not mention any breaking changes.

#### Problem 2
Pod security policy `gpu-operator-privileged` is missing extra permissions required by `nvidia-dcgm`. `nvidia-dcgm` tried to start a container with a `hostPort` configured on 5555. However, the psp does not allow that. To fix, we need to add to the privileged psp:

```
  hostPorts:
    - max: 5555
      min: 5555
```

However, the problems do not end here. Once the psp is updated, the daemonset starts up okay (although no logs are available - this part could be intended) but the `nvidia-dcgm-exported` pods are now failing as they cannot connect to the `nvidia-dcgm` pods on each node respectively. Upon further investigation, it turns out that while you would expect the `nvidia-dcgm` container with `hostPort` configured to be reachable on 5555, after looking at the networking (netstat on each node there is nothing listening on port 5555. To check:

```sh
sudo netstat -tulpn | grep LISTEN | grep 5555
```

A fix to this is to, again, alter the psp `gpu-operator-privileged` to add `hostNetwork: true` and also alter the `nvidia-dcgm` daemonset to add `hostNetwork: true` to the `spec`. Correct me if i am wrong, but the daemonset should not need to have `hostNetwork: true` in order to bind to a specific host port using the `hostPort` setting.

title: Cuda driver crash to cause kernel panic
GPU-operator doesn't allow to specify a volume to mount metrics file for nvidia-dcgm-exporter
body:
Hi,

A comment on `nvidia-dcgm-exporter` recommands to define by ourself the list of metrics to export: https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-monitoring-tools/issues/143#issuecomment-926807911
For example, to enable `DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL` or others metrics in https://github.com/NVIDIA/dcgm-exporter/blob/main/etc/dcp-metrics-included.csv.
It is possible to specify the location of the exporter collections with an environment var
https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/e0299a01333e43e9c234cddbe4058f7e42cc9568/deployments/gpu-operator/values.yaml#L190-L191
But there is currently no way to specify a ConfigMap or a Volume to mount into `nvidia-dcgm-exporter` daemonset in CRDs of gpu-operator:
https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/master/deployments/gpu-operator/crds/nvidia.com_clusterpolicies_crd.yaml#L402-L718

Do you have any plans to update CRDs to add this ?

### 1. Issue or feature description
I want to prevent containers from using GPU resources by default.

This issue seems to be describing my problem (specifically regarding specifying 0 GPUs, not omitting the request). And there is a comment suggesting to change the container toolkit settings. apiVersion: v1

title: Cannot mount another volume to nvidia-driver-ctr container
body:
In order to run the GPU operator on ppc64le I need to mount `/sys` to the `nvidia-driver-ctr` container, due to some GPU memory onlining details in combination with NVLink 2.0 protocol specific to Power9 systems equipped with V100 GPUs. Basically the file `/sys/fs/cgroup/cpusets/cpusets.mems` needs to get updated. (Here is a more detailed explanation of the issue: https://www.ibm.com/support/pages/cudasuccess-3-vs-0-initialization-error)

With the GPU Opeartor v1.7.0 everything works fine when I change `assets/state-driver/0500_daemonset.yaml` and add volume as well as volumeMounts, but for v1.9.0 somehow the `/sys` directory does not get mounted although I'm basically doing the same (check this commit [here](https://github.com/mgiessing/gpu-operator/commit/b59c8d62be8df12e8c1c4a9e2f7ca816019dc929#diff-90506e1fdf119d48ce82244f18e88ec9b0df9569a0dc7a2d49aeab5090f8a9e4))

Here an `oc describe pods nvidia-driver-daemonset-xxxx` for v1.7.0:

```
