title: Gather GPUCluster and DRA resources in must-gather.sh
body:
The [must-gather ](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/bde9e1def35b284758ebc1ca9d2b9b9c89f166e3/hack/must-gather.sh) script is a diagnostic tool used to help triage / debug an issue faced with a GPU Operator installation. The tool gathers environment information, configuration, and logs into a compressed archive (e.g. `.tar.gz`). 

The must-gather script does not currently gather any information regarding the new GPUCluster CRD. This CRD was introduced in the GPU Operator 26.7.0 release and is used by the operator to deploy and manage the NVIDIA DRA Driver for GPUs. 

The must-gather script should collect the following information:
- The GPUCluster CR spec and status
- Relevant DRA objects in the cluster. E.g. DeviceClasses and ResourceSlices associated with the NVIDIA DRA Driver for GPUs

title: Populate observedGeneration field in CR conditions
body:
Conditions added to a custom resource's status should contain the `observedGeneration` field. `observedGeneration` represents the `.metadata.generation` of the custom resource that the condition was set based upon. If the `observedGeneration` of a condition is less than the current `.metadata.generation` of the custom resource, then this indicates that the condition is stale.

Currently, this field is not added to any condition for any of the custom resources that the GPU Operator manages. All of the condition writers below omit this field:
- [ClusterPolicy](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/bde9e1def35b284758ebc1ca9d2b9b9c89f166e3/internal/conditions/clusterpolicy.go#L60-L99)
- [NVIDIADriver](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/bde9e1def35b284758ebc1ca9d2b9b9c89f166e3/internal/conditions/nvidiadriver.go#L66-L113)
- [GPUCluster](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/bde9e1def35b284758ebc1ca9d2b9b9c89f166e3/internal/conditions/gpucluster.go#L59-L105)

Adding this field is a shared improvement across all three CRDs.

title: Report which GPUCluster operands are blocking readiness
body: During the GPUCluster controller's reconciliation, if any of the operands (software components) that it deploys are not in a ready state, the GPUCluster CR will be marked `NotReady` and the controller will [add a condition](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/bde9e1def35b284758ebc1ca9d2b9b9c89f166e3/controllers/gpucluster_controller.go#L142-L143) indicating that the operands are not ready yet. This condition has a generic `Waiting for operand pods to be ready` message. This message should also add the list of operands that are not ready. We already have precedent for this with the ClusterPolicy controller which emits a similar condition [here](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/bde9e1def35b284758ebc1ca9d2b9b9c89f166e3/controllers/clusterpolicy_controller.go#L231-L236).

title: Reject conflicting healthcheck ports in the DRA kubelet-plugin daemonset
body: When ComputeDomains are enabled in the GPUCluster CR (`draDriver.computeDomains.enabled=true`), the kubelet-plugin daemonset will have two main containers (one for GPUs and one for ComputeDomains). Both containers run a gRPC healthcheck service that is checked by a liveness probe (see [here](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/20fb2db3ee43b85cb59cbb51c44e8a129bee1829/manifests/state-dra-driver/0500_daemonset.yaml#L199-L214) and [here](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/20fb2db3ee43b85cb59cbb51c44e8a129bee1829/manifests/state-dra-driver/0500_daemonset.yaml#L313-L328)). The GPUCluster controller should validate that different ports are configured for the two healthcheck services, and return an error if there is a collision.

title: Indicate number of nodes that an NVIDIADriver CR matches
body:
NVIDIADriver CR status should show how many nodes it's nodeSelector matches. For example, the below CR matches zero nodes, but one would not know that by looking at it's status.

```
apiVersion: nvidia.com/v1alpha1
kind: NVIDIADriver
metadata:
  name: driver-r595
spec:
  default: false
  driverType: gpu
  image: driver
  kernelModuleType: auto
  nodeSelector:
    nvidia.com/test: "false"
  repository: nvcr.io/nvidia
  version: 595.91.07
status:
  conditions:
  - lastTransitionTime: "2026-09-29T13:52:01Z"
    message: All resources have been successfully reconciled
    reason: Reconciled
    status: "True"
    type: Ready
  - lastTransitionTime: "2026-09-29T13:52:01Z"
    message: ""
    reason: Ready
    status: "False"
    type: Error
  state: ready
```

A new status field, like below, can be added to the NVIDIADriver CRD:
```
// +kubebuilder:printcolumn:name="Nodes",type=integer,JSONPath=`.status.matchedNodeCount`
// MatchedNodeCount is the number of eligible GPU nodes currently assigned
// to this NVIDIADriver.
MatchedNodeCount int32 `json:"matchedNodeCount"`
```

An example output from `kubectl get nvidiadriver` would be:
```
NAME          STATUS   DEFAULT   NODES   AGE
h100-driver   ready    false     0       2m
default       ready    true      5       1h
```

title: Make NVIDIADriver node-pool rendering deterministic
body: [getNodePools](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/20fb2db3ee43b85cb59cbb51c44e8a129bee1829/internal/state/nodepool.go#L147-L153) builds its return slice by iterating a Go map, so DaemonSet render order varies between reconciles. Sort pools by name before returning and add a multi-pool unit test that asserts stable ordering. This makes logs, manifests, and reconciler behavior easier to reason about.

title: feat: support metricRelabelings on the ServiceMonitor
body:
## Description

`ServiceMonitorConfig` only exposed `relabelings`, which maps to Prometheus **target** relabeling (`Endpoint.RelabelConfigs`) and runs before the scrape. Rewriting labels on **scraped samples** — e.g. collapsing `exported_namespace`/`exported_pod` back onto `namespace`/`pod`, the use case in #2938 — requires `Endpoint.MetricRelabelConfigs`, which had no API surface. Since the Helm chart passes `dcgmExporter.serviceMonitor` through to the ClusterPolicy verbatim, a `metricRelabelings` key was rejected by CRD schema validation.

This adds `MetricRelabelings` to `ServiceMonitorConfig` and applies it on both rendering paths:

- the ClusterPolicy controller (`applyServiceMonitorCustomEdits`)
- the DRA dcgm-exporter manifest template (`manifests/state-dcgm-exporter/0600_service_monitor.yaml`)

Because `DCGMExporterServiceMonitorConfig` is an alias of `ServiceMonitorConfig`, the field is also available to the operator-metrics ServiceMonitor.

The duplicated pointer-slice deref loop is factored into a shared `derefRelabelConfigs` helper so the two branches cannot drift.

Example:

```yaml
dcgmExporter:
  serviceMonitor:
    metricRelabelings:
      - action: replace
        regex: (.+)
        sourceLabels: [exported_namespace]
        targetLabel: namespace
```

> Supersedes #2939, which was closed. This revision additionally adds the rendered-manifest test coverage that review asked for on that PR, updates `config/samples/nvidia_v1alpha1_gpucluster.yaml` for consistency, and deduplicates the relabel-config conversion.

title: Report which GPUCluster operands are blocking readiness
body:
Fixes #2978

When nothing errors out but some operands just aren't ready yet, the GPUCluster `OperandNotReady` condition only said "Waiting for operand pods to be ready", so you had to go poke at pods to figure out what it was actually waiting on. This lists the not-ready states in the message, same format ClusterPolicy already uses (`clusterPolicyNotReadyMessage`). States that return `ignore` (e.g. DCGM when it's disabled) are left out.

### Changes
- New `gpuClusterOperandNotReadyMessage()` helper in `controllers/gpucluster_controller.go`, used when setting the `OperandNotReady` condition
- Unit tests: a table test for the helper, plus a reconcile test that checks the condition reason and message end to end with the fake state manager / condition updater

### Testing
`go test ./controllers/` passes, and `golangci-lint` is clean.

Also tried it on a couple of real clusters with a locally built operator image.

**k3s (Rancher Desktop, no GPU, node labeled so the DaemonSets schedule):** DCGM is disabled, so it's correctly left out of the list:

    Error  True  OperandNotReady  Waiting for operand pods to be ready; states not ready: [state-dra-driver state-dcgm-exporter state-dra-validation]

**RKE2 v1.36, single node with a T400:** I switched from ClusterPolicy to GPUCluster and watched the condition as things came up:

    18:08:28  notReady | Error/PrerequisiteNotMet: A ClusterPolicy CR "cluster-policy" exists; a ClusterPolicy CR and GPUCluster CR may not exist at the same time
    18:09:02  notReady | Error/OperandNotReady: Waiting for operand pods to be ready; states not ready: [state-dra-driver state-dcgm-exporter state-dra-validation]
    18:11:10  notReady | Error/OperandNotReady: Waiting for operand pods to be ready; states not ready: [state-dcgm-exporter]

The driver, the DRA plugin and the validator all came up and dropped off the list. dcgm-exporter stayed stuck, and the message pointed right at it. Its logs show it trying to list `v1beta1.ResourceSlice`, which that API server doesn't serve:

    "Failed to watch" err="failed to list *v1beta1.ResourceSlice: the server could not find the requested resource"

That's unrelated to this PR (happy to open a separate issue), but it's a nice example of why the extra detail helps.

title: Verify the triggering commit before running other CI jobs
body:
PRs can pass DCO while containing unsigned or unverified commits. DCO sign-off does not verify commit signatures.
Add a reusable workflow, .github/workflows/commit-verification.yaml, with:
```
on:
  workflow_call: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
```
The workflow should check GitHub’s signature-verification metadata for the triggering commit (github.sha) and fail if it is not verified. Report the commit SHA and verification reason, and fail if verification metadata cannot be retrieved.
Call it from [.github/workflows/ci.yaml](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yaml):
```
jobs:
  commit-verification:
    permissions:
      contents: read
    uses: ./.github/workflows/commit-verification.yaml
```
Make all other CI jobs depend on commit-verification through needs, preserving existing dependencies, so verification runs first and subsequent jobs run only after it succeeds.

title: ci: add commit verification workflow and update job dependencies
body:
## Description

Fixes #2990

PRs can pass DCO while containing unsigned or unverified commits — DCO sign-off does not verify commit signatures — so unverified code can run the whole pipeline (builds, image pushes, e2e) before anyone notices. This checks GitHub's signature-verification metadata for the triggering commit (`github.sha`) first and blocks everything else until it passes.

## Changes

- New `.github/workflows/commit-verification.yaml` reusable workflow (`workflow_call`, `contents: read`) — fails if the commit isn't `verified`, reports the SHA and verification `reason`, and fails if the metadata can't be retrieved
- Updated `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` — new `commit-verification` job runs first, added to `needs` of all other jobs (existing dependencies preserved)

## Tests

No Go code touched, so no unit tests — verified the workflow logic read-only with `gh` 2.101.0 against the live API, running the exact `gh api` command from the step.

**Unsigned commit** (local HEAD `36100733`) fails as expected:

    {"verified":false,"reason":"unsigned","signature":null,...}
    Commit SHA: 36100733af792370de3b62b10611df2c02c9fad3
    Verified: false
    Reason: unsigned
    ::error::Commit 36100733... is not verified (reason: unsigned).

**Verified commit** (origin `main`, GitHub PGP signature) passes:

    Verified: true
    Reason: valid
    ::notice::Commit main signature verified (reason: valid).

**Unretrievable metadata** (nonexistent SHA) fails closed:

    gh: No commit found for SHA: 0000... (HTTP 422)
    ::error::Could not retrieve verification metadata for commit 0000....

title: Ensure automated backport commits have verified signatures
body:
The cherry-pick workflow currently creates backport commits locally and pushes them without signing. Recent automated backports report verified: false with reason unsigned, even when the original commits were signed.

This is incompatible with CI signature verification proposed in #2992 and branch protection requiring signed commits.

Update .github/scripts/backport.js to produce verified backport commits. Follow the approach implemented in [nvidia-container-toolkit PR #2012](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/pull/2012):
- Recreate each cherry-picked commit through GitHub’s Git Data API, preserving its tree, message, and commit order.
- Update the backport branch to reference the resulting signed commit chain.
- Preserve existing PR creation and conflict-handling behavior.
This approach avoids managing a separate GPG or SSH signing key for the bot.

Acceptance criteria:
- GitHub reports verified: true for every generated backport commit.
- Backports preserve the expected changes and commit messages.
- Backport CI passes the signature-verification gate when enabled.
- Both clean backports and backports requiring manual conflict resolution remain supported.

title: Ensure automated backport commits have verified signatures

## Description

The cherry-pick workflow creates backport commits with a local `git push`, so they are unsigned (`verified: false`). That conflicts with signature verification (#2992) and branch protection that requires signed commits.

After pushing the backport branch, recreate each new commit through the GitHub Git Data API (preserving tree, message, and order), then force-update the backport branch to the signed chain. Same approach as NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit#2012. PR creation and conflict handling are unchanged; no bot GPG/SSH key is required.

title: [Bug]: Reconcile driver ownership when node labels match a different NVIDIADriver
body:
In GPU Operator v26.7.1, changes to node labels used by an NVIDIADriver selector can fail to trigger ownership reassignment when the node is currently owned by the default driver or has no driver owner.

The node-update predicate checks selector-label changes only against the node’s current owner. It therefore misses changes that make the node eligible for another driver.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Create a non-default NVIDIADriver with:
```
  spec:
     default: false
     nodeSelector:
       network.nvidia.com/operator.mofed.wait: "false"
```
2. Start with a GPU node whose label is "true". The node is owned by the default driver, if present, or has no owner.
3. Change the node label to "false".
4. Observe that nvidia.com/gpu-operator.driver.owner does not change to the matching non-default driver.

**Expected behavior**

Changes to any label referenced by a live NVIDIADriver selector should trigger ownership reconciliation, regardless of the node’s current owner.
- "true" → "false" assigns the matching non-default driver.
- "false" → "true" assigns the default fallback, if present, or removes ownership.
- Adding or removing selector labels also triggers reconciliation.

**Proposed fix**

Update the node-update predicate to check selector-label changes across all live NVIDIADriver resources, rather than only the current owner. Add regression coverage for default-owned, unowned, and custom-owned nodes, including label additions and removals.

title: fix scc permissions on openshift for MPS
body: ## Description With `MPSSupport=true` on OpenShift, workloads using an MPS-configured ResourceClaim remain in `ContainerCreating` because SCC admission rejects the dynamically created MPS control daemon. The daemon defaults to the namespace’s `default` service account, which cannot use the `nvidia-dra-driver` SCC. That SCC also disallows `hostPID`, which the daemon requires. This change: - Passes the kubelet plugin’s service account through `SERVICE_ACCOUNT_NAME` using the Downward API, so generated MPS daemons use the existing SCC-authorized account. - Enables `allowHostPID` in the DRA driver SCC. - Adds regression coverage for service-account wiring and SCC permissions, and updates rendered fixtures. ## Checklist - [x] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes - [x] Lint checks passing (`make lint`) - [x] Generated assets in-sync (`make validate-generated-assets`) - [x] Go mod artifacts in-sync (`make validate-modules`) - [x] Test cases are added for new code paths ## Testing Manually validated on OpenShift 4.22 with GPU Operator v26.7.1 using equivalent live configuration changes. ### Setup Enabled MPS in the GPUCluster: ```yaml spec: draDriver: featureGates: MPSSupport: true ``` Confirmed the DRA kubelet plugin rolled out with `MPSSupport=true` in `FEATURE_GATES` and logged `plugin_registered:true`. ### Reproduction manifests Created the test namespace: ```bash oc create namespace mps-repro ``` Applied this ResourceClaimTemplate: ```yaml apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1 kind: ResourceClaimTemplate metadata: name: shared-gpu namespace: mps-repro spec: spec: devices: requests: - name: mps-gpu exactly: deviceClassName: gpu.nvidia.com count: 1 config: - requests: - mps-gpu opaque: driver: gpu.nvidia.com parameters: apiVersion: resource.nvidia.com/v1beta1 kind: GpuConfig sharing: strategy: MPS mpsConfig: defaultActiveThreadPercentage: 50 ``` Applied this Pod, with both containers referencing the same claim and GPU request: ```yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: mps-repro namespace: mps-repro spec: restartPolicy: Never securityContext: runAsNonRoot: true seccompProfile: type: RuntimeDefault containers: - name: client-a image: nvcr.io/nvidia/k8s/cuda-sample:nbody-cuda11.6.0-ubuntu18.04 command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"] securityContext: allowPrivilegeEscalation: false capabilities: drop: ["ALL"] resources: claims: - name: shared-gpu request: mps-gpu - name: client-b image: nvcr.io/nvidia/k8s/cuda-sample:nbody-cuda11.6.0-ubuntu18.04 command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"] securityContext: allowPrivilegeEscalation: false capabilities: drop: ["ALL"] resources: claims: - name: shared-gpu request: mps-gpu resourceClaims: - name: shared-gpu resourceClaimTemplateName: shared-gpu tolerations: - key: nvidia.com/gpu operator: Exists effect: NoSchedule ``` ```bash oc apply -f mps-claim-template.yaml oc apply -f mps-pod.yaml ``` Released GPUs held by earlier test workloads so the new claim could allocate. ### Failure before the fix The workload remained `0/2 ContainerCreating`. Its events reported: ```text FailedPrepareDynamicResources: MPS control daemon is not yet ready: waiting for MPS control daemon to come online ``` The MPS daemon Deployment had no explicit `serviceAccountName`, so it used `default`. Its ReplicaSet reported SCC admission failures for privileged containers, hostPath volumes, and host PID access. ### Validate equivalent configuration changes Patched the generated MPS daemon Deployment to use the existing SCC-authorized service account: ```bash MPS_DEPLOYMENT=mps-control-daemon-1f71609f-63d6-4107-ad6c-4481cfb02ad6-40c05 oc patch deployment "$MPS_DEPLOYMENT" \ -n nvidia-gpu-operator --type=merge \ -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"serviceAccountName":"nvidia-dra-driver-kubeletplugin"}}}}' ``` Confirmed admission still failed specifically because `nvidia-dra-driver` disallowed `hostPID`. Enabled host PID access and immediately restarted the daemon Deployment, since Operator reconciliation reverted the manual SCC change: ```bash oc patch scc nvidia-dra-driver --type=merge \ -p '{"allowHostPID":true}' && oc rollout restart deployment "$MPS_DEPLOYMENT" \ -n nvidia-gpu-operator ``` ### Results - MPS control daemon reached `1/1 Running`. - The existing workload retried claim preparation automatically and reached `2/2 Running`. - No workload recreation was needed. This validates SCC admission and MPS claim preparation using equivalent manual changes. It does not validate a deployment of the PR build or CUDA execution through MPS; the workload containers ran `sleep`. ---

title: Fix ComputeDomain daemon permissions on OpenShift
body:
## Description:
When testing MNNVL on OpenShift 4.22.1 with NVL72 nodes and GPU Operator v26.7.1, ComputeDomain daemon Pods encounter two permission failures:
1. Incorrect SCC selection: Pods are admitted under restricted-v2 and crash because they cannot write /imexd/imexd.cfg. Although the daemon’s service account is listed in the nvidia-dra-driver SCC, that SCC has no priority, allowing OpenShift to prefer restricted-v2.
2. Missing RBAC permission: The daemon’s ClusterRole lacks delete on computedomaincliques.resource.nvidia.com. Owner-reference admission rejects its requests with:
```
   cannot set an ownerRef on a resource you can't delete
```

## Expected behavior: 
ComputeDomain daemon Pods should start successfully and manage clique owner references.

## Proposed fix:
Give the custom DRA SCC a positive priority and add the missing clique permission to both the daemon’s ClusterRole and the Operator’s Helm/OLM RBAC.

title: fix(bundle): pin vgpu-device-manager to the multi-arch index digest
body:
Fixes #3012

## Problem

`bundle/manifests/gpu-operator-certified.clusterserviceversion.yaml` pins `vgpu-device-manager:v0.5.1` to `sha256:0b20d3f4…`. That's the `linux/amd64` manifest, not the image index, so ARM GPU nodes pull the amd64 image and fail with `Exec format error`.

## Fix

Both references (the `vgpu-device-manager-image` relatedImages entry and the `VGPU_DEVICE_MANAGER_IMAGE` env var) now point at the v0.5.1 OCI image index:

```
$ curl -sI -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json" \
    https://nvcr.io/v2/nvidia/cloud-native/vgpu-device-manager/manifests/v0.5.1
content-type: application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json
docker-content-digest: sha256:a846793e78fac0d88156ee08f9835b9e29d99b0b316a165ea4a3acf0e27ad0fd
```

That index lists:
- `linux/amd64` → `sha256:0b20d3f41754048531d732d0180d2f1648feffedb6cf6f2cfa19fff8f9c35150` (the old pin)
- `linux/arm64` → `sha256:a981408d69578f6916810f7c92b65a8f38563ecaf4b91d87cc7a775fd48220d2`

## Other images

I compared every other tagged `nvcr.io` digest in the CSV against the tag's index digest the same way. They all match already (dcgm, cc-manager, driver-manager, mig-manager, sandbox-device-plugin, dra-driver, device-plugin, container-toolkit, dcgm-exporter, kubevirt-gpu-device-plugin). The OS-specific driver/gdrdrv refs are untagged, so I left them out of the check.

title: [Bug]: Driver upgrade does not evict pods that use nvidia.com/gpu only in a native sidecar
body:
**Describe the bug**
During an automatic driver upgrade, the upgrade controller does not delete workload pods whose nvidia.com/gpu resource is declared only in a native sidecar container (an entry in spec.initContainers with restartPolicy: Always).
The GPU pod filter, gpuPodSpecFilter in cmd/gpu-operator/main.go, only iterates pod.Spec.Containers, so such pods are treated as non-GPU pods ("No pods require deletion" logged). They  keep the GPU open, k8s-driver-manager cannot unload the driver, the driver pod goes into Init:CrashLoopBackOff and the node ends up in upgrade-failed.

**To Reproduce**
1. Run a Deployment whose main container has no GPU request, and a native sidecar with one:
```
  initContainers:
  - name: gpu-sidecar
    restartPolicy: Always
    resources:
      limits: 
        nvidia.com/gpu: 1
```
2. Change driver.version in the ClusterPolicy.
3. Observe the operator log and the driver pod.

**Expected behavior**
Pods that declare nvidia.com/gpu* in resources of any container, including native sidecars, are selected by gpuPodSpecFilter and deleted in pod-deletion-required.

**Environment (please provide the following information):**
 - GPU Operator Version: v26.7.1
 - OS: Ubuntu24.04

title: [Bug]: RHOCP CRI-O SELinux: GSP firmware read denial in workload context leads to RmInitAdapter failure
body:
On OpenShift with SELinux enforcing, a GPU whose first initialization happens after the driver container has finished installing cannot be initialized for compute. The kernel fails to load `gsp_tu10x.bin` with error `-13` (EACCES). The cause is an SELinux denial: the workload process (`container_t`) is not allowed to read the firmware file, which is labeled `container_var_run_t`.

The rest of the driver rootfs under `/run/nvidia/driver` is labeled `container_file_t`, which workloads can read. Only the firmware directory has a different label.

The GSP firmware is read at first GPU initialization, by whichever process first accesses the device. This matters because there are two paths:
- **Privileged initialization path:** a GPU that is already present when the driver container installs is initialized by `nvidia-installer` and `nvidia-persistenced`, both running as `spc_t`. The firmware label does not matter to them.
- **Workload initialization path:** a GPU whose first initialization happens after the driver installation is first accessed by the workload. The workload is `container_t` and is denied.

In our environment, the second GPU becomes available to the node only after the driver container has started. That is how we get a GPU on the workload initialization path.

Visible symptoms: the GPU shows up in `nvidia-smi` in the driver pod with 0 MiB used and no processes. Node Feature Discovery and GFD still see and label it. The workload does not crash on its own.

**To Reproduce**

1. OpenShift 4.22.9 worker, SELinux enforcing, GPU Operator v26.3.3. One GPU (GPU A) is present when the driver container installs.
2. Start a workload that uses GPU A. It works. First GPU initialization of GPU A was done by the privileged initialization path.
3. After the driver installation has completed, a second GPU (GPU B) becomes available to the node. How this happens is specific to our environment.
4. Start a second workload that requests GPU B. The first device access to GPU B comes from the workload.
5. The workload starts, but GPU B is not usable. The kernel log shows the firmware load failing, and the audit log shows the AVC denial for `python` in `container_t`.

We have not tried a case without a late-appearing GPU (see "Not confirmed yet").

**Expected behavior**

A GPU whose first initialization happens after driver installation can be initialized and used by a normal workload, with no extra SELinux policy. For example, the firmware files carry a label that `container_t` can read, or a privileged component performs the first GPU initialization.

**Environment**

- GPU Operator Version: v26.3.3
- NVIDIA DRA driver for GPUs: v0.4.1
- NVIDIA driver: 580.126.20 (open kernel module), GPU: NVIDIA A30
- OS: RHCOS (OpenShift 4.22.9)
- Kernel Version: 5.14.0-687.35.1.el9_8.x86_64
- Container Runtime Version: CRI-O 1.35.5
- Kubernetes Distro and Version: OpenShift (RHOCP) 4.22.9

**Evidence**

The SELinux workaround module was removed before the run.

*1. The workload is denied on the firmware file*

```
type=SYSCALL msg=audit(...): syscall=257 success=no exit=-5
  comm="python" exe="/usr/bin/python3.12"
  subj=system_u:system_r:container_t:s0:c7,c28
type=AVC msg=audit(...): avc: denied { read }
  comm="python" name="gsp_tu10x.bin" dev="tmpfs" ino=14990
  scontext=system_u:system_r:container_t:s0:c7,c28
  tcontext=system_u:object_r:container_var_run_t:s0 tclass=file permissive=0
```

The same denial repeats a few milliseconds later. GPU A, initialized on the privileged path, produced zero AVC denials in the same run. The device node itself is readable: `/dev/nvidia1` carries `container_file_t:s0:c7,c28`.

*2. Kernel log, same second as the denial*

```
kernel: nvidia 0000:96:00.0: loading /run/nvidia/driver/lib/firmware/nvidia/580.126.20/gsp_tu10x.bin failed with error -13
kernel: nvidia 0000:96:00.0: Direct firmware load for nvidia/580.126.20/gsp_tu10x.bin failed with error -2
kernel: NVRM: RmFetchGspRmImages: No firmware image found
kernel: NVRM: GPU 0000:96:00.0: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x61:0x56:1914)
kernel: NVRM: GPU 0000:96:00.0: rm_init_adapter failed, device minor number 1
```

`-13` is EACCES. `-2` is the fallback path (ENOENT). There is no equivalent failure for GPU A (`0000:95:00.0`). GPU B is `0000:96:00.0`.

*3. The privileged path succeeds on the same files*

Captured with `auditctl -w` on the firmware directory (logs allowed and denied accesses):

```
11:53:26  comm="nvidia-installe"  subj=system_u:system_r:spc_t:s0  success=yes  (creates gsp_tu10x.bin, gsp_ga10x.bin)
11:53:31  comm="nvidia-persiste"  subj=system_u:system_r:spc_t:s0  success=yes  (opens gsp_tu10x.bin)
```

The same pair, in the same order, was seen in two separate runs.

*4. The failure is not specific to one device*

In an earlier test (2026-09-15), the first device worked (22379 MiB used, active python process, no denial). Later in that test, a workload's first access to the same device after the driver installation failed with the same denial, on the same file and label:

```
Tue Sep 15 10:26:18 2026  avc: denied { read } for pid=341212 comm="python" name="gsp_tu10x.bin" ... tcontext=...container_var_run_t:s0
Tue Sep 15 10:50:14 2026  avc: denied { read } for pid=380168 comm="python" name="gsp_tu10x.bin" ... tcontext=...container_var_run_t:s0
```

So the variable is which path performs the first GPU initialization, not which physical device or slot it is.

*5. Label mismatch inside the same mount*

```
$ ls -Z /run/nvidia/driver/lib/firmware/nvidia/580.126.20/
system_u:object_r:container_var_run_t:s0 gsp_ga10x.bin
system_u:object_r:container_var_run_t:s0 gsp_tu10x.bin

$ ls -Z /run/nvidia/driver/lib64/ | head
system_u:object_r:container_file_t:s0 LLVMgold.so
system_u:object_r:container_file_t:s0 Mcrt1.o
...
```

`container_t` can read `container_file_t` under the base policy. It cannot read `container_var_run_t`. Same result in all three runs. The mount is on tmpfs and does not exist before the driver container installs.

*6. Driver modules load once per node*

The `nvidia`, `nvidia-modeset` and `nvidia-nvlink` modules load once, during the driver installation. No module load happens when GPU B is first initialized six minutes later. So the GSP firmware read is per device, at first GPU initialization.

**Other platforms we tested**

Same test on each: one GPU present at driver installation, workload on it, then a second GPU whose first initialization happens after driver installation. FACT = seen in the logs we collected. HYP = our assumption. UNKNOWN = the capture failed or was not taken.

| Area | Ubuntu + containerd | RHEL + containerd | RKE2 (SLES 16) | OpenShift (CRI-O) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GPU initialized after driver installation is usable | FACT: yes (79 GB used) | FACT: yes | FACT: yes | FACT: no, `RmInitAdapter failed` |
| GPU model / driver | A100 80GB / 580.126.20 | A100 80GB / 580.126.20 | A100 80GB / 595.71.05 | A30 / 580.126.20 |
| SELinux | UNKNOWN: not captured | FACT: enforcing | FACT: enabled (driver log). Mode not captured | FACT: enforcing |
| Runtime SELinux support | UNKNOWN | FACT: containerd `enableSelinux: true` | UNKNOWN | FACT: enabled |
| Denial on `gsp_*.bin` | UNKNOWN: no audit data | UNKNOWN: audit watch failed, pipeline audit files empty. A short host AVC sample has no firmware denial | FACT: `ausearch` returned no matches. UNKNOWN whether it covered the first initialization | FACT: repeated, reproducible |
| Kernel `-13` / `RmInitAdapter` | UNKNOWN: no kernel log | FACT: none in the host journal we have. It does not cover the test window | FACT: none in the kernel log | FACT: present, same second as the denial |
| Label of the firmware directory | UNKNOWN | UNKNOWN: `ls -Z` returned "Permission denied" | UNKNOWN: script used a hardcoded 580.126.20 path, node has 595.71.05 | FACT: `container_var_run_t` |
| Privileged `nvidia-smi` before the workload | Not done | Not done | Skipped (`NODE` not set) | Not done |
| First firmware read on the second GPU | UNKNOWN | UNKNOWN | UNKNOWN | FACT: the workload (`python`, `container_t`) |

What we take from this, and what we do not:
- The GPU initialized after driver installation works on the three other platforms. We do not know why. It could be a different firmware label, or a different process doing the first firmware read.
- The driver container script calls `chcon -R -t container_file_t /run/nvidia/driver/dev` when SELinux is enabled (seen in the RKE2 log, and the same step is printed in the RHEL log). It does not relabel the firmware directory. We have not checked whether the OpenShift driver container uses the same script.
- The driver message `knvlinkCoreShutdownDeviceLinks_IMPL ... for GPU1` also appears on RKE2 and RHEL runs where everything works. We think it is unrelated.

**Confirmed vs. not confirmed**

Confirmed by logs on this OpenShift setup:
- The firmware file is labeled `container_var_run_t`, the workload is denied, and the kernel firmware load fails with `-13` at the same second.
- `spc_t` components (installer, persistenced) read the same file without problems.
- The behavior reproduced in three runs.
- With a local SELinux module that allows `container_t` to read `container_var_run_t`, the same steps show zero denials.

Not confirmed yet:
- Whether the same denial happens for a GPU that is present at driver installation but whose first initialization comes from a workload (for example, with `nvidia-persistenced` stopped). This would give a reproduction without a late-appearing GPU. Not tested.
- The firmware label and the first firmware read on other platforms (see the table).
- Whether `nvidia-persistenced` initializes devices that become available after its start.
- Which component creates `/run/nvidia/driver/lib/firmware` and sets its label inside the driver container.

**Workaround (works, not a fix)**

A custom policy module allowing `container_t` to read `container_var_run_t` files. In a run where it was left installed by mistake, the same steps produced no denials. Illustrative form (our local module may differ in detail):

```
allow container_t container_var_run_t:file { read open getattr };
```

This widens access for all `container_t` workloads, which is why we would like a proper fix.

**Possible fixes**

1. **Label**: make the firmware directory use `container_file_t`, like the rest of `/run/nvidia/driver`. The driver script already relabels `/run/nvidia/driver/dev` with `chcon`, so extending that step to `/run/nvidia/driver/lib/firmware` may be a small change. Not tested.
2. **Initialization**: make sure a privileged component performs the first GPU initialization for GPUs whose first initialization happens after the driver installation, so the first firmware read never comes from an unprivileged workload.

**Information to attach**

- [x] kubernetes pods status: `kubectl get pods -n gpu-operator` (attached)
- [x] kubernetes daemonset status: `kubectl get ds -n gpu-operator` (attached)
- [ ] pod/ds in error state: not applicable, all pods are Running. The failure is inside the workload's GPU initialization.
- [x] `nvidia-smi` from the driver container: `kubectl exec DRIVER_POD_NAME -n gpu-operator -c nvidia-driver-ctr -- nvidia-smi` (attached, shows GPU B with 0 MiB and no processes)
- [ ] containerd logs: not applicable, the runtime is CRI-O. CRI-O logs from the node can be added if needed.
- [x] Audit log from the `auditctl -w` watch (key `gsp_access_watch`)
- [x] Full kernel log for the run (`journalctl -k`)
- [x] `ls -Z` output of the firmware directory and `lib64`

[rhocp-nvidia-issue.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33234350/rhocp-nvidia-issue.zip)

title: Fix GPU pod detection for native sidecars during driver upgrades
body:
## Description

Addresses #3026. During a driver upgrade, `gpuPodSpecFilter` checks GPU resources in `pod.Spec.Containers` but misses native sidecars in `pod.Spec.InitContainers` (`restartPolicy: Always`). A pod whose main container has no GPU request and whose native sidecar requests a GPU can therefore be skipped by pod deletion.

Check GPU and MIG limits and requests for native sidecars using the existing resource predicate. The ordinary container check, phase gate, DRA fallback, and handling of regular init containers remain unchanged.

Known limitation: A Pending pod with a currently running regular (non-sidecar) GPU init container is still not selected. This is an existing behavior outside this change. Scanning all init containers unconditionally would also select Running pods whose GPU init has already completed; a status-aware fix needs separate decisions for missing or stale status and retries. Please advise whether that case should be tracked separately.

## Checklist

- [x] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes
- [ ] Lint checks passing (`make lint`) — not run locally; `golangci-lint` is unavailable in this environment
- [ ] Generated assets in-sync (`make validate-generated-assets`) — not run; no generated assets changed
- [ ] Go mod artifacts in-sync (`make validate-modules`) — not run; no module or vendor files changed
- [x] Test cases are added for new code paths

## Testing

- Before the fix, three native sidecar cases failed: GPU limit, GPU request, and MIG request. Their non-GPU and regular-init controls passed.
- After the fix, `GOTOOLCHAIN=local GOFLAGS=-mod=vendor go test -count=1 ./cmd/gpu-operator ./controllers` passed: 20 operator subtests and 387 controller subtests (407 total). Run with Go 1.26.3 on Darwin arm64 using vendored dependencies.
- Focused `-race` filter tests passed (20 subtests) on the same production logic before the final comment-only edit. The final two-file diff passes `gofmt` and `git diff --check`.
- No GPU hardware or Kubernetes cluster upgrade test was run. Driver unload and end-to-end upgrade recovery remain unverified.

title: (fix): Reject conflicting DRA kubelet-plugin healthcheck ports when ComputeDomains are enabled
body:
## Description

Fixes #2979

With `draDriver.computeDomains.enabled: true` the kubelet-plugin DaemonSet runs
two containers, `gpus` and `compute-domains`, each binding a gRPC health service
in the shared pod network namespace. Configured on the same port, the second
bind fails with `EADDRINUSE` and that container crash-loops; which one loses is
a startup race, so the symptom is hard to trace back to the GPUCluster spec.

The DRA driver state now validates the two healthcheck ports before rendering.
The check runs on the resolved ports, so setting only one field to the other
container's default (51516 / 51515) is caught too, and a disabled health
service never collides. A collision is reported through the existing
`getManifestObjects` error path: the GPUCluster gets a `ReconcileFailed`
condition naming both fields and the port, and the DaemonSet is left untouched.

Validation of the containers' metrics endpoints (`HTTP_ENDPOINT`), raised
during review, is deferred to a follow-up PR.

## Checklist

- [x] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes
- [x] Lint checks passing (`make lint`)
- [x] Generated assets in-sync (`make validate-generated-assets`)
- [x] Go mod artifacts in-sync (`make validate-modules`)
- [x] Test cases are added for new code paths

## Testing

Unit tests: `TestDRADriverHealthcheckPortCollision` covers equal explicit
ports, either port set to the other container's default, distinct ports, the
shipped defaults, computeDomains disabled, and one or both health services
disabled. The error cases fail against the pre-fix validator.

Manual testing on a kind cluster with mock NVML (nvml-mock via the run-ai
fake-gpu-operator), so both kubelet-plugin containers start and reach their
health bind:

- Release operator v26.7.1 with `computeDomains.kubeletPlugin.healthcheck.port: 51516`:
  both containers render on 51516 and `compute-domains` crash-loops with
  `failed to listen on :51516: listen tcp :51516: bind: address already in use`.
- Operator built from this PR: distinct ports 52000 / 52001 render with the
  probes on them, both containers ready with no restarts across two liveness
  periods, GPUCluster `ready`; the colliding spec is rejected with
  `ReconcileFailed: ... must differ when computeDomains is enabled; both resolve to 51516`
  while the DaemonSet and both containers stay unchanged; restoring distinct
  ports returns the GPUCluster to `ready`.

Test bed and captured evidence (not part of this PR):
https://github.com/jramkissoon/nvidia-gpu-operator/tree/gpu-operator-issue-%232979-rebased-26.7.2/deploy/issue-test-bed

title: olm: add nodeAffinity and tolerations to the operator
body:
This commit adds the nodeAffinity and tolerations to the operator 
controller's deployment spec. This change also aligns the OLM bundle 
with the helm chart as the node affinity and tolerations to control plane 
nodes is already added by default by the helm chart.

This nodeAffinity setting ensures that the gpu-operator controller prefers 
control plane/master nodes in an OCP cluster. Conventionally, control 
plane nodes are CPU nodes, so we always want the operator controller pods 
to land on CPU nodes as they become unaffected by pod evictions or drains
performed by operators like the gpu-operator and/or the network-operator.

body:
Bumps [sigs.k8s.io/kustomize/kustomize/v5](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kustomize) from 5.8.1 to 5.8.3.
Release notes

Sourced from sigs.k8s.io/kustomize/kustomize/v5's releases.

kustomize/v5.8.3

This release eliminates dependencies and compressed blobs that were an issue when bumping kustomize-in-kubectl. No functional changes in kustomize.

chore

#6310: chore: bump to Go 1.27 and latest kube-openapi #6318: Update kyaml to v0.21.3 #6320: Update cmd/config to v0.21.3 #6321: Update api to v0.21.3

kustomize/v5.8.2

Introduction

In this release, we implemented refactoring to update dependencies and add new features.

This release adds the kustomize edit add configuration and kustomize edit remove component commands. #6037 #6083 The built-in OpenAPI schema is now loaded from a pre-compiled bundle embedded in the binary. #6190 The schema itself is still based on Kubernetes v1.21.2, so the output of kustomize build is not expected to change. If you notice any difference, please file an issue.

Feature

title: fix(validator): re-probe the host driver while waiting for a driver container
body: ## Summary `driver-validation` probes the host for a pre-installed driver exactly once, before entering the driver-container wait loop. On a node where the driver ships with the OS image, that probe can run before the kernel modules have finished loading — kubelet starts the validator while the node's driver install is still in progress. The single failed probe then commits the validator to waiting for a driver container, and when the driver is not managed by the operator no such container is ever going to exist, so the pod stays in `Init` forever even though the host driver became usable seconds later. In `Driver.runValidation`, `validateHostDriver` is called once and `validateDriverContainer` owns an unconditional retry loop, so there is no path back to the host check once the first probe has failed. Deleting the pod is the only recovery: the replacement re-runs the host probe against a by-then-loaded driver and proceeds normally. ## How it shows up Observed on EKS AL2023 NVIDIA AMIs, where `nvidia-kmod-load.service` takes 57–86s (it installs the kmod and regenerates the initramfs via dracut) and kubelet starts about 9s into it. On one node the validator container started at 08:05:27 and `nvidia-kmod-load.service` finished at 08:05:57, a 30s miss: ``` 08:05:27 info Attempting to validate a pre-installed driver on the host NVIDIA-SMI has failed because it couldn't communicate with the NVIDIA driver. 08:05:27 info No pre-installed driver detected on the host: exit status 9 08:05:27 info Validating containerized driver installation 08:05:27 info Attempting to validate a driver container installation 08:05:27 warn failed to validate the driver, retrying after 5 seconds ... repeats indefinitely ``` The host driver is fully healthy the whole time the pod waits — `nvidia-smi` on the node reports the GPU, all `/dev/nvidia*` nodes are present, and `nvidia-persistenced` is running. `/run/nvidia/driver` is empty, as expected on a node with no driver container. Reproduces on any GPU node where the driver is installed by the OS image rather than by the operator (`nvidia.com/gpu.deploy.driver=false`), and loading the modules takes longer than kubelet's start-to-first-pod time. Environment where it was observed: - GPU Operator Version: v26.3.3 (the code path is unchanged on `v26.7.1` and `main`) - OS: Amazon Linux 2023.12.20260611 (EKS NVIDIA accelerated AMI) - Kernel Version: 6.18.33-63.124.amzn2023.x86_64 - Container Runtime Version: containerd 2.2.4 - Kubernetes Distro and Version: EKS v1.36.2 ## The change The wait loop moves out of `validateDriverContainer` into a new `waitForDriver`, which retries the container *and* re-probes the host on each iteration, so a driver that becomes usable after startup is picked up. `validateDriverContainer` is reduced to a single attempt. The driver container readiness check (`.driver-ctr-ready`) is also a single attempt now. Previously, with `WITH_WAIT=true`, it blocked until the file appeared. On a node where a driver DaemonSet exists in the cluster but doesn't run on that node (e.g. `driver.enabled=true` with the node labelled `nvidia.com/gpu.deploy.driver=false`), the file never appears, so the host would never have been re-probed. Retried host probes are silent, to avoid repeating the same `nvidia-smi` failure output every interval. Behaviour is otherwise unchanged: the first host probe keeps its existing logging and fast path, `isDriverManagedByOperator` is still resolved once, and the non-waiting path returns the same wrapped error. ## Checklist - [x] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes - [x] Lint checks passing (`make lint`) - [x] Generated assets in-sync (`make validate-generated-assets`) - [x] Go mod artifacts in-sync (`make validate-modules`) - [x] Test cases are added for new code paths ## Testing Unit test `Test_waitForDriver` covers four cases, including the regression one: the container probe failing while the host driver appears late. I verified it fails without the fix — the container probe is given a finite failure count, so removing the re-probe makes the case fail on its assertion rather than hang. `Test_waitForDriver_driverManagedByOperatorWithLateHostDriver` runs the real `validateDriverContainer` with the driver marked as operator-managed and waiting enabled, so the readiness check is exercised for real. A timeout guard turns a regression into a failure instead of a hang. It fails against the previous blocking readiness check. `make unit-test` passes. `make lint` reports zero issues in `cmd/nvidia-validator/`. E2E was not run, since the holodeck suite needs NVIDIA infrastructure; `./tests/e2e/` and `./tests/e2e/suites/` were compile-checked and `go vet` is clean. ---

title: [Feature]: Allow external RBAC configuration/dropping bootstrap-only RBAC permissions
body:
👋🏻 
We've been looking at using gpu-operator to simplify some of our GPU infrastructure (and get rid of a couple of pain points at the same time!) - however, and, this might just be an us-problem: at $DAYJOB, we prefer to manage RBAC configurations ourselves/explicitly (i.e., have our own manifests in our gitops repo).

We looked into having our own ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBindings created and dropping any permissions that were unnecessary in our infra (or too broad and not required if the operator no longer needed them to bootstrap itself), but the operator currently doesn't expose a way to skip trying to manage its RBAC configs. 
(i.e., we tried to do this, and were blocked by the operator crashing when it unconditionally tried to manage RBAC and whatnot on launch without the necessary permissions to do so :p)

As far as I can tell, there's no way to skip this code atm, so I'm totally happy to give implementing a feature toggle/env var/whatever a shot as long as y'all don't think this isn't a silly idea...but I figured y'all would want an issue/feature request first before talking about PRs/implementation :D

title: fix: fail the node pool when its additional driver configs do not render
body: ## Description `stateDriver.getManifestObjects` logs the error from `getDriverAdditionalConfigs` and carries on (`internal/state/driver.go:333`): ```go renderData.AdditionalConfigs, err = s.getDriverAdditionalConfigs(ctx, cr, clusterInfo, nodePool) if err != nil { logger.Error(err, "error rendering addition driver volume", "NodePool", nodePool.name) } ``` Every other fallible step in the same loop returns instead: `getDriverSpec`, `getGDSSpec`, `getGDRCopySpec`, `renderManifestObjects`, `handleDefaultImagesInObjects`. Two things follow from carrying on. The call assigns into `renderData.AdditionalConfigs`, so the failure leaves that field nil, and `manifests/state-driver/0500_daemonset.yaml` guards every use of it with `{{- if and .AdditionalConfigs .AdditionalConfigs.VolumeMounts }}` and `.AdditionalConfigs.Volumes`. The driver therefore renders with none of the volumes the user configured: no custom package repository, no custom CA certificates, no kernel module parameters, no vGPU licensing config. And `getDriverAdditionalConfigs` only ever returns `nil` alongside its error, so nothing partial is being salvaged. What a user sees: they set `spec.repoConfig.name` (or `certConfig`, `kernelModuleConfig`, a vGPU `licensingConfig`) on an `NVIDIADriver`, the ConfigMap is missing or misnamed or the node's distro is not in `RepoConfigPathMap`, and the reconcile reports success. The `NVIDIADriver` goes Ready once the pods come up, and the driver runs against the default repository. The only trace is one log line; nothing reaches the CR status or its conditions. A driver built against the wrong package repository is not a milder failure than a reconcile error, it is a harder one to find. The ClusterPolicy path for the same inputs does not behave this way. `transformDriverContainer` in `controllers/object_controls.go` returns `fmt.Errorf("ERROR: failed to create ConfigMap VolumeMounts for custom repo config: %v", err)` to its caller. ## Checklist - [x] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes - [ ] Lint checks passing (`make lint`) - [x] Generated assets in-sync (`make validate-generated-assets`) - [x] Go mod artifacts in-sync (`make validate-modules`) - [x] Test cases are added for new code paths `make lint` fails here, with three `staticcheck` SA4023 findings around `resolveHostNvidiaSMI` in `cmd/nvidia-validator/main.go`. It fails the same way on an untouched tree and has nothing to do with this change, so I left it alone. ## Testing `TestGetManifestObjectsAdditionalConfigsErrorIsLogged` pinned the old behaviour, with a comment reading "The driver is still deployed, silently without the repo config the user asked for". It arrived in #2658, which added unit tests across `internal/state`, so it recorded what the code does rather than what it should do. I renamed it to `TestGetManifestObjectsAdditionalConfigsError` and flipped the assertions, which keeps the same fixture: one GPU node, an `NVIDIADriver` whose `spec.repoConfig.name` points at a ConfigMap that is not in the fake client. With only the test change applied and `driver.go` untouched: ``` --- FAIL: TestGetManifestObjectsAdditionalConfigsError (0.09s) driver_manifest_test.go:538: Error: An error is expected but got nil. ``` and with the fix, `go test ./internal/state/` is ok. `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/state/` and `gofmt -l` are clean, and `go test ./...` passes everywhere except `tests/e2e`, which needs a cluster and fails identically on an untouched tree. No GPU or cluster was used. The whole path is covered by the fake client. ---

title: Mark the NVIDIADriver NotReady when its secretEnv Secret is missing
body: Fixes #3208 `kubectl get nvidiadriver` keeps printing `ready` after the Secret named by `spec.secretEnv` goes missing, and the driver stops being reconciled until something unrelated wakes the controller. The branch at `controllers/nvidiadriver_controller.go:183-194`: ```go secretName := instance.Spec.SecretEnv if len(secretName) > 0 { key := client.ObjectKey{Namespace: r.Namespace, Name: secretName} if err := r.Get(ctx, key, &corev1.Secret{}); err != nil { logger.Error(err, "failed to get secret") if condErr := r.conditionUpdater.SetConditionsError(ctx, instance, conditions.ReconcileFailed, err.Error()); condErr != nil { logger.Error(condErr, "failed to set condition") } return reconcile.Result{}, nil } } ``` Two things are missing, and they compound. **The state is left stale.** Every other error branch in `Reconcile` assigns it first, at lines 98, 113, 126 (`Disabled`), 152, 166 and 176. This one does not, and `nvDriverUpdater.SetConditionsError` cannot make up for it: `internal/conditions/nvidiadriver.go:104-107` copies `cr.Status.State` across and only falls back to `NotReady` when it is empty, under a comment that says whose job it is. ```go // Ensure status.state is not empty when updating the CR status. // The caller should set the state appropriately in the CR // depending on the error condition. instance.Status.State = cr.Status.State if instance.Status.State == "" { instance.Status.State = nvidiav1alpha1.NotReady } ``` So on a fresh install with the Secret absent from the start the fallback does the right thing, and the case that breaks is the one where the CR has already reconciled once: `helm upgrade --set driver.secretEnv=` before the Secret exists or into the wrong namespace, a rotation done as delete-then-recreate, a rename. `.status.state` is a printcolumn (`api/nvidia/v1alpha1/nvidiadriver_types.go:522`), so that is what the operator, `kubectl wait` and any CI gate reading it see. **And nothing comes back for it.** `reconcile.Result{}, nil` asks for no requeue, and `SetupWithManager` watches NVIDIADriver, ClusterPolicy, GPUCluster and Node but not Secrets, so creating the Secret raises no event of its own. The driver stays frozen until a Node label changes, a ClusterPolicy or GPUCluster generation bumps, or the operator restarts. The ClusterPolicy controller gets the same user error right. `createSecretEnvReference` at `controllers/object_controls.go:3827` returns an error, which reaches `clusterpolicy_controller.go:182-189` and both sets `NotReady` and returns the error, so the request is requeued with backoff. ### The change Set `instance.Status.State = nvidiav1alpha1.NotReady` the way the siblings do. `SetupWithManager` now also watches Secrets in the operator namespace and enqueues the NVIDIADrivers whose `spec.secretEnv` names the Secret, on create, update and delete. That covers both cases, a Secret that shows up late and one deleted after a successful reconcile (the second one was pointed out in review). Reconcile only checks that the Secret exists, so the watch and the lookup use `PartialObjectMetadata` and no Secret data ends up in the cache. Since #2886 the cache keeps Secrets in the operator namespace only, and both the kustomize and the Helm roles already grant `watch` on secrets, so no RBAC change is needed. A missing Secret returns without requeue and waits for the watch. Any other lookup error is returned, so it gets retried with backoff like in the ClusterPolicy controller. ### Test `TestEnqueueNVIDIADriversForSecret` checks that a Secret event (with the Secret absent from the client, as on delete) enqueues only the driver that references it, and nothing for a Secret of the same name in another namespace. `TestReconcileMissingSecretEnvSetsNotReadyState`, a fourth sibling to the three status tests already in `controllers/nvidiadriver_controller_test.go`, seeded with `Status.State: Ready` the way `TestReconcileConflictSetsNotReadyState` is. On `main` it fails on the state: ``` Error: Not equal: expected: "notReady" actual : "ready" ``` `TestReconcileMissingSecretEnvPersistsNotReady` (added by @Wizard52007) runs the same case with the real `NewNvDriverUpdater` and reads the driver back, so it also checks that the state and the Error/Ready conditions are actually written to the status. `go build ./...`, `go test ./controllers/` (all pass) and `golangci-lint run ./controllers/...` (0 issues). `go test ./...` fails only in `tests/e2e` `TestE2E`, which needs a live cluster and fails the same way on a clean `main`. I have no GPU cluster here, so everything above is from reading the code plus the fake-client test. ---

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>kubernetes-sigs/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu (nvcr.io/nvidia/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu)</summary>

### [`v0.5.1`](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu/releases/tag/v0.5.1)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu/compare/v0.5.0...v0.5.1)

This is a patch release of the DRA Driver for NVIDIA GPUs. It includes reliability fixes for ComputeDomain and Kubelet plugin.

##### Bug Fixes

- Fixed a race in the ComputeDomain controller that could incorrectly remove live nodes from ComputeDomain status, reassign IMEX node indices, and disrupt GPU memory export/import operations. This was most reproducible with `ComputeDomainCliques` disabled ([#​1440](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu/pull/1440), [#​1418](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu/issues/1418)).
- Fixed an IMEX DNS search-domain flood caused by unresolved static node names falling through to cluster DNS. [#​1466](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu/issues/1466)
- Add a `resources.computeDomains.imex.config` Helm value to override or add arbitrary `nvidia-imex` daemon config file settings (e.g. `IMEX_NODE_DISCONNECTED_GRACE_TIME`). Defaults to `{}`, no behavior change unless set. [#​1497](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu/pull/1497)
- Compute Domain daemon pods now reuse the controller's own `priorityClassName`. CD daemon pods now default to `system-node-critical` priority, matching the controller's own default. [#​1498](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu/pull/1498)
- Fixed bug where certain MIG profiles do not get the CI profile with the most multiprocessors when created. [#​1454](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu/issues/1454)
- Disabled registration of the unimplemented DRA resource health service in both kubelet plugins, preventing repeated `device health reporting is not supported by this driver` errors on Kubernetes v1.36 ([#​1425](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu/pull/1425), [#​1423](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu/issues/1423)).
- Standardized log messages and error formatting across the driver to improve troubleshooting ([#​1376](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu/pull/1376), [#​1369](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu/issues/1369)).

##### Installation

body:
**Context:**

Small cluster with 1 GPU. Both the  nvidia gpu operator's dra-validation and other nvidia GPU workloads needing the same GPU.

**Problem**

The daemonset nvida-dra-validator aquires the GPU (via resource claim template) and runs in 2 steps:
- 1. list available gpu on a node (GPU needed)
- 2. print  "all validations successful" every 86400s without requiring the GPU

The combination of Daemonset and step 2 prevents other GPU workloads from running despite the actual hardware/software GPU validation completed.
