title: olm: fix dead docs link in CSV manifest
[Bug]: NVIDIADriver spec.labels can override the driver DaemonSet's app and component labels
body:
**Describe the bug**
`manifests/state-driver/0500_daemonset.yaml` (lines 23–24 and 64–65) appends `.Driver.Spec.Labels` verbatim after the operator's own `app` and `app.kubernetes.io/component` labels, on both the DaemonSet metadata and the pod template.

`internal/render` decodes the rendered manifest with `k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/yaml.NewYAMLOrJSONDecoder`, which uses non-strict `yaml.YAMLToJSON` (`vendor/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/yaml/decoder.go:100`). Duplicate mapping keys are resolved last-wins without an error. I confirmed this with the vendored `sigs.k8s.io/yaml`: a mapping with `app` twice returns the second value from `YAMLToJSON`, while `YAMLToJSONStrict` returns `key "app" already set in map`.

Consequences, depending on the key a user sets in `spec.labels`:

- `app`: the pod template label no longer matches the immutable selector `app: {{ .Driver.AppName }}`, so the DaemonSet create/update is rejected and the driver is not deployed on that node pool.
- `app.kubernetes.io/component`: the DaemonSet and pods lose `component=nvidia-driver`. That label is used by the upgrade controller (`BuildState` with `app.kubernetes.io/component=nvidia-driver`), orphaned-pod detection (`controllers/nodelabeling_controller.go:593`) and the validator's `isDriverManagedByOperator` (`cmd/nvidia-validator/main.go:713`). Auto-upgrade stops seeing the driver and the validator treats the node as host-driver.

The ClusterPolicy path already protects these keys in `applyCommonDaemonsetLabel` (`controllers/object_controls.go:809`). Draft PR #2973 adds equivalent filtering for GPUCluster only.

**To Reproduce**
Found by code review; not yet reproduced on a cluster. Expected repro:
1. Create an NVIDIADriver with `spec.labels: {app.kubernetes.io/component: custom}` and `upgradePolicy.autoUpgrade: true`.
2. Change the driver version.
3. Observe that the driver DaemonSet has `app.kubernetes.io/component: custom` and no node receives an upgrade state label.

Same with `spec.labels: {app: custom}` → DaemonSet create fails with a selector/template mismatch.

**Expected behavior**
Reserved keys in `spec.labels` are ignored (with a warning/condition) or rejected at admission, as on the ClusterPolicy path.

**Suggested fix**
Filter reserved keys before rendering (shared helper with the ClusterPolicy path), and/or add CEL validation on `NVIDIADriverSpec.Labels` rejecting `app` and `app.kubernetes.io/component`. Optionally switch the renderer to strict YAML so duplicate keys fail loudly.

**Environment (please provide the following information):**
 - GPU Operator Version: main @ f806d6b
 - Found by code inspection; affects any platform using the NVIDIADriver CRD.

title: [Bug]: ClusterPolicy isDaemonSetReady can report Ready from a DaemonSet status of an older generation
body:
**Describe the bug**
#2968 fixed `internal/state/state_skel.go:isDaemonSetReady` to require `status.observedGeneration >= metadata.generation`. The ClusterPolicy implementation in `controllers/object_controls.go:4030` still lacks that check:

- line 4040 returns Ready whenever `status.desiredNumberScheduled == 0`, including for a DaemonSet whose status the DaemonSet controller has not populated yet;
- line 4045 trusts `status.numberUnavailable` before the new generation is observed.

A freshly created or just-updated operand DaemonSet can therefore be reported Ready on the first reconcile pass, so ClusterPolicy can flip Ready → NotReady and later states proceed before the operand is actually scheduled.

**To Reproduce**
Found by code review; not yet reproduced on a cluster. Unit-level: call `isDaemonSetReady` with a DaemonSet with `generation: 2`, `status.observedGeneration: 1`, `desiredNumberScheduled: 0` → returns Ready.

**Expected behavior**
Same semantics as the fixed `state_skel` implementation: not ready until `observedGeneration >= generation`.

**Suggested fix**
Add the observedGeneration guard, or share one readiness helper between the ClusterPolicy and NVIDIADriver/GPUCluster stacks.

**Environment (please provide the following information):**
 - GPU Operator Version: main @ f806d6b (code inspection)

title: [Bug]: Upgrade controller reads ClusterPolicy controller globals without synchronization
body:
**Describe the bug**
`UpgradeReconciler.reconcileClusterPolicyDriverUpgrades` reads the package-level `clusterPolicyCtrl.openshift` and `clusterPolicyCtrl.ocpDriverToolkit.enabled` (`controllers/upgrade_controller.go:135`). These fields are written by `ClusterPolicyReconciler` in `clusterPolicyCtrl.init()` (`controllers/state_manager.go` ~849–925) on a different controller goroutine, with no lock.

Two effects:
1. A data race (the race detector would flag it in an envtest run with both controllers).
2. On OpenShift with the Driver Toolkit, if the upgrade controller reconciles before the first ClusterPolicy reconcile (e.g. right after operator start), it uses `app=nvidia-driver-daemonset`. DTK driver DaemonSets are relabelled `app=<name>-<rhcosVersion>` (`controllers/object_controls.go:3321`), so `BuildState` finds no driver pods until the next 2-minute requeue.

**To Reproduce**
Found by code review; not yet reproduced. Run the controllers under `-race` in envtest with a ClusterPolicy that has `driver.upgradePolicy.autoUpgrade: true`.

**Expected behavior**
The upgrade controller derives its selector from its own reads (ClusterPolicy + cluster info), not from shared mutable state.

**Environment (please provide the following information):**
 - GPU Operator Version: main @ f806d6b (code inspection)

title: [Bug]: Driver auto-upgrade fails on nodes running GPU pods owned by a DaemonSet
body:
**Describe the bug**
`gpuPodSpecFilter` (`cmd/gpu-operator/main.go`) counts every Running/Pending pod that requests `nvidia.com/gpu*` or holds a GPU ResourceClaim, including pods owned by a DaemonSet.

The pod manager in k8s-operator-libs builds its drain helper with `IgnoreAllDaemonSets: true` (`vendor/github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-operator-libs/pkg/upgrade/pod_manager.go:152`), so those pods are excluded from `GetPodsForDeletion`. The check `numPodsCanDelete != numPodsToDelete` (line 194) then fails ("Cannot delete all required pods") and the node moves to drain or `upgrade-failed`. Drain ignores DaemonSet pods too, so it cannot clear them either.

Result: any GPU-consuming DaemonSet (inference agents, custom exporters, etc.) blocks driver auto-upgrade on every node where it runs. Related to, but different from, #2570 (consumers without a GPU resource request).

**To Reproduce**
Found by code review; not yet reproduced on a cluster. Expected repro:
1. Deploy a DaemonSet whose pods request `nvidia.com/gpu: 1`.
2. Enable `driver.upgradePolicy.autoUpgrade` with `podDeletion` and change the driver version.
3. The node logs "Cannot delete all required pods" and ends in `upgrade-failed`.

**Expected behavior**
Either DaemonSet-owned GPU pods are deleted explicitly (the DaemonSet recreates them after the driver restarts), or they are excluded from the count with a clear event.

**Environment (please provide the following information):**
 - GPU Operator Version: main @ f806d6b (code inspection)

title: [Bug]: Orphaned driver pod migration sets upgrade-required on NVIDIADriver pools with autoUpgrade disabled
body:
**Describe the bug**
`labelNodesWithOrphanedDriverPods` (`controllers/nodelabeling_controller.go:581`) sets the upgrade state label to `upgrade-required` (line 625) on any node owned by a live NVIDIADriver that runs an ownerless driver pod. It does not check that NVIDIADriver's `upgradePolicy.autoUpgrade`.

For an NVIDIADriver with `autoUpgrade: false`, `reconcileNVIDIADriverUpgrades` removes the same label (`controllers/upgrade_controller.go:262`). Each later node-labeling reconcile adds it back, so the label flaps and the orphaned pod is never replaced.

**To Reproduce**
Found by code review; not yet reproduced. Expected: migrate from a ClusterPolicy-managed driver to an NVIDIADriver with `upgradePolicy.autoUpgrade: false`, leaving the old driver pods orphaned; watch the node's upgrade state label across reconciles.

**Expected behavior**
Skip nodes whose NVIDIADriver has auto-upgrade disabled, and report (event/condition) that the orphaned pod needs manual replacement.

**Environment (please provide the following information):**
 - GPU Operator Version: main @ f806d6b (code inspection)

title: [Bug]: Malformed logr calls drop errors; validator transform errors are ignored
body:
**Describe the bug**
Seven calls pass printf-style arguments to logr's key/value API:

- `controllers/resource_manager.go:72`
- `controllers/object_controls.go:2374, 2406, 4013, 4065, 4856, 5261`

e.g. `n.logger.Info("Could not get PodList", err)`. With zap in production mode this logs an "odd number of arguments" DPanic and the error is not logged as an error; with `--zap-devel=true` DPanic panics.

At 2374 and 2406, errors from `TransformValidatorComponent` are only logged as WARN and rendering continues, so a partially transformed validator DaemonSet can be deployed.

**To Reproduce**
Found by code review. Any failing path above, e.g. a `List` error in `isDaemonSetReady`, produces the malformed log line.

**Expected behavior**
Errors logged with `logger.Error(err, msg)`; transform errors returned so the state reports NotReady.

**Suggested fix**
Fix the seven calls, return the validator transform error, and enable `loggercheck` in `.golangci.yml`.

**Environment (please provide the following information):**
 - GPU Operator Version: main @ f806d6b (code inspection)

title: [Bug]: nvidia-validator waits the full timeout on a failed validation pod; loadPodSpec panics
body:
**Describe the bug**
- `waitForPod` (`cmd/nvidia-validator/main.go:1347`) only returns on phase `Succeeded`. If the plugin or CUDA validation pod reaches `Failed`, it keeps polling for 60 × 5 s = 5 minutes and never logs why the pod failed.
- `loadPodSpec` calls `panic(err)` on a read error (line 1370) and indexes `slice[1]` without a length check (line 1378); the parsed `kind` is only logged.

**To Reproduce**
Found by code review. Make the CUDA validation pod fail (e.g. a broken runtime class) and observe the validator wait 5 minutes before erroring, with no failure reason in its log.

**Expected behavior**
Return immediately on `PodFailed` with the container's termination reason/message; return errors from `loadPodSpec` instead of panicking.

**Environment (please provide the following information):**
 - GPU Operator Version: main @ f806d6b (code inspection)

title: [Feature]: Share readiness, reserved-label filtering and OS-tag logic between the ClusterPolicy and NVIDIADriver/GPUCluster stacks
body:
**Motivation**
Several recent defects are the same fix applied to one stack but not the other:

- #2968 added an `observedGeneration` guard to `internal/state/state_skel.go:isDaemonSetReady`; the ClusterPolicy copy in `controllers/object_controls.go:4030` still lacks it (#3060).
- Reserved operand labels are protected on the ClusterPolicy path (`applyCommonDaemonsetLabel`, `object_controls.go:809`) but not for NVIDIADriver (#3059) or GPUCluster (#2955, draft #2973).
- OS-tag derivation is duplicated in `controllers/state_manager.go:605` and `internal/state/nodepool.go:162`.

**Proposal**
An internal package (e.g. `internal/operand`) exporting `IsDaemonSetReady`, `FilterReservedLabels` and `OSTag`, called by both stacks, with one table-driven test suite. Future fixes then land once.

Related: #3059, #3060, #2955, #2973. Found during a code review of `main` @ f806d6b.

title: [Feature]: CEL validation rejecting reserved label keys in operand label maps
body:
**Motivation**
User label maps are merged into operand DaemonSets, and reserved keys (`app`, `app.kubernetes.io/component`, `app.kubernetes.io/name`, `app.kubernetes.io/part-of`) either break the selector or detach the operand from the code that finds it (#3059, NVIDIA/gpu-operator#2955). Today this is silent: the ClusterPolicy path drops such keys with a log line, and the NVIDIADriver/GPUCluster templates let them win.

**Proposal**
Add `x-kubernetes-validations` on the label maps (`NVIDIADriverSpec.Labels`, GPUCluster `daemonsets.labels`, ClusterPolicy `daemonsets.labels`), for example:

```
// +kubebuilder:validation:XValidation:rule="!self.exists(k, k in ['app','app.kubernetes.io/component','app.kubernetes.io/name','app.kubernetes.io/part-of'])",message="reserved operand label keys cannot be set"
```

Ratcheting validation (GA in Kubernetes 1.33) lets existing objects keep reconciling; for ClusterPolicy it could start as a warning-only change. This is a lighter alternative to the admission webhook in NVIDIA/cloud-native-team#741 for this one check.

Related: NVIDIA/gpu-operator#3059, NVIDIA/gpu-operator#2955, NVIDIA/cloud-native-team#741, NVIDIA/gpu-operator#3066.

title: [Feature]: Strict YAML decoding in internal/render, plus a hostile-label render test
body:
**Motivation**
`internal/render/render.go` decodes rendered manifests with `yamlDecoder.NewYAMLOrJSONDecoder` (line 139), which uses non-strict `yaml.YAMLToJSON`. Duplicate mapping keys are resolved last-wins with no error, which is how a user label can silently replace an operand's `app` or component label (#3059). Any future template bug that emits a key twice will fail the same silent way.

**Proposal**
1. Split rendered output into documents and convert each with `sigs.k8s.io/yaml.YAMLToJSONStrict`, so duplicate keys become render errors surfaced as a failed state.
2. Add a unit test that renders every manifest under `manifests/` and `assets/` with label and annotation maps containing reserved keys, asserting either an error or that the operator's values survive.

Related: #3059, #3067.

title: [Feature]: Replace the package-global clusterPolicyCtrl and run tests with -race
body:
**Motivation**
`controllers/clusterpolicy_controller.go:61` declares a package-level `clusterPolicyCtrl` that the ClusterPolicy reconciler mutates in `init()` and other controllers read (the upgrade controller at `upgrade_controller.go:135`; `state_manager.go:615` and `665` read `operatorNamespace`). This causes an unsynchronized read across controller goroutines (#3061) and makes the code hard to test in isolation.

**Proposal**
1. Build the controller state per reconcile (or behind an accessor with a lock), and have other controllers derive what they need (OpenShift/DTK detection, namespace) from their own reads.
2. Add `-race` to `make unit-test` and to any envtest suite that starts more than one controller, so this class of bug is caught in CI.

Related: #3061.

title: [Feature]: State manager should read before create instead of creating every object on every reconcile
body:
**Motivation**
`internal/state/state_skel.go:createOrUpdateObjs` (line 301) calls `Create` for every rendered object on every reconcile and treats `AlreadyExists` as the signal to fall back to Get + Update. NVIDIADriver and GPUCluster requeue every 5 s while NotReady (and GPUCluster every minute when Ready), so a steady-state cluster sends a constant stream of failing Create calls: API server load, audit-log noise, and admission webhooks invoked for no change.

**Proposal**
Get the object from the informer cache first; Create only on NotFound; Update only when the desired hash differs. Server-side apply (see the drift-detection proposal filed alongside this) would also remove the pattern.

title: [Feature]: Correct drift on operand DaemonSets instead of comparing only the stored hash annotation
body:
**Motivation**
`createOrUpdateObjs` (`internal/state/state_skel.go:301`) skips the update when the DaemonSet's `NvidiaAnnotationHashKey` annotation equals the hash of the desired object. The hash is computed from the desired object only, so if someone edits the live DaemonSet (image, env, tolerations) and leaves the annotation alone, the operator never restores it. Drift persists until the CR spec changes.

**Proposal**
Use server-side apply with a dedicated field manager for operand objects: apply the desired object on each reconcile and let the API server compute the no-op. This corrects drift on fields the operator owns, leaves fields owned by others alone, and replaces the create-then-update pattern in #3070. If SSA is too large a change, compare a hash of the relevant live fields rather than the stored annotation.

Related: #3070.

title: [Feature]: Reduce the operator's Pod cache: scope or metadata-only watches
body:
**Motivation**
The node-labeling controller watches `corev1.Pod` cluster-wide (`controllers/nodelabeling_controller.go:784`) to catch driver pods turning Running and to find DRA claim pods per node, so the manager caches every Pod in the cluster with full specs and status. On large clusters this dominates the operator's memory, even though only driver pods (by label) and pods on GPU nodes are relevant.

**Proposal**
- Cache driver pods via a label-selected informer (`app.kubernetes.io/component=nvidia-driver` in the operator namespace) using controller-runtime `cache.Options.ByObject`.
- For per-node DRA claim checks, either use a metadata-only watch (`PartialObjectMetadata`) plus targeted reads, or list by `spec.nodeName` field selector through the API reader when needed.

This complements #2886 (reducing what is stored in the cache).

title: [Feature]: Use the cached client in gpuPodSpecFilter instead of the API reader
body:
**Motivation**
`cmd/gpu-operator/main.go` builds the upgrade pod-deletion filter with `gpuPodSpecFilter(ctx, mgr.GetAPIReader())`. For every candidate pod with ResourceClaims, `controllers.PodHasNVIDIAGPUClaim` then does a live `GET` per claim against the API server, on every upgrade pass and for every node being upgraded.

The node-labeling controller already calls the same helper with the manager's cached client (`nodeHasDRAClaimPods`), so ResourceClaims are already served from the cache.

**Proposal**
Pass `mgr.GetClient()` (or a dedicated cached reader) to `gpuPodSpecFilter`. If freshness is a concern for a claim allocated moments ago, fall back to the API reader only on cache miss.

title: [Feature]: Operator readiness probe should reflect informer cache sync, not healthz.Ping
body:
**Motivation**
`cmd/gpu-operator/main.go:255` registers `mgr.AddReadyzCheck("check", healthz.Ping)`, so the operator pod reports Ready as soon as the HTTP server starts, before its informer caches have synced. Rollouts, PodDisruptionBudgets and monitoring treat a new operator replica as serving while it cannot yet reconcile.

**Proposal**
Register a readiness checker that fails until the manager's cache has synced, e.g. a closure calling `mgr.GetCache().WaitForCacheSync` with a short timeout, and keep `healthz.Ping` for liveness only.

title: [Feature]: Use exponential backoff instead of fixed 5 s requeues for failing NVIDIADriver/GPUCluster states
body:
**Motivation**
When a state is not ready, `NVIDIADriverReconciler.Reconcile` and `GPUClusterReconciler.Reconcile` return `RequeueAfter: 5s` with a nil error, including when a state reports an `ErrInfo` (a render or apply error that will not fix itself). The controllers' exponential rate limiter (`minDelayCR`..`maxDelayCR`) is bypassed, so a permanently broken pool re-renders and re-applies every manifest about 720 times an hour, with matching log volume.

**Proposal**
- When any state returns `ErrInfo`, return the error so the rate limiter applies backoff.
- Keep a short requeue only for "waiting for pods", or rely on the DaemonSet watches the state manager already registers to trigger the next reconcile.

title: Fix malformed logr calls flagged by loggercheck
body: Fixes #3064 **Problem** Seven calls passed printf-style arguments to logr's key/value API (e.g. `n.logger.Info("Could not get PodList", err)`). zap reports these as "odd number of arguments" (DPanic, which panics with `--zap-devel=true`), and the errors weren't logged as errors. **Changes** - `controllers/object_controls.go`: the four `List` failures now use `n.logger.Error(err, msg)`. The WARN logs in `TransformValidator` and `TransformSandboxValidator` pass the error as an `"error"` key/value pair instead of a `%v` placeholder. - `controllers/resource_manager.go`: the `filepath.Walk` debug log uses key/value pairs. - `.golangci.yml`: enable `loggercheck` so this can't come back. Per review, the change no longer alters behaviour: the validator transforms still log and continue. Returning those errors can follow as a separate PR. **Testing** - `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` - `go test ./controllers/...` passes - `golangci-lint run ./...` (v2.14.0, with `loggercheck` enabled): 0 issues Single commit, rebased onto current main and signed off (DCO). ---

title: [Bug]: default-kind management.nvidia.com/gpu incompatible with non-cdi strategies, making GPU pods unresolable
body:
**Describe the bug**
The operator sets default-kind to [management.nvidia.com/gpu](http://management.nvidia.com/gpu), and that kind contains only the "all" device by design. Any device list that arrives as bare names therefore cannot resolve in CDI mode: it is qualified with a kind that is guaranteed not to contain it. That makes the volume-mounts device list strategy and `ACCEPT_NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES_AS_VOLUME_MOUNTS` incompatible with `cdi.enabled`. 

**To Reproduce**
  1. Deploy GPU Operator with cdi.enabled=true.
  2. Set `devicePlugin.env.DEVICE_LIST_STRATEGY=cdi-cri,cdi-annotations,volume-mounts` and `toolkit.env.ACCEPT_NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES_AS_VOLUME_MOUNTS=true` in ClusterPolicy.
  3. Run a pod requesting nvidia.com/gpu: 1 with `runtimeClassName: nvidia`.

```
  apiVersion: v1
  kind: Pod
  metadata:
    name: test-cdi-device-plugin
    namespace: cdi-test
  spec:
    tolerations:
    - key: nvidia.com/gpu
      value: "true"
      effect: NoSchedule
    restartPolicy: Never
    containers:
    - name: gpu-test
      image: nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:13.0.0-base-ubuntu24.04
      command: ["sh", "-c", "nvidia-smi -L"]
      resources:
        limits:
          nvidia.com/gpu: 1
```

The container never starts with error - 

```
  Normal   Pulling    12s   kubelet            spec.containers{gpu-test}: Pulling image "nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:13.0.0-base-ubuntu24.04"
  Normal   Pulled     8s    kubelet            spec.containers{gpu-test}: Successfully pulled image "nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:13.0.0-base-ubuntu24.04" in 4.301s (4.301s including waiting). Image size: 139357825 bytes.
  Normal   Created    8s    kubelet            spec.containers{gpu-test}: Container created
  Warning  Failed     8s    kubelet            spec.containers{gpu-test}: Error: failed to create containerd task: failed to create shim task: OCI runtime create failed: could not apply required modification to OCI specification: error modifying OCI spec: failed to inject CDI devices: unresolvable CDI devices management.nvidia.com/gpu=GPU-67fa9265-2b87-d8ce-e708-13e93416062c

```


**Expected behavior**
(1) The management.nvidia.com/gpu as default shouldn't get applies on workload pods. 

(2) It would help if the CDI page stated that when CDI is enabled, `DEVICE_LIST_STRATEGY` must contain only CDI strategies and `ACCEPT_NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES_AS_VOLUME_MOUNTS` must be unset in ClusterPolicy - https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/cloud-native/gpu-operator/25.10/cdi.html#about-the-container-device-interfacehttps://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/cloud-native/gpu-operator/25.10/cdi.html#about-the-container-device-interface

**Environment (please provide the following information):**

nvidia-container-toolkit version: v1.18.1
NVIDIA Driver Version: 580.126.20
Host OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
Kernel Version: 6.8.0-1046-nvidia

CPU Architecture x86_64 and arm64

title: fix[device-plugin] add DEVICE_LIST_STRATEGY env var guardrail
body:
This commit adds additional validation to the devicePlugin operand transformation logic. When CDI is enabled, it is required that the DEVICE_LIST_STRATEGY env var value includes one of "cdi-annotations" and "cdi-cri". While the current transformation code adds these values to DEVICE_LIST_STRATEGY when .spec.cdi.enabled is true, the same resolved value gets overridden when the gpu-operator user sets the DEVICE_LIST_STRATEGY env var explicitly in the devicePlugin section of the ClusterPolicy custom resource. 

This changes addresses a major limitation in the gpu-operator where feedback from an invalid devicePlugin config  only happens at gpu pod workload scheduling which is a significant delay. This provides a poor UX as users waste hours debugging the containerCreate failures instead of identifying the invalid devicePlugin config. This fix changes that by failing at the ClusterPolicy reconcile stage.

title: [Bug]: container-toolkit DaemonSet: containerd-socket hostPath volume lacks mountPropagation: HostToContainer, pins host ZFS mounts and blocks zfs destroy ("dataset is busy")
body:
**Problem**

The nvidia-container-toolkit-daemonset in GPU Operator v26.7.1 mounts these hostPath volumes:
|  volume |  hostPath | mountPath | mountPropagation |
| --------- | ---------- | ------------ | --------------------- |
| host-root | / | /host | HostToContainer |
| driver-install-dir | /run/nvidia/driver | /driver-root | HostToContainer   |
| containerd-socket | /run/containerd | /runtime/sock-dir/ | not set (private) |

The toolkit container's own rootfs lives under /run/containerd. Its /host sub-mount carries every host mount, including all ZFS datasets. Because containerd-socket is a private recursive bind, the whole mount tree is copied into the container's mount namespace when the container starts. After that, the copy never receives unmount events from the host.

**Impact**

- Any ZFS dataset that is mounted on the host when the toolkit container starts stays pinned in the container's mount namespace.
- Later, the host unmounts the dataset, and it reports mounted=no. But zfs destroy still fails with cannot destroy '<dataset>': dataset is busy.
- The dataset stays undeletable until the toolkit container restarts. The restart re-pins every dataset that exists at that moment.
- This affects every container restart, including node reboots. Datasets created after the container starts are not affected.

**Evidence**

After the dataset is unmounted on the host, its mount entries are still found in the toolkit process's mount namespace:
$ grep -l <dataset> /proc/[0-9]*/mountinfo
/proc/<pid>/mountinfo          # comm=nvidia-toolkit
.../runtime/sock-dir/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/k8s.io/<container-id>/rootfs/host/<dataset mountpoint>  - zfs

**Environment**

- NVIDIA GPU Operator v26.7.1 (Helm chart gpu-operator-v26.7.1)
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04
- Kernel Version: 6.8.0-142-generic
- Container Runtime Version: containerd v2.1.4
- Container-toolkit image: nvcr.io/nvidia/k8s/container-toolkit:v1.20.1
- GPU Driver: 580.105.08
- Host filesystems: ZFS datasets mounted on the host
- Kubernetes Distro and Version: Kubelet v1.33.5

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Create and mount a ZFS dataset on a GPU node.
2. Restart the nvidia-container-toolkit pod on that node, or reboot the node.
3. Unmount the dataset on the host and run zfs destroy -r <dataset>.
4. The destroy fails with dataset is busy. The dataset's mount is still listed in the toolkit process's /proc/<pid>/mountinfo.

**Requested fix**

Set mountPropagation: HostToContainer on the containerd-socket volume, the same as host-root and driver-install-dir, so that host unmounts propagate into the container. A setting in ClusterPolicy to configure it would also work. Patching the DaemonSet by hand isn't a durable workaround because the operator reconciles it back.

title: [Bug]: driver-validation hides why a pre-installed driver failed and loops without a reason
body:
**Describe the bug**

With `driver.enabled=false`, if `nvidia-smi` exists on the host but fails (for example `Failed to initialize NVML: Driver/library version mismatch` after an unattended upgrade of the driver packages without a reboot), the `driver-validation` init container of `nvidia-operator-validator` does three things. It logs `No pre-installed driver detected on the host: exit status 18`. It then falls through to the driver-container path. After that it logs `failed to validate the driver, retrying after 5 seconds\n` every 5 seconds without the underlying error. The pod stays in `Init`, and nothing in the validator log says that the host driver is installed but broken.

**To Reproduce**

1. Use a node with a pre-installed driver and `driver.enabled=false`.
2. Make the host `nvidia-smi` fail. One way is to upgrade the driver user-space packages without reloading the kernel module. A fake `/host/usr/bin/nvidia-smi` that prints the mismatch message and exits non-zero gives the same logs.
3. Read the `driver-validation` container logs of a fresh `nvidia-operator-validator` pod on that node.

**Expected behavior**

The log says that `nvidia-smi` was found on the host and failed, and the retry warning includes the error it is retrying on.

**Environment**

- GPU Operator v26.3.3 (also current `main`), pre-installed driver on Ubuntu, Kubernetes v1.34, containerd.

Related: #1276, #1687 (users stuck on the same retry line without a reason). I have a small patch ready.

This issue was drafted with AI assistance and reviewed by me.

title: fix(validator): say why host driver validation failed
body:
## Description

When a node has a pre-installed driver (`driver.enabled=false`) and `nvidia-smi` on the host cannot talk to the driver, for example after the driver packages were upgraded without a reboot, the `driver-validation` init container logs the following. This output is from the reproduction described under Testing, not from a real node: the fake host `nvidia-smi` exits with 18, which I picked because it is `NVML_ERROR_LIB_RM_VERSION_MISMATCH` in `nvml.h`. I later measured a real mismatch: on a host with kernel module 580.95.05, the 610.43.03 nvidia-smi and libnvidia-ml (extracted from the installer, not installed) print `Failed to initialize NVML: Driver/library version mismatch` and exit 18 in 10 of 10 runs, so the reproduction matches. The validator logs whatever exit status nvidia-smi returns.

```
Attempting to validate a pre-installed driver on the host
Failed to initialize NVML: Driver/library version mismatch
No pre-installed driver detected on the host: exit status 18
Validating containerized driver installation
Attempting to validate a driver container installation
failed to validate the driver, retrying after 5 seconds\n
failed to validate the driver, retrying after 5 seconds\n
...
```

and stays in `Init` forever. Both log lines point away from the problem. A driver is installed on the host, and the retry warning never says what failed (it also prints a literal `\n`). #1276 and #1687 show users stuck on the same retry line without a reason.

This PR:

- `validateHostDriver`: when `nvidia-smi` was found on the host but failed, return `found '<path>' on the host, but running it failed: <err>`.
- `runValidation`: log `No usable pre-installed driver detected on the host: ...` instead of `No pre-installed driver detected ...`.
- `validateDriverContainer`: include the error in the retry warning and drop the trailing `\n`.

Control flow does not change. Validation still falls through to the driver container path, which is still needed when the host has a stray `nvidia-smi` but the driver comes from the driver container.

This overlaps with #3034 on the retry warning line. If #3034 merges first, I will rebase and move the error into the warning in `waitForDriver`.

## Checklist

- [x] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes
- [ ] Lint checks passing (`make lint`) (golangci-lint not available locally; `gofmt -s` and `go vet` with `GOOS=linux` are clean)
- [x] Generated assets in-sync (`make validate-generated-assets`) (no generated files changed)
- [x] Go mod artifacts in-sync (`make validate-modules`) (no module changes)
- [ ] Test cases are added for new code paths (log/error text only; `validateHostDriver` chroots into `/host`, so it is not unit-testable without a refactor)

## Testing

- `go test ./cmd/nvidia-validator/` passes.
- On a cluster running GPU Operator v26.3.3, I ran the validator on a GPU node in a temporary pod with the `nvidia-operator-validator` service account. `/host` was a fake root whose `/usr/bin/nvidia-smi` prints `Failed to initialize NVML: Driver/library version mismatch` and exits with 18. The run used `WITH_WAIT=true`, `--component driver`, and a 12s timeout, and I ran it once with the `main` binary and once with the patched binary, both built from the same commit (`CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux`).

Before (`main`):
```
level=info msg="No pre-installed driver detected on the host: exit status 18"
level=warning msg="failed to validate the driver, retrying after 5 seconds\n"
```
After:
```
level=info msg="No usable pre-installed driver detected on the host: found '/usr/bin/nvidia-smi' on the host, but running it failed: exit status 18"
level=warning msg="failed to validate the driver, retrying after 5 seconds: failed to locate driver libraries: error locating \"libnvidia-ml.so.1\""
```

Prepared with help from Claude (AI), including the local checks described above.

Fixes #3085

title: Publish a daily GPU Operator chart and OLM bundle with main-branch operand images
body: ## Description Publish a daily Helm chart and OLM bundle with main-branch operand images for CI and QA, and run forward compatibility against them. - `publish-main-chart.yaml` (daily) resolves the newest main image of each operand, prepares the chart values once, and publishes the chart, the bundle and a build record (chart, bundle and image digests), all tagged `0.0.0-main-`, for example `0.0.0-main-20261016`. There is one build per date: a run stops if that date's record exists, unless started by hand with `overwrite`. The record is pushed only when both chart and bundle were published. DCGM, DCGM exporter, GDS, GDRCopy, the driver and the DRA driver stay on released versions. - It reuses the RC workflow's pieces: `merge-yaml.py` for the chart values, `update-csv-images.py` for the bundle CSV, and two new composite actions, shared by both workflows, that set up the bundle tools and validate and push the bundle. The CSV name and version are unchanged, so a main bundle is installed on its own, not through a catalog. - `forward-compatibility.yaml` (Mondays) installs the chart of the newest recorded build, and fails if it is dated before yesterday (UTC) or its digest changed. `e2e-tests.yaml` can now install a published chart via `chart_reference` and `chart_version`. ## Using a main build ``` VERSION=0.0.0-main-20261016 # or the newest: $(regctl tag ls ghcr.io/nvidia/gpu-operator/main-builds | sort | tail -n 1) regctl artifact get ghcr.io/nvidia/gpu-operator/main-builds:${VERSION} | jq . helm install gpu-operator oci://ghcr.io/nvidia/gpu-operator/charts/gpu-operator --version ${VERSION} operator-sdk run bundle ghcr.io/nvidia/gpu-operator/gpu-operator-bundle:${VERSION} ``` ## Checklist - [x] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes - [x] Lint checks passing (`make lint`): no Go changes; shellcheck and actionlint are clean on the changed scripts and workflows apart from findings that already exist on main - [x] Generated assets in-sync (`make validate-generated-assets`): no generated assets touched - [x] Go mod artifacts in-sync (`make validate-modules`): no module changes - [ ] Test cases are added for new code paths: the repo has no shell test framework, so the scripts were tested with local harnesses (below) ## Testing - Script tests with stubbed `curl`, `regctl`, `helm` and `sleep`. - Packaged a main chart and bundle with real main images: overrides render in the ClusterPolicy, and `operator-sdk bundle validate` and `make validate-csv` pass. - Ran the daily workflow on a fork: chart, bundle and record were published as `0.0.0-main-20261020`, and the record was read back as forward compatibility reads it. Re-running the whole run found that date published and skipped publishing, leaving the chart unchanged. closes: https://github.com/NVIDIA/cloud-native-team/issues/586 ---

title: Configure CDI annotation prefixes in toolkit container when CDI is enabled
body: ## Description This aligns the transformToolkitCtrForCDI() method with the transformDevicePluginCtrForCDI() to ensure the same prefixes are configured with both components. Without explicitly configuring the CDI annotation prefixes in the toolkit container, the nvidia-ctk-installer was NOT adding these annotation prefixes to containerd's (or crio's) container_annotations allowlist. As a consequence, any container annotations set by the k8s-device-plugin, in its AllocateResponse, were not making it into the OCI runtime spec for the container. ## Checklist - [x] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes - [x] Lint checks passing (`make lint`) - [x] Generated assets in-sync (`make validate-generated-assets`) - [x] Go mod artifacts in-sync (`make validate-modules`) - [x] Test cases are added for new code paths ## Testing Ran a sanity test on both k8s + containerd and OpenShift. I verified that https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/issues/3077 is no longer an issue with this change. This is because the container annotation added by the k8s-device-plugin actually makes its way to the `nvidia` runtime. The problematic volume mount is never processed and the container runs as expected with access to one GPU. As a follow-up, https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/pull/2146 aims to provide a more robust solution to handle scenarios where CDI is used AND the `volume-mounts` strategy is configured with the toolkit / plugin. ---

title: add a tolerations field for Helm
body:
## Description

<!-- Brief description of the change, including context or motivation -->

title: [Bug]: dcgm-exporter no longer gets hostNetwork when a host DCGM is set through dcgmExporter.env
body:
**Describe the bug**

For DCGM running on the host (DGX BaseOS), `TransformDCGMExporter` enables `hostNetwork` and `ClusterFirstWithHostNet` when `dcgm.enabled` is false and `DCGM_REMOTE_HOSTENGINE_INFO` starts with `localhost`, so the exporter can reach `nv-hostengine` on `localhost:5555`.

The check reads the variable from the container (`controllers/object_controls.go`, the `else` branch after `config.DCGM.IsEnabled()`), but `dcgmExporter.env` is only applied at the end of the function. The shipped `assets/state-dcgm-exporter/0800_daemonset.yaml` does not set the variable, so the check always sees an empty value and the exporter stays on the pod network, where `localhost:5555` is not reachable.

The order changed in 54c270cf3 ("Ensured user-supplied envvars take precedence"), first released in v25.10.0. The existing test case "transform dcgm exporter with dcgm running on the host itself(DGX BaseOS)" still passes because it puts the variable on the input DaemonSet container as well as in `dcgmExporter.env`.

**To Reproduce**

Found by reading the code and confirmed with a unit test on main (dbb11e851): `TransformDCGMExporter` with `dcgm.enabled: false`, `dcgmExporter.env: [{name: DCGM_REMOTE_HOSTENGINE_INFO, value: "localhost:5555"}]` and the container env empty returns a DaemonSet with the variable set but `hostNetwork: false`.

Expected on a cluster (not run):

1. Install with `--set dcgm.enabled=false --set dcgmExporter.env[0].name=DCGM_REMOTE_HOSTENGINE_INFO --set dcgmExporter.env[0].value=localhost:5555` on a node running `nv-hostengine`.
2. The `nvidia-dcgm-exporter` pod runs without `hostNetwork` and cannot connect to the host engine.

Setting `dcgmExporter.hostNetwork: true` works around it.

**Expected behavior**

A `localhost` value from `dcgmExporter.env` enables `hostNetwork` as it did before v25.10.0. A fix that runs the check after the user env is applied is in #3092.

**Environment (please provide the following information):**
 - GPU Operator Version: main at dbb11e851; the same code is in v26.7.2, and the order changed in v25.10.0
 - OS, kernel, container runtime, Kubernetes distro: not run on a cluster; reproduced with a unit test (Go 1.27.2, macOS arm64)

title: fix(dcgm-exporter): enable hostNetwork for a host DCGM set through dcgmExporter.env
body:

title: Allow configuring the Toolkit DaemonSet RuntimeClass
body:
## Description

When a node uses the NVIDIA runtime as its default runtime, the Container Toolkit DaemonSet also depends on that runtime to start. If the host NVIDIA runtime files are missing or corrupted, the Toolkit pod cannot start to reinstall them.(about [issue](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/issues/2153))

This PR adds an optional `toolkit.runtimeClassName` setting to Helm values and `spec.toolkit.runtimeClassName` to ClusterPolicy. It allows the Toolkit pod, including its init containers, to use an existing RuntimeClass backed by an independent runtime such as system runc.

Example Helm values:

```yaml
toolkit:
  runtimeClassName: toolkit-runc
```

The referenced RuntimeClass and its runtime handler must already be configured. An empty value preserves the current behavior of using the node's default runtime.

The setting applies only to the Toolkit DaemonSet. It is independent of `operator.runtimeClass` and the NVIDIA runtime configuration installed on the host. The generated CRDs are synchronized across the source manifests, Helm chart, and OLM bundle.

This enables the Toolkit installer to run again after its container restarts even when the host NVIDIA runtime is unavailable. Installation atomicity and durability are outside the scope of this change.

title: [Bug]: ClusterPolicy reconcile panics when a DaemonSet has no annotations
body:
## Describe the bug

`isDaemonsetSpecChanged` panics when the live DaemonSet object has a nil annotation map. controller-runtime recovers the panic, so the operator process stays up, but that ClusterPolicy reconcile does not converge.

This was found by reading `controllers/object_controls.go` on main (operator v26.7.2). It is not a live cluster repro. The panic was added in [`7843bcbfa`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/commit/7843bcbfa), which assumed both DaemonSets already had an annotation map. Issue #499 was a different nil-map panic, in `applyCommonDaemonsetMetadata`, and that one was fixed.

## To reproduce

From the code path:

1. Call `isDaemonsetSpecChanged` with a live DaemonSet whose `metadata.annotations` is nil.
2. A real `apps/v1` read does not produce that nil map. etcd stores the internal DaemonSet, and conversion to `apps/v1` always writes `deprecated.daemonset.template.generation`. Removing `nvidia.com/last-applied-hash` leaves that annotation, so the map stays non-nil.
3. A unit test or a fake client can still pass a nil map. On main, that panics before the missing-hash branch runs.

Unit test, on current main:

```
go test -count=1 -run TestIsDaemonsetSpecChanged/nil_live_annotations ./controllers/
```

That case panics with `appsv1.DaemonSet.Annotations must be allocated prior to calling isDaemonsetSpecChanged()`.

## Expected behavior

Treat a nil live annotation map like a missing hash: set `nvidia.com/last-applied-hash` on the desired DaemonSet and update it. The NVIDIADriver path in `internal/state/state_skel.go` already does this with `GetAnnotations()`.

The desired object should still be required to have an allocated annotation map. The caller allocates that before the compare.

I will open a pull request with that change. This does not implement #3071 (detecting spec drift beyond the stored hash).

title: Fix DaemonSet hash compare when live annotations are nil
body:
## Description

`isDaemonsetSpecChanged` panics when the live DaemonSet object has a nil annotation map. A nil map is now treated as a missing `nvidia.com/last-applied-hash`: the hash is recorded and the DaemonSet is updated.

Fixes #3096

The desired object is still required to have an allocated annotation map. The caller allocates that before the compare, and that programmer error still panics. A live `apps/v1` DaemonSet from the API server keeps `deprecated.daemonset.template.generation`, so deleting the hash key does not nil the map. The nil map is the unit-test and fake-client input. On main that input panicked before the missing-hash branch could run.

This is not #499. That panic was in `applyCommonDaemonsetMetadata` and was fixed earlier. This also does not implement #3071. The compare is still the stored hash. The only new path is a nil live map, which previously panicked before the missing-hash branch could run.

title: [Bug]: Precompiled node pools drop kernels that sanitize to the same name
body:
## Describe the bug

With `spec.usePrecompiled: true`, `getNodePools` keeps one node pool per sanitized kernel name. `getSanitizedKernelVersion` strips `x86_64`, `aarch64`, and an optional `_64k`. Two nodes whose raw `feature.node.kubernetes.io/kernel-version.full` values differ only by architecture or page size collapse into one pool.

The surviving pool's node selector and driver image tag use the first node's raw kernel. The other nodes get no driver DaemonSet. The NVIDIADriver can still become Ready.

This was found by reading `internal/state/nodepool.go` on main (operator v26.7.2). It is not a live cluster repro.

## To reproduce

From the code path. `TestGetSanitizedKernelVersion` already expects these two strings to become `5.14.0-427.37.1.el9.4`:

- `5.14.0-427.37.1.el9_4.x86_64`
- `5.14.0-427.37.1.el9_4.aarch64`

Put one GPU node on each kernel, with the same OS, under one NVIDIADriver that sets `usePrecompiled: true`.

On current main, `getNodePools` returns one pool. The unit test is:

```
go test -count=1 -run TestGetNodePoolsKeepsPrecompiledKernelsThatSanitizeTogether ./internal/state/
```

That test fails with 1 pool instead of 2.

## Expected behavior

One pool per raw kernel. Nodes with the same raw kernel still share a pool. The sanitized name can stay shared. The selector and the image tag for each pool must keep that pool's own raw kernel.

I will open a pull request with that change.

title: Keep separate precompiled pools when kernel names match
body:
## Description

Precompiled node pools were keyed on the sanitized kernel name. That name drops `x86_64`, `aarch64`, and `_64k`, so two kernels that differ only by architecture or page size became one pool. The map key now includes the raw `feature.node.kubernetes.io/kernel-version.full`. Nodes with the same raw kernel still share one pool. The sanitized name is unchanged, and equal names sort by the raw kernel.

title: Filter DaemonSet watch updates to readiness changes
body: ## Description The ClusterPolicy and GPUCluster controllers watch their DaemonSets without a predicate. Every status update enqueues a full reconcile. During a rollout the DaemonSet controller rewrites the status once per pod. On a large cluster this means thousands of reconciles that all compute the same result. This change adds a predicate to both watches. An update is reconciled when the generation, labels, annotations, or deletion state change. It is also reconciled when one of the seven status comparisons the reconcilers read changes: - `desiredIsZero`: DesiredNumberScheduled == 0 - `currentIsZero`: CurrentNumberScheduled == 0 - `unavailableIsZero`: NumberUnavailable == 0 - `misscheduledIsZero`: NumberMisscheduled == 0 - `allUpdated`: UpdatedNumberScheduled == DesiredNumberScheduled - `allAvailable`: NumberAvailable == DesiredNumberScheduled - `generationObserved`: ObservedGeneration >= Generation The predicate does not ask whether a comparison is true or false. It asks only whether the comparison changed between the old and the new object. **If none of the seven changed, the reconciler would reach the same result as last time, so the update is dropped.** ### Example A 10-node DaemonSet in the middle of a rollout: 6 pods available, 4 unavailable. `unavailableIsZero` is false and `allAvailable` is false. One more pod becomes ready: 7 available, 3 unavailable. `unavailableIsZero` is still false. `allAvailable` is still false. Nothing changed. The update is dropped. The last pod becomes ready: 10 available, 0 unavailable. `unavailableIsZero` becomes true. `allAvailable` becomes true. The update is reconciled, and the reconciler moves the operand from NotReady to Ready. ### Why this is low risk The predicate changes when the reconciler runs, not what it computes. Both reconcilers requeue after 5 seconds while any operand is not ready. The GPUCluster reconciler also resyncs every minute while ready. If the predicate ever drops an update that mattered, the next poll picks it up. Create, delete, and generic events are always reconciled. The NVIDIADriver controller's DaemonSet watch is not changed in this PR. ## Checklist - [x] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes - [x] Lint checks passing (`make lint`) - [x] Generated assets in-sync (`make validate-generated-assets`) - [x] Go mod artifacts in-sync (`make validate-modules`) - [x] Test cases are added for new code paths ## Testing Unit tests in `internal/state/daemonset_predicate_test.go`. One table test covers sixteen old-and-new pairs: each of the seven comparisons flipping, generation, label, annotation, and deletion changes, and the no-op cases above. One test covers the create, delete, and generic paths. `go test ./internal/state/ ./controllers/` and `go vet` pass. ### Measured effect Test setup: a kind cluster with 200 kwok fake GPU nodes and all the operands. Each measurement sets 50 of the 200 device-plugin pods NotReady in place and lets them return to Ready 2 to 12 seconds later, which is what a container restart on real nodes looks like to the DaemonSet controller. This produces about 100 DaemonSet status updates. Only two of them change a readiness comparison: the first pod going NotReady and the last pod going Ready. The rest change pod counts only. ClusterPolicy reconciles were counted from `controller_runtime_reconcile_total` during the recovery. | | DaemonSet status updates | ClusterPolicy reconciles | Operator CPU seconds | API requests from the operator | |---|---|---|---|---| | Before (main at 05555342e) | 100 | 47 | 1.9 | 7,200 | | After (this PR on the same commit) | 100 | 6 | 0.5 | 1,000 | | Change | | **-87%** | **-75%** | **-86%** | Values are the mean of three measurement runs. Before: 49, 46, 47 reconciles. After: 6, 6, 7. The remaining reconciles after the change are the two readiness-change events plus the 5-second requeue while the ClusterPolicy is not ready. CPU seconds are `process_cpu_seconds_total` and API requests are `rest_client_requests_total`, both from the operator's metrics endpoint over the ~70-second measurement window. The predicate does not make a reconcile cheaper. Each reconcile still costs about 150 API requests (about 45 PUT, 45 POST, and 60 DELETE) on both builds. It removes reconciles that would have produced the same result as the previous one. Note: 100 DaemonSet status updates do not produce 100 reconciles before the change, because a reconcile takes several seconds and the work queue merges updates that arrive while a reconcile runs. The measurement covers the ClusterPolicy path only. The GPUCluster controller uses the same predicate and the same 5-second requeue while operands are not ready, so the same reduction in reconciles per status update applies to it. ---

title: fix: allow enabling/disabling host subscriptions for driver pod
body: ## Summary Alternative implementation. Fixes #2817 by making host subscription mounts independent of custom repository configuration. Previously, configuring `driver.repoConfig` implicitly disabled RHEL host subscription mounts. This prevented driver installations that require both host subscription repositories and additional custom repositories. ## Changes Add `driver.hostSubscription.enabled` to Helm, ClusterPolicy, and NVIDIADriver: | Configuration | Behavior | |---|---| | Omitted | Preserve automatic mounts for eligible OS/runtime combinations | | `true` | Mount standard subscription paths, retaining eligibility checks | | `false` | Skip host subscription mounts | Use a pointer boolean to distinguish omitted values from explicit `false`. Custom repositories no longer implicitly disable subscriptions. The `hostSubscription` object also leaves room for future configuration, such as custom subscription paths. title: dcgm-exporter: support DCGM 4.7 metric names for dcgm-exporter 4.9.0
body: ## Description **Ready for review. Can merge now.** This PR does not change image pins. It works with the DCGM Exporter and DCGM the Operator ships today, and with newer DCGM Exporter releases that users set through `dcgmExporter.version` and `dcgm.version`. Newer DCGM Exporter releases rename their default metrics to DCGM 4.7 field names and deprecate `dcp-metrics-included.csv`. This PR makes the Operator work with both the current and the newer releases: - **Default metrics file:** `/etc/dcgm-exporter/default-counters.csv` instead of `dcp-metrics-included.csv`. Both files list the same metrics in 4.8.4 and 4.9.0, so the default metric set does not change. - **OpenShift `accelerator_*` recording rules:** read the new metric name, convert it back to the unit the series already reports, and fall back to the old name (`new converted or old`). Recorded names, labels, and values are unchanged with either exporter version, so existing dashboards and alerts keep working. Some series names say bytes or hertz but report percent, MiB, or MHz; this PR keeps those units rather than change values under existing consumers. - **Startup probe:** on `/health`, every 5 s for up to 5 minutes, for both dcgm-exporter DaemonSets. On a node with many GPUs and a large metric file, the exporter can take about 60 s to answer, which is the current liveness limit. The liveness and readiness probes start once it succeeds, so their 45 s initial delays are removed; a fast start now becomes ready sooner. DCGM Exporter's own Helm chart adds the same probe in 4.9.0. - **Renovate:** updates the `dcgm` and `dcgm-exporter` images in one PR. ### Upgrade and rollback DCGM Exporter 4.9.0 needs a DCGM 4.7 or later host engine, so the `dcgm` and `dcgmExporter` images must move together. Renovate opens that pin update when the images are published; it is a separate change. - With a standalone DCGM 4.6.x host engine (`dcgm.enabled: true`, the OpenShift default, or a GPUCluster with standalone DCGM), exporter 4.9.0 exits at startup with an error that lists the fields the host engine refuses. Embedded mode is not affected. - During the upgrade, a node's exporter can restart a few times until that node's DCGM pod runs 4.7. - To roll back, roll back both images together. An older Operator's rules read only the old metric names, so `accelerator_*` series are empty while nodes run exporter 4.9.0. ## Checklist - [x] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes - [x] Lint checks passing (`make lint`) - [x] Generated assets in-sync (`make validate-generated-assets`) - [x] Go mod artifacts in-sync (`make validate-modules`) - [x] Test cases are added for new code paths ## Testing - `make fmt`, `make lint`, `make unit-test`, `helm lint deployments/gpu-operator`, `make validate-modules` and `make validate-generated-assets` pass. - `go test ./internal/state/...` passes with the updated golden files; `TestDCGMExporter` checks the startup probe and that the liveness and readiness probes have no initial delay. - `renovate-config-validator .github/renovate.json` passes. - After rebasing onto current `main`: `go build ./...`, and `go test ./internal/state/ ./controllers/` pass again. - DCGM Exporter 4.9.0, run with the environment the Operator sets (default, remote host engine, DRA, HPC, pod labels, custom metrics ConfigMap), passes `config validate`. Against a DCGM 4.7.0 host engine it serves all 7 rule source metrics; against DCGM 4.6.1 it exits at startup as described above. - Not run: `make validate-csv`, `make validate-helm-values` (no pin change), e2e, and a real OpenShift cluster. --- - The recording rules were checked locally with `promtool test rules` (4.8.x names, 4.9.0 names giving the same values, a mixed fleet, a GPU reporting both); that test is not part of this PR.

title: Fix E2E failures

It then sees the new readiness marker through its separate validations mount while continuing to load NVML from the old filesystem, leaving toolkit in init and blocking the other operands. Keep host and container paths separate, including custom driver directories and host-installed drivers. title: NVIDIADriver rejects `kernelModuleType: auto` with GDS enabled, blocking driver deployment
body:
### Description

In GPU Operator v26.7.2, switching from ClusterPolicy driver management to NVIDIADriver management with unchanged driver settings fails when:

- `driver.kernelModuleType=auto`
- GDS is enabled with version `2.29.4`

The NVIDIADriver controller requires the configured kernel module type to be explicitly `open`. It rejects `auto` before the driver container can resolve the appropriate module type.

The same settings work through the ClusterPolicy driver path.

### Environment

- GPU Operator: v26.7.2
- NVIDIA driver: 595.91.07
- Kernel module type: auto
- GDS: 2.29.4
- GDRCopy: v2.6
- RDMA: disabled
- Installation method: OCI Helm chart

### Steps to reproduce

Use a GPU test cluster without an existing GPU Operator installation.

#### 1. Create shared values

```bash
cat > gpu-operator-repro.yaml <<'EOF'
driver:
  enabled: true
  repository: nvcr.io/nvidia
  image: driver
  version: "595.91.07"
  kernelModuleType: auto
  usePrecompiled: false
  rdma:
    enabled: false
    useHostMofed: false

gds:
  enabled: true
  repository: nvcr.io/nvidia/cloud-native
  image: nvidia-fs
  version: "2.29.4"

gdrcopy:
  enabled: true
  repository: nvcr.io/nvidia/cloud-native
  image: gdrdrv
  version: "v2.6"
EOF
```

RDMA is disabled to avoid introducing a MOFED dependency into this reproduction.

#### 2. Install v26.7.2 with ClusterPolicy driver management

```bash
helm install gpu-operator \
  oci://nvcr.io/nvidia/cloud-native-charts/gpu-operator \
  --version v26.7.2 \
  --namespace gpu-operator \
  --create-namespace \
  --values gpu-operator-repro.yaml \
  --set driver.nvidiaDriverCRD.enabled=false \
  --wait \
  --timeout 30m
```

Verify the baseline is ready:

```bash
kubectl wait --for=jsonpath='{.status.state}'=ready \
  clusterpolicy/cluster-policy \
  --timeout=30m

kubectl get clusterpolicy
kubectl get pods -n gpu-operator
kubectl get ds -n gpu-operator
```

#### 3. Upgrade to the same version with NVIDIADriver management enabled

Keep the same values and enable creation of the default NVIDIADriver:

```bash
helm upgrade gpu-operator \
  oci://nvcr.io/nvidia/cloud-native-charts/gpu-operator \
  --version v26.7.2 \
  --namespace gpu-operator \
  --values gpu-operator-repro.yaml \
  --set driver.nvidiaDriverCRD.enabled=true \
  --set driver.nvidiaDriverCRD.deployDefaultCR=true \
  --wait \
  --timeout 30m
```

#### 4. Inspect the resulting state

```bash
kubectl get nvidiadriver default -o yaml
kubectl get pods -n gpu-operator
kubectl get ds -n gpu-operator
```

### Actual behavior

The default NVIDIADriver remains `notReady`:

```yaml
status:
  conditions:
  - message: ""
    reason: Error
    status: "False"
    type: Ready
  - message: >-
      GPUDirect Storage driver '2.29.4' is only supported with NVIDIA
      OpenRM drivers. Please set 'useOpenKernelModules=true' to enable
      OpenRM mode
    reason: ReconcileFailed
    status: "True"
    type: Error
  state: notReady
```

In the reproduction cluster, after the upgrade:

- No NVIDIA driver DaemonSet exists.
- No NVIDIA driver pod exists.
- Other operands, including the container toolkit, device plugin, GPU feature discovery, DCGM exporter, and operator validator, remain running.

### Expected behavior

`kernelModuleType: auto` should be handled consistently between the ClusterPolicy and NVIDIADriver driver paths.

When automatic selection resolves to open kernel modules, enabling GDS should not cause the NVIDIADriver controller to reject the configuration before driver deployment.

If explicit `open` is intentionally required for this configuration, that restriction should be documented and the error should reference `kernelModuleType: open`, rather than the deprecated `useOpenKernelModules` field.

### Code analysis

All references below are permanent links to commit
`5a9c8a8b3f5bac7fb06ad3c2a05771fceb8b4832`, tagged `v26.7.2`.

#### 1. The open-module helper only accepts explicit `open`

`NVIDIADriverSpec.IsOpenKernelModulesEnabled()` checks:

```go
return d.KernelModuleType == "open"
```

Consequently, it returns false for `auto`, without resolving what module type the driver container would select.

https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/5a9c8a8b3f5bac7fb06ad3c2a05771fceb8b4832/api/nvidia/v1alpha1/nvidiadriver_types.go#L718-L721

#### 2. GDS validation rejects the CR before driver resources are synchronized

The NVIDIADriver reconciler checks:

```go
if instance.Spec.IsGDSEnabled() &&
    instance.Spec.IsOpenKernelModulesRequired() &&
    !instance.Spec.IsOpenKernelModulesEnabled() {
    // Set notReady / ReconcileFailed and return.
}
```

The controller returns before reaching `r.stateManager.SyncState(...)`.

This blocks driver resource reconciliation; it is not merely a readiness reporting problem.

https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/5a9c8a8b3f5bac7fb06ad3c2a05771fceb8b4832/controllers/nvidiadriver_controller.go#L173-L200

#### 3. The ClusterPolicy driver path passes the module type to the container

The ClusterPolicy transformation sets `KERNEL_MODULE_TYPE` from the configured `kernelModuleType`, allowing `auto` to reach the driver container.

https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/5a9c8a8b3f5bac7fb06ad3c2a05771fceb8b4832/controllers/object_controls.go#L3625-L3631

#### 4. Migration removes ClusterPolicy-managed driver DaemonSets

When NVIDIADriver management is enabled, the ClusterPolicy controller cleans up its driver DaemonSets using orphan propagation, intending to preserve running pods until replacements are deployed.

https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/5a9c8a8b3f5bac7fb06ad3c2a05771fceb8b4832/controllers/state_manager.go#L958-L977

However, the NVIDIADriver validation failure blocks creation of replacement driver resources.

The observed absence of a replacement DaemonSet is therefore consistent with an early reconciliation failure, rather than a failure to assign ownership to a newly created DaemonSet.

### Impact

This blocks operator-managed driver provisioning and convergence to the desired driver configuration.

In the reproduction cluster, migration leaves no driver DaemonSet or driver pod. Other operands remain healthy, but that does not establish that driver lifecycle management is working.

In a separate observed cluster, an existing DaemonSet owned by NVIDIADriver continued running while the CR reported notReady. Therefore, the visible impact depends on existing driver resources and reconciliation history.

No immediate GPU workload outage has been established. However:

- Fresh driver deployment is blocked for this configuration.
- Driver resource updates are blocked while validation fails.
- Migration can leave the cluster without an operator-managed driver DaemonSet.
- Healthy operand pods can obscure the incomplete driver deployment.

### Workaround

Use explicit `driver.kernelModuleType=open`, retaining the other settings:

```bash
helm upgrade gpu-operator \
  oci://nvcr.io/nvidia/cloud-native-charts/gpu-operator \
  --version v26.7.2 \
  --namespace gpu-operator \
  --values gpu-operator-repro.yaml \
  --set driver.nvidiaDriverCRD.enabled=true \
  --set driver.nvidiaDriverCRD.deployDefaultCR=true \
  --set driver.kernelModuleType=open \
  --wait \
  --timeout 30m
```

This satisfies the explicit-open validation check. Successful rollout of the workaround has not yet been confirmed in this reproduction.

title: [Bug]: ClusterPolicy precompiled DaemonSets collapse kernels that differ only by arch
body:
**Describe the bug**

With `driver.usePrecompiled=true` on a ClusterPolicy, `precompiledDriverDaemonsets` walks every raw `feature.node.kubernetes.io/kernel-version.full`. The DaemonSet name is built with `getSanitizedKernelVersion`, which strips `x86_64`, `aarch64`, and `_64k`. The node selector and the image tag keep the raw kernel.

Two kernels that differ only by architecture or page size therefore share one name. `DaemonSet` updates that object, and the last loop iteration wins. The other kernel's nodes get no driver. Go map order is random, so which kernel wins can change on the next reconcile.

This is the ClusterPolicy driver path. `driver.nvidiaDriverCRD.enabled` defaults to false. Pull request #3099 changes `internal/state/nodepool.go` only.

**To Reproduce**

The inputs are the ones `TestGetSanitizedKernelVersion` already treats as equal:

- `5.14.0-427.37.1.el9_4.x86_64`
- `5.14.0-427.37.1.el9_4.aarch64`

Those strings are the shape of a RHEL `uname -r`, which is what Node Feature Discovery stores in `feature.node.kubernetes.io/kernel-version.full`.

On current main, one reconcile creates `nvidia-driver-daemonset-5.14.0-427.37.1.el9.4-ubuntu22.04` for the first kernel and then updates that same object for the second kernel. The log line is `DaemonSet is different, updating`, and one DaemonSet remains. Its node selector and image are the second kernel.

The regression test is `TestPrecompiledDriverDaemonSetsStayDistinctWhenKernelsSanitizeTogether`. It drives `ClusterPolicyController.step()` with `usePrecompiled: true` and those two node labels. On main it fails with 1 DaemonSet instead of 2.

This is a controller test, not a live cluster capture.

**Expected behavior**

One DaemonSet per raw kernel. Each object keeps that kernel in its node selector and in the precompiled image tag. Kernels that do not sanitize together, such as `5.4.0-generic` and `5.4.135-generic`, keep the names they have today.

**Environment (please provide the following information):**
 - GPU Operator Version: main (controller unit test)
 - OS: any OS whose NFD kernel label includes the architecture, for example RHEL `5.14.0-427.37.1.el9_4.x86_64`
 - Kernel Version: two kernels that differ only by `.x86_64` / `.aarch64` or `_64k`
 - Container Runtime Version: n/a
 - Kubernetes Distro and Version: n/a

title: Keep separate precompiled drivers when kernel names match
body: ## Description `driver.usePrecompiled=true` on a ClusterPolicy builds the driver DaemonSet name with `getSanitizedKernelVersion`. That helper strips `x86_64`, `aarch64`, and `_64k`. The node selector and the precompiled image tag still use the raw `feature.node.kubernetes.io/kernel-version.full`. Two kernels that differ only by architecture or page size share one name. `DaemonSet` updates that object, and the last loop iteration wins. The other kernel's nodes get no driver. Map iteration order is not stable, so the surviving selector can change on the next reconcile. This pull covers both paths. On a ClusterPolicy, `driver.nvidiaDriverCRD.enabled` defaults to false, so `driver.usePrecompiled=true` builds these DaemonSets. The name keeps the architecture and page-size tokens. `_` is rewritten to `.`. A kernel that contains `_` also gets a short hash of the raw string, so `x86_64` and `x86.64` do not share a name. Kernels with no `_`, such as `5.4.0-generic`, keep the previous name. After the new objects are created, a stale precompiled DaemonSet in the operator namespace is deleted. A DaemonSet in another namespace is left alone. One failed delete does not skip the rest. NVIDIADriver pools in `internal/state/nodepool.go` (the change from #3099) key each pool on the raw kernel as well as the sanitized name. Nodes with the same raw kernel still share one pool. This change does not touch API types or modules. ## Testing Red, before the name change, on the real `ClusterPolicyController.step()` path: ``` go test -count=1 -timeout 180s -run TestPrecompiledDriverDaemonSetsStayDistinctWhenKernelsSanitizeTogether ./controllers/ ``` The controller created `nvidia-driver-daemonset-5.14.0-427.37.1.el9.4-ubuntu22.04` for `5.14.0-427.37.1.el9_4.x86_64`, then logged `DaemonSet is different, updating` for `5.14.0-427.37.1.el9_4.aarch64` against that same name. title: Prevent upgrade controller from reading ClusterPolicy controller globals
body: ## Description Fixes #3061. Depends on: https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-operator-libs/pull/166. There was a chance the upgrade controller could read the ClusterPolicy controller's state while it was actively being edited. That caused a data race, and on OpenShift with DTK it could search by the wrong label at startup. At startup it could also read that state before it was set, so on OpenShift with DTK it searched by the wrong label. It now always uses app.kubernetes.io/component=nvidia-driver, which every driver pod has, so it no longer reads that state. `NVIDIADriver`-owned DaemonSets are filtered out by passing in `isOwnedByNVIDIADriver` as a `BuildState` ownership filter introduced in `k8s-operator-libs` [#166](https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-operator-libs/pull/166). Note: This fix was tried before, in bd806dd2d, and reverted in 96a20af5c before v23.9.0 shipped. The component label `app.kubernetes.io/component=nvidia-driver` was added in the same release cycle, so every cluster upgrading to v23.9.0 had driver pods created by an older operator, and none of them had the label. Driver pods are OnDelete, so they only get new labels when they're deleted and recreated. With no labeled pods, BuildState couldn't find them and upgrades would have stalled, which is why it was reverted. That's no longer a concern because every driver pod created since v23.9.0 (Oct 2023) has the label, and auto-upgrade has since replaced the older pods. ## Checklist - [x] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes - [x] Lint checks passing (`make lint`) - [x] Generated assets in-sync (`make validate-generated-assets`) - [x] Go mod artifacts in-sync (`make validate-modules`) - [x] Test cases are added for new code paths ## Testing Unit tests added that - Check that the ClusterPolicy upgrade path always selects driver pods by `app.kubernetes.io/component=nvidia-driver`, whatever `clusterPolicyCtrl` holds: before the first ClusterPolicy reconcile, on OpenShift with DTK, and on OpenShift without DTK. - Check that the OpenShift Driver Toolkit transform renames the `app` label but keeps the component label on both the DaemonSet and its pod template, which the new selector depends on. - Check that the ClusterPolicy upgrade path drops nodes whose driver DaemonSet is owned by an NVIDIADriver, keeping ClusterPolicy-owned and orphaned driver pods, so leftover NVIDIADriver pods aren't upgraded by ClusterPolicy. ---
