title: [gpu-op] NVIDIADriver ignores spec.gds.imagePullPolicy
body:
NVIDIADriver accepts `spec.gds.imagePullPolicy`, but the rendered GDS container (`nvidia-fs-ctr`) always uses `IfNotPresent`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a NVIDIADriver with GDS enabled and a non-default image pull policy:

   ```yaml
   spec:
     gds:
       enabled: true
       repository: nvcr.io/nvidia/cloud-native
       image: nvidia-fs
       version: "2.29.4"
       imagePullPolicy: Always
   ```

2. Inspect the generated driver DaemonSet's `nvidia-fs-ctr` container.

### Expected behavior

The container uses the configured policy:

```yaml
imagePullPolicy: Always
```

### Actual behavior

The container uses:

```yaml
imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```

The [NVIDIADriver DaemonSet template hardcodes this value](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/6532a331b5907ecd6a99c3714ef2b922427a6888/manifests/state-driver/0500_daemonset.yaml#L452-L455).

This also affects `imagePullPolicy: Never`. The requested policy is silently ignored, potentially changing registry access and cached-image behavior when containers start.

### Verification

Verified through manifest rendering against main at `6532a331b5907ecd6a99c3714ef2b922427a6888`:

| Configured policy | Rendered GDS policy |
|---|---|
| Omitted | `IfNotPresent` |
| `IfNotPresent` | `IfNotPresent` |
| `Always` | `IfNotPresent` |
| `Never` | `IfNotPresent` |

Controls confirmed that:

- The equivalent GDS configuration through ClusterPolicy preserves `Always` and `Never`.
- NVIDIADriver's GDRCopy container preserves its configured image pull policy.

### Suggested fix

Render `spec.gds.imagePullPolicy` for the GDS container, retaining `IfNotPresent` when the setting is omitted.

Add regression coverage for omitted, `IfNotPresent`, `Always`, and `Never` values.

title: [gpu-op] Adopt semantic version image tags for DCGM Exporter
body:
GPU Operator currently references DCGM Exporter images using the legacy combined tag format:

```text
<dcgm-version>-<exporter-version>-distroless
```

Upstream now publishes exporter-only semantic version tags, such as `4.9.0`.

In [this review comment on PR #3163](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/pull/3163#discussion_r4495694087), the DCGM Exporter maintainer recommends switching to `X.Y.Z` tags and notes that publishing both formats will not continue indefinitely.

### Proposed enhancement

Migrate GPU Operator's default DCGM Exporter image references and dependency-update configuration to the upstream semantic version tag format.

For example:

```text
4.7.0-4.9.0-distroless → 4.9.0
```

### Scope

- Update the default image tag in the Helm chart.
- Update the OLM bundle image references, related images, and corresponding digests.
- Update relevant examples and validation fixtures.
- Update Renovate's DCGM Exporter versioning rule, which currently matches the legacy combined format and derives the version from its DCGM prefix.
- Preserve coordinated DCGM/DCGM Exporter updates and verify compatibility using the exporter release's bundled DCGM version.

### Acceptance criteria

- Default DCGM Exporter references use a supported `X.Y.Z` image tag.
- Renovate recognizes and orders updates by the exporter version.
- Helm and OLM references remain consistent, with verified image digests.
- The selected image supports the required architectures and passes the existing image and manifest validation checks.

This is a migration of the default tag format; user-provided image tags should remain supported.

title: [gpu-op] GPUCluster does not propagate image pull secrets to ComputeDomain daemons
body:
GPUCluster applies `spec.draDriver.imagePullSecrets` to the DRA kubelet-plugin and ComputeDomain controller pods, but does not forward those secrets to the ComputeDomain daemon pods created by the controller.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure GPUCluster to use a DRA image in a private registry, enable ComputeDomains, and specify the registry credentials:

   ```yaml
   spec:
     draDriver:
       repository: private-registry.example.com/nvidia
       image: dra-driver-nvidia-gpu
       version: v0.5.1
       imagePullSecrets:
         - registry-secret
       computeDomains:
         enabled: true
   ```

2. Ensure the Secret exists in the GPU Operator namespace.
3. Create a ComputeDomain workload that causes the controller to create ComputeDomain daemon pods.

### Expected behavior

The generated ComputeDomain daemon pods receive the configured image pull secrets and can pull the private DRA image.

### Actual behavior

The ComputeDomain controller Pod receives `imagePullSecrets`, but its container is not configured with `CD_DAEMON_IMAGE_PULL_SECRET_NAMES`. Consequently, the controller does not propagate those credentials to the daemon pods it creates.

Without another source of registry credentials, the generated daemon pods can fail with image pull authentication errors even though the controller itself starts successfully.

### Verification

Inspected main at `6532a331b5907ecd6a99c3714ef2b922427a6888`:

- Rendering with two configured pull secrets preserves both in the controller Pod's `imagePullSecrets`.
- The controller container's environment omits `CD_DAEMON_IMAGE_PULL_SECRET_NAMES`.
- Upstream DRA driver v0.5.1 reads that environment variable and forwards the names into its dynamically generated daemon Pod specs.

This was verified through manifest rendering and upstream source inspection, without a live private-registry deployment. Node credentials, ServiceAccount defaults, admission injection, or cached images may mask the issue.

### Related upstream implementation

Upstream DRA driver v0.5.1 already forwards chart image pull secrets through this environment variable:

- [Upstream controller Helm template](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu/blob/v0.5.1/deployments/helm/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu/templates/controller.yaml#L89-L94)
- [Upstream controller configuration](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu/blob/v0.5.1/cmd/compute-domain-controller/main.go#L131-L136)

GPU Operator's corresponding template does not include it:

- [GPU Operator ComputeDomain controller template](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/6532a331b5907ecd6a99c3714ef2b922427a6888/manifests/state-dra-driver/0600_controller-deployment.yaml#L109-L112)

### Suggested fix

When `spec.draDriver.imagePullSecrets` is configured, render `CD_DAEMON_IMAGE_PULL_SECRET_NAMES` in the ComputeDomain controller container with the comma-separated Secret names.

Add regression coverage for multiple configured secrets and for an empty secret list.

title: [gpu-op] GPUCluster silently ignores daemonsets.podSecurityContext
body:
GPUCluster accepts `spec.daemonsets.podSecurityContext`, but does not propagate it to the Pod specs of its DRA driver, DCGM, DCGM exporter, or validator DaemonSets.

For example:

~~~yaml
spec:
  daemonsets:
    podSecurityContext:
      seLinuxOptions:
        type: spc_t
        level: s0
~~~

### Expected behavior

The configured context appears under `spec.template.spec.securityContext` in the managed DaemonSets, while preserving required container-level settings such as `privileged: true` and explicit `runAsUser` values.

### Actual behavior

All four GPUCluster DaemonSet templates omit the pod security context. The configuration is accepted but silently has no effect. The equivalent configuration is honored through ClusterPolicy.

### Verification

Verified against main at `9339140ceff2b60ca6f2c8e56d15d253044c30f4`:

- Rendering each of the four GPUCluster DaemonSets drops the supplied context.
- A ClusterPolicy control preserves it.
- Rendering the upstream DRA driver v0.5.1 chart preserves the supplied context.

Runtime impact depends on the cluster’s security configuration; these checks establish the configuration omission.

### Related implementations

GPU Operator added pod security context support for ClusterPolicy DaemonSets and NVIDIADriver in [PR #2120](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/pull/2120). Later, [PR #2703](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/pull/2703) fixed forwarding `daemonsets.podSecurityContext` from Helm values into ClusterPolicy.

Upstream DRA driver v0.5.1 also supports this configuration:

- [Kubelet-plugin DaemonSet template](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu/blob/v0.5.1/deployments/helm/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu/templates/kubeletplugin.yaml#L53-L54) renders `kubeletPlugin.podSecurityContext`.
- [Controller Deployment template](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu/blob/v0.5.1/deployments/helm/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu/templates/controller.yaml#L48-L49) renders its separate `controller.podSecurityContext`.

### Suggested fix

Render the common pod security context into the four GPUCluster DaemonSets and add regression coverage confirming that pod settings and required container-level security settings are both preserved.

title: [gpu-op] Dotted ConfigMap names generate invalid driver volumes in ClusterPolicy and NVIDIADriver
body:
### Describe the bug

Driver configuration referencing a ConfigMap whose name contains dots produces an invalid driver DaemonSet in both the ClusterPolicy and NVIDIADriver paths.

ConfigMap names follow DNS subdomain naming rules, which allow dots. However, the operator copies the ConfigMap name directly into Pod volume names and corresponding volume mounts. Volume names follow DNS label rules and cannot contain dots.

Affected settings, verified independently in both paths:
- repoConfig
- certConfig
- kernelModuleConfig

### To reproduce

Create a ConfigMap in the GPU Operator namespace:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: driver.config
data:
  custom.list: |
    # Custom repository configuration
```

Reference it using either configuration below.

For an otherwise valid ClusterPolicy:

```yaml
spec:
  driver:
    repoConfig:
      configMapName: driver.config
```

For an otherwise valid NVIDIADriver:

```yaml
spec:
  repoConfig:
    name: driver.config
```

The resulting driver DaemonSet includes:

```yaml
volumes:
  - name: driver.config
    configMap:
      name: driver.config
```

The generated volume name violates Kubernetes naming rules, making the DaemonSet Pod template invalid.

### Expected behavior

Generate a valid, deterministic volume name and use it consistently in volume mounts. Preserve the original ConfigMap name in `configMap.name`.

### Code locations

Both files contain `createConfigMapVolumeMounts` and `createConfigMapVolume` helpers that use the ConfigMap name directly:

- `controllers/object_controls.go` — ClusterPolicy path
- `internal/state/driver.go` — NVIDIADriver path

title: [gpu-op] Skip E2E tests for documentation-only and repository maintenance changes
body:
## Description

### Problem

The CI workflow currently builds images and invokes the E2E suites without considering which files changed. Documentation-only changes and edits to `.github/renovate.json` therefore trigger GPU infrastructure provisioning and E2E testing even though they do not change operator behavior.

Skipping these unnecessary runs would reduce infrastructure usage and contributor wait times.

### Proposed improvement

Add a change-detection job and conditionally skip E2E tests when **all changed files** belong to an explicitly approved list of documentation or repository maintenance paths.

Initial candidates include:

- `docs/**`
- Explicitly selected README and contributor documentation files
- `.github/renovate.json`

Continue running relevant lightweight checks, including configuration validation.

A Renovate configuration change should be distinguished from a Renovate-generated dependency update. Updates to Go dependencies, operand images, Helm dependencies, or other runtime components should retain E2E coverage.

### Implementation considerations

- Apply filtering to `pull-request/<number>` branches initially. Preserve existing behavior for `main`, release branches, manual runs, and scheduled forward-compatibility testing.
- Evaluate the complete PR diff against its target branch, rather than only the latest commit or push. A documentation commit following a code change must not cause E2E tests to be skipped.
- Run E2E tests for mixed changes, unknown paths, or when the comparison base cannot be determined.
- Account for both old and new paths when evaluating renames.
- Use job-level conditions and preserve a reliable required-check result. Workflow-level path filtering can leave required checks pending.
- Ensure the final check distinguishes an intentional skip from an E2E failure, cancellation, or unexpected skip.
- Keep the existing release dependency on successful E2E testing intact.

### Acceptance criteria

- Documentation-only and approved repository maintenance changes skip E2E tests.
- Mixed documentation and runtime changes run E2E tests.
- Dependency, operand image, deployment, build, and relevant CI changes retain E2E coverage.
- The workflow summary explains why E2E tests ran or were skipped.
- Required checks complete correctly for intentional skips and report failures when required tests fail.
- Lightweight tests cover the change classifier, including renames, missing comparison bases, and code changes followed by documentation commits.

title: [gpu-op] NVIDIADriver does not schedule a retry when its secretEnv Secret is missing
body:
When a NVIDIADriver references a `secretEnv` Secret that does not exist yet, reconciliation records error conditions but returns an empty result and a nil error. No retry is scheduled, and the controller has no watch for the referenced Secret.

This can occur when GitOps creates the NVIDIADriver before another controller creates its Secret.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a NVIDIADriver with `spec.secretEnv` referencing a Secret that does not exist in the GPU Operator namespace:

   ```yaml
   spec:
     secretEnv: driver-env
   ```

2. Allow reconciliation to run and record the missing-Secret error.
3. Create the referenced Secret in the GPU Operator namespace.

### Expected behavior

The controller retries reconciliation and proceeds once the Secret exists, without requiring an unrelated event.

While the dependency is missing, `status.state` should be `notReady`, consistent with the error conditions.

### Actual behavior

The Secret lookup failure returns:

```go
return reconcile.Result{}, nil
```

Creating the Secret alone does not enqueue the NVIDIADriver. Recovery depends on another qualifying event, such as a driver spec change, a relevant node-label change, or an operator restart.

Additionally, if the driver was previously ready, this branch can leave contradictory status:

```yaml
status:
  state: ready
  conditions:
    - type: Ready
      status: "False"
    - type: Error
      status: "True"
      reason: ReconcileFailed
```

### Verification

Verified against main at `9339140ceff2b60ca6f2c8e56d15d253044c30f4` using a focused unit test:

- A missing Secret returns a nil error, `Requeue=false`, and `RequeueAfter=0`.
- A previously ready driver retains `status.state=ready` while its conditions report an error.
- An existing-Secret control proceeds to state synchronization normally.

[Relevant Secret lookup and error handling](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/blob/9339140ceff2b60ca6f2c8e56d15d253044c30f4/controllers/nvidiadriver_controller.go#L183-L195)

### Suggested fix

Set the driver's state to `notReady` and return the Secret lookup error so the controller's configured retry backoff applies.

Alternatively, handle `NotFound` with a bounded `RequeueAfter` and return other lookup errors normally. A watch for referenced Secrets could provide faster recovery but is not required for a minimal fix.

title: [gpu-op] Align `Age` column across all CRs
body:
The ClusterPolicy and NVIDIADriver CRs use `type=string` for the `Age` column. The GPUCluster CR uses `type=date`. We should use `type=date` for all CRs as that is consistent with built-in resources like Pods, Deployments, etc.

Below is sample output that shows the current `Age` column for all CRs.
```
# kubectl get clusterpolicy
NAME             STATUS   AGE
cluster-policy   ready    2026-10-26T18:21:00Z
```

```
# kubectl get nvd
NAME      STATUS   DEFAULT   AGE
default   ready    true      2026-11-06T03:30:01Z
```

```
# kubectl get gpucluster
NAME          STATUS   AGE
gpu-cluster   ready    7m26s
```

**Fix:** Change all CRs to `type=date`, then run `make manifests` and `make sync-crds`.
**Done when:** The CRDs are regenerated in `config/crd/bases`, `deployments/gpu-operator/crds`, and `bundle/manifests`, and `kubectl get` shows a relative age

title: Remove duplicated getRuntimeString helper
body: Fixes #3212 `controllers/state_manager.go` and `controllers/clusterinfo/clusterinfo.go` each defined their own `getRuntimeString` mapping a node's `ContainerRuntimeVersion` prefix to a runtime (`docker`/`cri-o`/`containerd`). The two copies return identical values (`consts` strings vs `gpuv1.Runtime` constants hold the same `"docker"`/`"crio"`/`"containerd"` values). This exports the `clusterinfo` copy as `GetRuntimeString`, deletes the `state_manager` copy and its duplicate test, and calls the shared helper from `state_manager` with a `gpuv1.Runtime(...)` conversion at the call site. No behavior change. ---

title: Honor explicit nlsEnabled=false in NVIDIADriver helm template
body: ## Issue Fixes #3211 ## Description `templates/nvidiadriver.yaml` rendered `licensingConfig.nlsEnabled` with `| default true`. Sprig's `default` treats `false` as empty, so an explicit `driver.licensingConfig.nlsEnabled=false` was always rendered as `true`. This updates both the `secretName` and `configMapName` branches to render explicit booleans directly via `kindIs "bool"` while retaining `| default true` for non-boolean values. Explicit `false`/`true` booleans and legacy string overrides (e.g. `--set-string driver.licensingConfig.nlsEnabled=false`) are preserved, while unset, `null`, and empty-string overrides (e.g. `--set-string driver.licensingConfig.nlsEnabled=`) continue to fall back to `true`. ## Checklist - [x] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes - [x] Lint checks passing (`make lint`) - [x] Generated assets in-sync (`make validate-generated-assets`) - [x] Go mod artifacts in-sync (`make validate-modules`) - [x] Test cases are added for new code paths ## Testing Added `TestNVIDIADriverLicensingConfig` in `deployments/gpu-operator/chart_test.go` covering both `secretName` and `configMapName` branches with: - explicit `false` -> `false` - explicit `true` -> `true` - `--set-string driver.licensingConfig.nlsEnabled=false` -> `false` - unset / `null` / `""` / `--set-string driver.licensingConfig.nlsEnabled=` -> `true` Verified locally: - `helm lint deployments/gpu-operator/` - `go test -race -v ./deployments/gpu-operator/...` - `golangci-lint run ./deployments/gpu-operator/...` - `make fmt` and `make license-check` ---

title: Read driver upgrade state from the manager cache
body: ## Issue None. ## Description The upgrade state manager reads the driver DaemonSets, the driver Pods, and every node with a driver pod from the API server on every pass, also when no upgrade is in progress. Pass the manager's client to `NewClusterUpgradeStateManager` so that it reads these objects from the cache. The Node cache transform now keeps `spec.unschedulable` and the `Ready` condition, which the upgrade library reads to count unavailable nodes and to uncordon. Companion to NVIDIA/k8s-operator-libs#164, which adds a client parameter to `NewClusterUpgradeStateManager`. This PR vendors that change as `v0.0.0-20261125224746-ff50b2aeb6d0` and must move to a library release before it merges. The vendor update also brings in the k8s-operator-libs commits merged since the current version. One of them adds a `filters` parameter to `BuildState`, so the test fake in `upgrade_controller_test.go` takes it too. ## Checklist - [x] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes - [x] Lint checks passing (`make lint`) — the only findings are 3 staticcheck SA4023 findings in `cmd/nvidia-validator/main.go`, which upstream main also has - [x] Generated assets in-sync (`make validate-generated-assets`) - [x] Go mod artifacts in-sync (`make validate-modules`) - [x] Test cases are added for new code paths ## Testing - `TestCache` checks that the Node transform keeps `spec.unschedulable` and the `Ready` condition. - `go test ./controllers/... ./cmd/...` passes. - Scale test with 200 fake GPU nodes (kwok), one driver upgrade per test window: Node GETs to the API server fell from 10,049 to about 470 per upgrade, and the `maxUnavailable` limit and uncordon worked as before. The full results are in NVIDIA/k8s-operator-libs#164. ---

title: Pass image pull secrets to ComputeDomain daemons

On clusters using a private registry, the daemon pods couldn't pull their image. This sets `CD_DAEMON_IMAGE_PULL_SECRET_NAMES` (comma-separated, the env var `compute-domain-controller` reads) on the controller deployment when `imagePullSecrets` is set. It's left unset otherwise. This switches the GPU Operator's defaults to the new tags: - `deployments/gpu-operator/values.yaml`: `4.7.0-4.9.0-distroless` → `4.9.0` - OLM bundle CSV: both DCGM Exporter references (`relatedImages` and `DCGM_EXPORTER_IMAGE`) now use `4.9.0` - `.github/renovate.json`: the versioning regex for `nvcr.io/nvidia/k8s/dcgm-exporter` now matches plain `X.Y.Z`. The old regex read the DCGM version as the major version, so Renovate compared the wrong number. I kept the existing digest in the CSV, since `4.9.0` should be the same image as `4.7.0-4.9.0-distroless`. Could a maintainer confirm the digest matches? title: Fix ConfigMap-derived volume names
body: ## Issue Fixes #3204 ## Description ConfigMap names may contain dots and exceed 63 characters, while Pod volume names must be DNS labels of at most 63 characters. The driver configuration helpers currently use the ConfigMap name directly for both volumes and mounts, so valid ConfigMap names such as `driver.config` produce invalid DaemonSet Pod templates. Add `ConfigMapVolumeName` and use it for `repoConfig`, `certConfig`, and `kernelModuleConfig` volumes and mounts in both the ClusterPolicy and NVIDIADriver paths: - Preserve names that already satisfy volume naming rules, avoiding unnecessary changes to existing Pod templates. - For other valid ConfigMap names, replace dots with hyphens, truncate the prefix as needed, and append a 16-character hexadecimal suffix derived from the SHA-256 hash of the full original name. The resulting volume name stays within 63 characters. - Keep `configMap.name` pointing to the original ConfigMap; mounted files and paths are unchanged. The device-plugin configuration path also uses the shared `createConfigMapVolume` helper but constructs its mounts separately. Update `addSharedMountsForPluginConfig` to use the same naming helper so its mounts continue to match the volume. Add regression tests for naming boundaries, both driver configuration paths (including NVIDIADriver template rendering), and device-plugin volume/mount matching. A generated name can still match another ConfigMap's preserved valid name. Resolving conflicts across all volumes in a Pod is outside the scope of this fix. ## Checklist - [x] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes - [x] Lint checks passing (`make lint`) - [x] Generated assets in-sync (`make validate-generated-assets`) - [x] Go mod artifacts in-sync (`make validate-modules`) - [x] Test cases are added for new code paths ## Testing Using Go 1.27.4 and golangci-lint 2.14.0: - `make fmt unit-test`: passed. - `make check`: passed, including lint, license, module, and generated-asset checks. No generated or dependency changes. No live Kubernetes/GPU cluster or end-to-end testing. ---

title: Remove no-op writes API writes from operator reconcile
body: ## Issue Fixes [#721](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cloud-native-team/issues/721) ## Description Each ClusterPolicy reconcile sends about 110-130 API write calls that change nothing. The operator writes operand objects without first checking what exists: - **POST that returns 409**. Each object function calls Create on every reconcile and uses the AlreadyExists error as the signal that the object exists (for example controllers/object_controls.go:365-373). - **PUT with no change**. When the object exists, most object functions call Update with no comparison against the live object (for example controllers/object_controls.go:401-409). Only the DaemonSet path skips the update when its hash annotation matches. - **DELETE that returns 404**. For a disabled state, each object function calls Delete on every reconcile and ignores NotFound (for example controllers/object_controls.go:352-358). This occurs on both ClusterPolicy paths and NVIDIADriver/GPUCluster paths. This PR fixes these three issues in both gpu operator "modes" by comparing against Objects stored in cache prior to updates. ### Changes **`internal/utils/sync_object.go` (new)** - `ContentEqual` reports whether a live object matches the desired one: its labels, annotations, owner references and content. It compares only kinds that the API server stores exactly as sent: RBAC objects, ConfigMap, ServiceAccount, RuntimeClass and DeviceClass. For any other kind it reports a change, so those objects are still updated every time. - `SyncObject` reads an object from the cache, creates it only when missing, deletes it only when present, and updates it only when `ContentEqual` reports a change. `SyncOptions` adds `CreateOnly`, which ServiceAccounts use, and `PreserveLiveFields`, which keeps a Service's assigned ClusterIP. **ClusterPolicy path (`controllers/object_controls.go`)** - Every control function now writes its object through `SyncObject`. DaemonSets keep their hash comparison. **NVIDIADriver and GPUCluster path (`internal/state/state_skel.go`)** - `createOrUpdateObjs` now reads before creating and skips unchanged updates with `ContentEqual`. Before comparing, it merges the live ServiceAccount secrets into the desired object, so secrets added by other controllers don't count as a change. - `getObj` reads a typed object when the scheme knows the kind. The client would otherwise send unstructured reads straight to the API server instead of the cache. The objects below are still updated on every reconcile. For these kinds, a live object never matches the rendered manifest, so a direct comparison would always report a change. Three things cause this: 1. Defaults: the API server, or a platform such as OpenShift, fills in fields that the manifest leaves empty. 2. CRDs installed by another project: the cluster's Prometheus installation can define fields and defaults that the operator's vendored types don't have. 3. Annotations from other controllers: the Deployment controller adds `deployment.kubernetes.io/revision`, for example. - `Service` - `ResourceClaimTemplate` - `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` - `ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding` - `Deployment` - `ClusterPolicy/status` - `NVIDIADriver/status` - `GPUCluster/status` ## Checklist - [x] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes - [x] Lint checks passing (`make lint`) - [x] Generated assets in-sync (`make validate-generated-assets`) - [x] Go mod artifacts in-sync (`make validate-modules`) - [x] Test cases are added for new code paths ## Testing The number of no-op API writes per ClusterPolicy reconcile remained independent of node count. In matched before/after KWOK tests at 5, 110, 500, 550, 2,470 and 2,500 simulated GPU nodes, steady-state writes decreased from 150 to 5 per reconcile (96.7%): - **POST 409**: 42 → 0 per reconcile. - **DELETE 404**: 66 → 0 per reconcile. - **Unchanged PUT**: 42 → 5 per reconcile. - **API reads**: 0 → 0 per reconcile after cache warm-up. Across three DaemonSet rollout waves per version, measured write rates were: - 5 nodes: 117.72 → 4.14 writes/s (96.5% reduction). - 110 nodes: 341.98 → 1.69 writes/s (99.5% reduction). - 500 nodes: 392.63 → 1.51 writes/s (99.6% reduction). - 550 nodes: 388.31 → 1.69 writes/s (99.6% reduction). - 2,470 nodes: 351.78 → 1.80 writes/s (99.5% reduction). - 2,500 nodes: 336.52 → 1.91 writes/s (99.4% reduction). These figures were obtained on a CPU-only cluster running KWOK. ---

title: [Bug]: Node labeling stops at the first node patch failure, skipping remaining nodes
body:
**Motivation**
While reviewing the node labeling controller for behavior at large cluster sizes (5,000+ nodes), I found that a single failing node patch stops the whole labeling pass. I found this by reading the code and confirmed it with a unit test, not from a production incident.

- [x] I would like to work on this issue.

**Describe the bug**
`labelGPUNodes` in `controllers/nodelabeling_controller.go` patches nodes in one loop and returns on the first patch error:

```go
if err := nlc.client.Patch(ctx, &node, client.MergeFrom(original)); err != nil {
    return result, fmt.Errorf("unable to label node %s: %w", node.Name, err)
}
```

When one node's patch fails:
- the remaining nodes in that pass are not labeled;
- `Reconcile` returns early, so `AssignOwners`, `labelNodesWithOrphanedDriverPods` and `applyDriverAutoUpgradeAnnotation` are skipped for all nodes;
- if the failure persists (for example, an admission webhook rejecting one node), those steps keep being skipped on every retry.

A node deleted between the List and the Patch returns `NotFound` and aborts the pass the same way.

At larger cluster sizes, the chance that at least one node is failing at any moment goes up, so one node can hold back labeling for the whole cluster.

**To Reproduce**
Unit test with the fake client: three GPU nodes (`feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-10de.present=true`), with an interceptor that makes the Patch fail for the first node. After `labelGPUNodes` runs, the other two nodes do not have `nvidia.com/gpu.present=true` (0 of 2 nodes patched).

**Expected behavior**
A patch failure on one node should not prevent the other nodes from being labeled. Errors should be collected and returned after all nodes are processed, and nodes deleted after the List (`NotFound`) should be skipped.

Proposed fix: continue the loop on a patch error, return the collected errors with `errors.Join`, and ignore `NotFound`. I have a small fix with a regression test ready and can open a PR if this approach works for you.

**Environment (please provide the following information):**
 - GPU Operator Version: `main` at commit 6094104
 - OS / Kernel / Container Runtime: N/A (reproduced with a unit test)
 - Kubernetes Distro and Version: N/A (controller-runtime fake client)

title: [Feature] Add GPU configuration manager (power limit, locked clocks, ECC mode)
body:
This issue tracks a series of patches that add an optional operand
that sets GPU power limit, locked clocks and ECC mode on each node
from a ConfigMap, and applies them again after every driver load.

## PRs

Merge in order. PRs come from a fork, so each one also contains the
commits of the PRs before it: so **review only the last commit**.

- [ ] #3247 
- [ ] #3248
- [ ] #3249
- [ ] #3250
- [ ] #3251
- [ ] #3252
- [ ] #3253
- [ ] #3254
- [ ] #3255
- [ ] #3256
- [ ] #3257
- [ ] #3258
- [ ] #3259

## Outstanding tasks

- [ ] k8s-driver-manager: pause the manager during a driver reload, 
then raise the default `driver.manager` image version in Helm and the CSV to that release.
- [ ] go-nvml: switch to a tagged release.
- [ ] e2e tests in `tests/e2e`.

title: gpu-config [1/13]: add the GPU configuration state file
body: Part of #3246 (1/13). Depends on: none. Adds `internal/gpuconfig/statefile`: the node-local state file and lock that the GPU configuration manager and the `gpu-config` init container use to record the decision and the gate pass for each driver load. Not used yet. ---

title: gpu-config [2/13]: identify driver loads and driver readiness
body: Part of #3246 (2/13). Depends on: none. Review only the last commit. Adds `internal/gpuconfig/loadid`: the driver load ID (the inode of `/sys/module/nvidia`) and the driver readiness check, based on the validator's ready files. Not used yet. ---

title: gpu-config [3/13]: derive the sync label value
body: Part of #3246 (3/13). Depends on: #3247. Review only the last commit. Adds `internal/gpuconfig/status`: the value of the `nvidia.com/gpu-config.state` node label. Not used yet. ---

title: gpu-config [4/13]: parse the GPU configuration document
body: Part of #3246 (4/13). Depends on: none. Review only the last commit. Adds `internal/gpuconfig/config`: parsing and validation of the configuration document, matching GPUs to entries, and the document hash. `go.yaml.in/yaml/v2` becomes a direct dependency. Not used yet. ---

title: gpu-config [5/13]: apply GPU settings through NVML
body: Part of #3246 (5/13). Depends on: #3250. Review only the last commit. Adds `internal/gpuconfig/apply` (with `nvmllib` and a test fake): range checks, then writing power limit, locked clocks and ECC mode through NVML. Adds go-nvml as a direct dependency, at a pseudo-version that includes NVIDIA/go-nvml#216. A tagged release is tracked in #3246. Not used yet. ---

title: gpu-config [6/13]: decide when it is safe to apply GPU settings
body: Part of #3246 (6/13). Depends on: #3247, #3250, #3251. Review only the last commit. Adds `internal/gpuconfig/decision`: the once-per-driver-load decision to apply or skip. This is the safety-critical part. Not used yet. ---

title: gpu-config [7/13]: add the gate that holds GPU allocators
body: Part of #3246 (7/13). Depends on: #3247. Review only the last commit. Adds `internal/gpuconfig/gate`: the logic of the `gpu-config` init container, which holds GPU allocators until the manager has decided for the current driver load. Not used yet. ---

title: gpu-config [8/13]: publish the node status labels
body: Part of #3246 (8/13). Depends on: #3249, #3250, #3251. Review only the last commit. Adds `internal/gpuconfig/publish`: writes the `nvidia.com/gpu-config.*` status labels on the node. Not used yet. ---

title: gpu-config [9/13]: add the Kubernetes client of the GPU configuration manager
body: Part of #3246 (9/13). Depends on: #3248, #3250, #3252, #3253, #3254. Review only the last commit. Adds `internal/gpuconfig/kube`: the API client of the manager and the init container, including the document watches and the DRA claim and slice reads. Not used yet. ---

title: gpu-config [10/13]: add the GPU configuration manager main loop
body: Part of #3246 (10/13). Depends on: #3247 to #3255. Review only the last commit. Adds `internal/gpuconfig/applier`: the manager's per-node loop that binds to a driver load, decides once, and publishes status. Not used yet. ---

title: gpu-config [11/13]: add the GPU configuration manager binary and the validator step
body: Part of #3246 (11/13). Depends on: #3247 to #3256. Review only the last commit. Adds the `gpu-config-manager` binary, the only cgo-built command, and the validator's `gpu-config` component. Both go into the operator image, and go-nvml is added to `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. Nothing deploys them yet. ---

title: gpu-config [12/13]: deploy the GPU configuration manager from ClusterPolicy
body: Part of #3246 (12/13). Depends on: #3247 to #3257. Review only the last commit. Adds `spec.gpuConfigManager` (disabled by default) to ClusterPolicy, CRDs and Helm, the manager DaemonSet, the `gpu-config` init container in the validator, and the node deploy label. The init container is rendered on every cluster, so validator pods roll once on upgrade. ---

title: gpu-config [13/13]: deploy the GPU configuration manager from GPUCluster
body: Part of #3246 (13/13). Depends on: #3247 to #3258. Review only the last commit. Adds `spec.gpuConfigManager` to GPUCluster, the DRA-stack manager DaemonSet, and the `gpu-config` init container in the DRA kubelet plugin. Kubelet plugin pods roll once on upgrade. ---

title: Bump `k8s-operator-libs` to 2026-10-20 (42ee2fff224f)
body: **Superseded by https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/pull/3263 after the head-branch rename.** Addresses [#722](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cloud-native-team/issues/722) (Scalability: reduce log lines) This PR bumps `k8s-operator-libs` to the current version. `gpu-operator` main currently vendors `k8s-operator-libs` `d720f2557494` (2026-06-29). This version predates commit 60f980a (2026-08-24, "Index pods by controller UID in one pass"). In it, BuildState calls GetPodsOwnedbyDs once per driver DaemonSet with the full driver Pod list, so a pass writes (number of driver DaemonSets) x (number of driver pods) "Pod" log lines, plus a full Pod log dump for each pod of another driver DaemonSet. With more than one driver DaemonSet (precompiled kernel pools, NVIDIADriver CRs), this library bump reduces these lines. ## Baseline versus library bump | Workers | Scenario | Idle lines/s | Upgrade lines/s | Upgrade seconds | Upgrade lines | | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 500 | Baseline GPU Operator with its original pinned library | 2.300 | 457.488 | 232.332 | 106,289 | | 500 | Baseline GPU Operator with library bumped to `42ee2fff224f` (this PR) | 1.706 | 449.583 | 233.156 | 104,823 | | 2,500 | Baseline GPU Operator with its original pinned library | 4.267 | 471.600 | 1,231.013 | 580,546 | | 2,500 | Baseline GPU Operator with library bumped to `42ee2fff224f` (this PR) | 3.348 | 427.501 | 1,391.251 | 594,761 | Idle upgrade-library lines per complete pass (mean of two passes): | Workers | Baseline | Library bump | | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 500 | 341 | 252 | | 2,500 | 809 | 611.5 | Measurements use a kind control plane with KWOK workers, two driver DaemonSets, and a CPU-only simulated driver-upgrade workflow. Rates count all emitted operator output with info-level configuration and default production Zap sampling. One valid capture per phase and worker count was selected; every idle window includes two complete upgrade-library passes. The multiplicative count above describes logging calls before sampling. The foreign-pod call passes the full Pod object; the logger's encoder/development mode determines whether it is rendered as a full object or compact identifiers. Target: the 2026-10-20 snapshot `42ee2fff224f` (`v0.0.0-20261020171813-42ee2fff224f`). The baseline operator source was `0addf2f67b32`. The published source tree matches the benchmarked library-bump tree. Indexing change: [NVIDIA/k8s-operator-libs@60f980a](https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-operator-libs/commit/60f980a097cc03dfce0647473b8e54f91c297369). Related: https://github.com/NVIDIA/cloud-native-team/issues/722 ---

title: Improves structured logging and error handling across GPU Operator controllers.
body: ## Summary Improves structured logging and error handling across GPU Operator controllers. ## Changes - Replaces formatted log messages with structured logging fields for improved consistency and observability. - Updates version logging in `cmd/gpu-operator/main.go` to use structured logging. - Updates Service and DaemonSet transformation logs to use structured fields instead of `fmt.Sprintf`. - Updates runtime information logs to include node names, errors, and runtime details as structured fields. - Improves OpenShift version discovery error handling in `getContainerRuntime()`. - Returns the OpenShift version discovery error immediately when discovery fails, instead of continuing with container runtime detection using the node list. - Preserves the existing behavior when the OpenShift version endpoint returns HTTP 404, indicating that the cluster is not an OpenShift cluster. ## Testing - Added a regression test for OpenShift version discovery failure. - Verifies that the error is propagated, the runtime remains empty, and node listing is not attempted. - Ran `go test -count=1 ./controllers/clusterinfo`. - Ran `git diff --check`. title: Remove default MIG config ConfigMap
body:
## Issue

Part of #2913

## Description

The `default-mig-parted-config` ConfigMap was mounted into mig-manager as
`config-default.yaml`, a fallback for R535 drivers that cannot list MIG
profiles while MIG mode is disabled. R535 is no longer supported.

This reverts commit db0bb63ec. The `mig-parted-config` volume is again
added only when `migManager.config.name` is set. The certification suite
now selects the single-strategy profile from the custom ConfigMap when
one is set, and from the per-node ConfigMap otherwise.

ClusterPolicies created with a CRD before v26.3.0 can still have
`default-mig-parted-config` as `migManager.config.name`, because it was the
CRD default. The operator and the certification suite treat that name
as not set, so mig-manager uses the generated config.

NVIDIA/mig-parted#598 removes the matching fallback from mig-manager and
publishes the per-node ConfigMap also when a custom config is set.
Older mig-manager versions treat `DEFAULT_CONFIG_FILE` as optional. On
upgrade, an existing `default-mig-parted-config` ConfigMap stays until
the ClusterPolicy is deleted. Nothing reads it.

## Checklist

- [x] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes
- [ ] Lint checks passing (`make lint`)
- [ ] Generated assets in-sync (`make validate-generated-assets`)
- [ ] Go mod artifacts in-sync (`make validate-modules`)
- [ ] Test cases are added for new code paths

## Testing

`go test ./controllers/` passes, including the updated `TestMIGManager`
and `TestTransformMigManager`, which has a case for the old
ConfigMap name. The certification suite changes are
checked with `go build` and `go vet` only; they have no unit tests.

title: [Bug]: Missing H200 NVL (0x233B10DE) in default-mig-parted-config for all-1g.35gb
body:
### Description
In `default-mig-parted-config`, the `all-1g.35gb` profile is missing the PCI device ID `0x233B10DE` for **NVIDIA H200 NVL** (it currently only includes `0x233510DE` for H200 SXM and `0x31C210DE` for GB300).

Notably, `0x233B10DE` is already listed alongside `0x233510DE` in the `all-balanced` profile, and H200 NVL hardware supports four `1g.35gb` MIG instances per GPU.

Because of this omission, applying `nvidia.com/mig.config=all-1g.35gb` on an H200 NVL node results in a silent no-op: `nvidia-mig-manager` skips all GPUs, exits with code `0`, and falsely marks `nvidia.com/mig.config.state=success` while MIG remains disabled (or retains the previous MIG configuration).

### Environment
- **GPU**: 2x NVIDIA H200 NVL (PCI Device ID: `0x233B10DE`)
- **NVIDIA Driver**: `595.71.05` (CUDA `13.2`)
- **GPU Operator Version**: `<v25.10.1>`
- **Kubernetes Version**: `v1.33.5`
- **Container Runtime**: `containerd://2.1.4`
- **OS / Kernel**: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS / `6.8.0-71-generic`

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Deploy NVIDIA GPU Operator on a node equipped with NVIDIA H200 NVL (`0x233B10DE`).
2. Label the node with `nvidia.com/mig.config=all-1g.35gb`:
   ```bash
   kubectl label nodes <node-name> [nvidia.com/mig.config=all-1g.35gb](https://nvidia.com/mig.config=all-1g.35gb) --overwrite
   ```
3. Check the node labels and `nvidia-smi` output.

### Actual Behavior
- Node label reports `nvidia.com/mig.config.state=success`.
- `nvidia-smi` shows MIG mode is still `Disabled` (no `1g.35gb` instances created).
- `nvidia-mig-manager` logs show `mig-parted` skipping the H200 NVL GPUs due to the `device-filter` mismatch:
  ```text
  time="2026-11-19T23:10:14Z" level=debug msg="Applying MIG device configuration..."
  time="2026-11-19T23:10:14Z" level=debug msg="Walking MigConfig for (device-filter=[0x233510DE], devices=all)"
  time="2026-11-19T23:10:14Z" level=debug msg="Walking MigConfig for (device-filter=[0x31C210DE], devices=all)"
  time="2026-11-19T23:10:14Z" level=debug msg="Running apply-exit hook"
  MIG configuration applied successfully
  ```

### Expected Behavior
`all-1g.35gb` should match NVIDIA H200 NVL (`0x233B10DE`) and partition each GPU into 4x `1g.35gb` MIG instances.

### Proposed Fix
Add `"0x233B10DE"` to the `device-filter` under `all-1g.35gb` in `default-mig-parted-config`:

```yaml
  all-1g.35gb:
    # H200-141GB, H200 NVL
    - device-filter: ["0x233510DE", "0x233B10DE"]
      devices: all
      mig-enabled: true
      mig-devices:
        "1g.35gb": 4
    # GB300
    - device-filter: ["0x31C210DE"]
      devices: all
      mig-enabled: true
      mig-devices:
        "1g.35gb": 7
```

title: Clean up GPU node labels on stack deletion
body: ## Summary Deleting a `ClusterPolicy` or `GPUCluster` now removes that stack's node labels. The operator waits until the stack's operands are gone, removes the stack's `nvidia.com/gpu.deploy.*` labels, and then releases the CR. Labels that an independent `NVIDIADriver` driver still needs are kept. Fixes # This is the first of three stacked PRs. The base branch is `main`. ## Problem Today, deleting a stack CR leaves its deploy labels on every GPU node. The labels can point at operands that no longer exist, and a later install of the other stack starts with stale labels. The operator cannot clean up after the CR is gone, because nothing tells it which stack owned the labels. ## Changes ### Deletion lifecycle - The ClusterPolicy and GPUCluster controllers add the finalizer `nvidia.com/gpu-operator-node-cleanup`. ClusterPolicy adds it only after the singleton check and the GPUCluster conflict check. - When a CR is deleted, its controller tears down the operands and reports progress in a new `OperandsRemoved` condition. While the teardown runs, `Ready` is `False`. - The node-labeling controller removes the labels after `OperandsRemoved` is `True`, and then removes the finalizer. ### Operand teardown - The controller deletes the DaemonSets and Deployments that the CR controls directly. It uses foreground propagation and a UID precondition, and it checks again every 5 seconds until they are gone. Foreground deletion makes sure that their ReplicaSets and Pods are also gone. - ClusterPolicy also waits for the validator Pods that the CR owns directly (plugin and CUDA validation). These Pods can use GPUs, and their owner workloads do not track them. Succeeded validator Pods are left for garbage collection. - GPUCluster deletes the DRA providers (`nvidia-dra-driver-kubelet-plugin` and `nvidia-dra-driver-controller`) only after all other operand workloads are gone. Then the claim consumers can unprepare their claims. The existing `gpuClusterFinalizer` drain is kept and runs first. ### Node label cleanup - For ClusterPolicy, the controller removes the deploy labels that only the device-plugin stack uses. For GPUCluster, it removes `dra-driver`, `dra-validator`, `dcgm-dra`, and `dcgm-exporter-dra`. - Labels with the value `false` stay, so per-node opt-outs survive a reinstall. Discovery labels are not changed. - `gpu.deploy.driver` and `gpu.deploy.vgpu-manager` are removed only if all of these conditions are true: - No other stack CR exists that is not deleting. - No deleting ClusterPolicy is still tearing down its built-in driver. - No `NVIDIADriver` CR exists. - Node patches use an optimistic lock. A conflict is retried in the next pass. The finalizer is removed only after a pass finds no node to change. - While a cleanup is pending, the node-labeling controller does not add or remove stack labels. It also does not report the "both ClusterPolicy and GPUCluster exist" error, so a migration between stacks can continue. `NVIDIADriver` owner assignment continues. The driver auto-upgrade annotation is updated only for `NVIDIADriver`-managed drivers. - The node-labeling controller also reacts when `OperandsRemoved` becomes `True`, and when a node is deleted. ### Helm uninstall - The pre-delete hook (`cleanup-gpuclusters`) now deletes the `ClusterPolicy` and the `GPUCluster`, and waits until both are gone. Then the operator is still running while the finalizers complete. - By default, the hook selects the chart's CRs by name and by Helm release annotations. With `operator.cleanupCRD=true`, it deletes all stack CRs before the CRD cleanup hook runs. - The hook deletes with background propagation and a UID precondition. A missing CR or CRD is not an error, and read errors are retried. Helm `--timeout` limits the wait. The hook has no timeout of its own. - The README has a new section, "Recovering a Helm uninstall that times out". ## User-visible behavior changes - `kubectl delete clusterpolicy` and `kubectl delete gpucluster` now return only after the operands are gone and the labels are removed. Use `kubectl describe` to see the `OperandsRemoved` condition, which lists the workloads that still block the deletion. - `helm uninstall` now waits for the stack teardown. The default Helm timeout of 5m can be too short on large clusters. ## Known limitations - **Unreachable nodes:** Operand Pods on an unreachable node stay in Terminating, so the CR deletion and `helm uninstall` wait. The README describes how to recover. The current GPUCluster drain has the same behavior. - **Orphan deletion:** `--cascade=orphan` is not honored. The operator still deletes the operands and removes the labels. - **Downgrade:** After a rollback to an older chart, the new finalizer stays, and the older operator does not remove it. Remove `nvidia.com/gpu-operator-node-cleanup` from each CR before the rollback. - **Driver labels after a full uninstall:** With a chart-managed `NVIDIADriver`, the driver labels stay after a full uninstall. Helm removes the `NVIDIADriver` after the hook, and the `NVIDIADriver` controller does not clean labels on deletion. - **`k8s-driver-manager` restores labels:** A `k8s-driver-manager` init container that runs during the teardown can add labels again after cleanup, because it writes back values that it read earlier. The fix belongs in `k8s-driver-manager`. ## Testing - New unit tests in `controllers/source_lifecycle_test.go`, `controllers/nodelabeling_controller_test.go`, and `cmd/cleanup-gpuclusters/main_test.go` cover: - teardown ownership and the DRA order; - the validator Pod wait; - the label cleanup, including opt-outs, driver labels, and conflicts; - restart and failure paths; - the hook's delete and wait. - `make fmt` and `make unit-test` pass. - All CI checks pass, including `e2e-tests-containerd` and `e2e-tests-nvidiadriver`. - TODO: Test on an actual Kubernetes cluster with GPU Nodes. ---

title: Select the GPU allocator per node
body: ## Select the GPU allocator per node Part 2 of 3 in a stacked series. Base branch: `feature/node-label-cleanup`. ### Summary This PR adds per-node allocator selection(DRA/Device plugin). Each GPU node records whether it uses the device-plugin stack (`ClusterPolicy`) or the DRA stack (`GPUCluster`). The operator then places only the operands of the selected stack on that node. Mixed-stack activation stays disabled in this PR. The "both CRs exist" checks in the ClusterPolicy, GPUCluster, and node-labeling controllers are unchanged. ### Selection policy The new `internal/coexistence` package resolves the allocator for each node in this order: 1. The `nvidia.com/gpu.deploy.mode` label (`device-plugin` or `dra`), if an administrator set it. 2. The recorded selection in the `nvidia.com/gpu-operator.selected-allocator` annotation, if the recorded stack still exists. 3. The operator default from `operator.defaultGPUAllocationStack`, if it is set. 4. The only stack that exists. If both stacks exist, `device-plugin` is used. An invalid mode label or annotation closes placement for that node only. The node-labeling controller withdraws the operand labels and emits an `InvalidAllocatorSelection` Warning Event on the node. ### Node labeling - `selectNode` records the selection and applies the deploy labels of the selected stack. - A node that waits for an unavailable stack loses its operand labels. The `gpu.deploy.driver` and `gpu.deploy.vgpu-manager` labels stay. - The `gpu.deploy.dra-driver` label stays while pods with DRA claims run on the node. - A node is not changed until its selected source has the node-cleanup finalizer. This keeps running operands in place during an upgrade. - Node patches use optimistic locking, so a concurrent mode change cannot be overwritten. - Changes to any `nvidia.com/gpu.deploy.*` label or to the selection annotation start a reconcile. - Source cleanup removes the selection annotation of the deleted stack. ### Adoption gate (Initial upgrade to version with the changes) `ClusterPolicy` and `GPUCluster` now have a `NodeSelectionInitialized` condition. A source controller does not reconcile operands until each eligible GPU node has: - A selection record. - Compatible placement labels. - No enabled deploy labels of the other stack. The condition is set once and is not checked again after that. ### Operand placement Operand DaemonSets get a required node affinity on the mode label: - `ClusterPolicy` DaemonSets require the mode to be absent or `device-plugin`. The driver and vGPU manager DaemonSets are exempt, including the renamed precompiled and OpenShift DTK variants. - `GPUCluster` DaemonSets require the mode to be absent or `dra`. - `NVIDIADriver` DaemonSets are not changed. ### Other changes - The process-wide `defaultGPUWorkloadConfig` variable is removed. The sandbox default workload now comes from `ClusterPolicy.Spec.SandboxWorkloads` each time. Node labeling and adoption therefore no longer depend on when `ClusterPolicyController.init` runs. - Helm adds `operator.defaultGPUAllocationStack` (default `null`). The chart sets `DEFAULT_GPU_ALLOCATION_STACK` from this value. It rejects invalid values and rejects setting the variable through `operator.env`. The operator reads the value once at startup and exits if the value is invalid. ### Testing - `make fmt` - `make unit-test` - Helm render with `operator.defaultGPUAllocationStack=dra` - TODO: Test the changes on an actual Kubernetes cluster with GPU Nodes. ---

title: Allow ClusterPolicy and GPUCluster to coexist
body: ## Allow ClusterPolicy and GPUCluster to coexist Part 3 of 3 in a stacked series. Base branch: `feature/gpu-allocator-selection`. ### Summary This PR enables mixed-stack clusters. A `ClusterPolicy` (device-plugin stack) and a `GPUCluster` (DRA stack) can now exist together. Each GPU node uses the stack that the per-node selection from #3274 picks. Coexistence is supported only in ClusterPolicy-first order. The `ClusterPolicy` must be created before the `GPUCluster`, or in the same second. The "both CRs exist" checks in the ClusterPolicy, GPUCluster, and node-labeling controllers and in the Helm chart are removed. ### Creation order - Creation timestamps have second precision. Equal timestamps count as ClusterPolicy-first, so one Helm install can create both CRs. - A `ClusterPolicy` that is newer than the `GPUCluster` is rejected. The ClusterPolicy controller sets it to `NotReady` with the message "ClusterPolicy must be created before GPUCluster". - `resolveActiveConfig` hides a rejected `ClusterPolicy` from the node-labeling, GPUCluster, NVIDIADriver, and upgrade controllers. A rejected `ClusterPolicy` cannot change DRA placement or driver configuration. ### Admission policy A `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` and binding, both named `gpu-operator-clusterpolicy-creation`, deny `ClusterPolicy` creation while a `GPUCluster` exists. - The policy uses `GPUCluster` as its parameter kind, with `parameterNotFoundAction: Allow`. When no `GPUCluster` exists, creation is allowed. - `failurePolicy` is `Ignore`, so the policy does not block `ClusterPolicy` creation after the `GPUCluster` CRD is removed. The ClusterPolicy controller enforces the order if admission is not active yet. - The Helm chart renders the policy when the cluster serves the DRA `DeviceClass` API. The GPUCluster reconciler also creates or updates the policy, which covers OLM and other installs without Helm. - The resources have no owner references, so deleting a `GPUCluster` does not remove them. Helm removes them on uninstall. - RBAC for `validatingadmissionpolicies` and `validatingadmissionpolicybindings` is added to `config/rbac/role.yaml`. The Helm ClusterRole and the OLM CSV already grant it. ### DRA prerequisites While an active `ClusterPolicy` exists, the DRA stack starts only when all of these are true: 1. `spec.hostPaths.rootFS` is empty or `/` (`HostRootPrerequisiteNotMet`). 2. The driver is disabled or `driver.useNvidiaDriverCRD=true` (`DriverPrerequisiteNotMet`). 3. The `ClusterPolicy` has `NodeSelectionInitialized=True` (`NodeAdoptionPending`). The GPUCluster reconciler and node placement use the same function, `clusterPolicyCoexistenceBlocker`, so the two cannot disagree. `GPUCluster` adoption stays pending while DRA placement is not eligible. A prerequisite change during adoption therefore cannot complete adoption. ### Host root The DRA stack uses `/` as the host root (see #2572). - After the `GPUCluster` has `NodeSelectionInitialized=True`, the operator ignores changes to the ClusterPolicy `rootFS`. ClusterPolicy operands and `NVIDIADriver` drivers continue to use `/`. The ClusterPolicy controller emits a `HostRootIgnored` Warning Event. - After the `GPUCluster` is removed, the saved `rootFS` takes effect and the operands roll out. - The driver renderer normalizes an empty host root to `/`. Existing driver DaemonSets that hashed an empty root keep their config digest, so this upgrade does not roll drivers. - The ClusterPolicy and NVIDIADriver controllers reconcile again when a `GPUCluster` finishes adoption or is removed. ### Node labeling - Node labeling continues while a source is in teardown. Nodes of the deleting stack stay reserved until their cleanup is observed. Other nodes keep their assignment to the surviving stack. - A failed source cleanup is logged and retried. It does not stop labeling on other nodes. - Node labeling also reconciles when a `GPUCluster` finishes adoption. ### Helm - The chart no longer rejects `clusterPolicy.deployCR=true` together with `gpuCluster.deployCR=true`. - The new template `allocator-coexistence-policy.yaml` renders the admission policy and binding. ### Known limitations - Coexistence does not support a custom host root. A `ClusterPolicy` with a `rootFS` other than `/` blocks the `GPUCluster`. A future `NVIDIADriver` field or operator setting can remove this limit. - A `ClusterPolicy` cannot be created again while a `GPUCluster` exists. To change the order, delete the `GPUCluster` first. ### Testing - `make fmt` - `make unit-test` - Helm render with the DRA API enabled, to verify that the output includes the admission policy and binding - TODO: Test the changes on an actual Kubernetes cluster with GPU nodes. ---

title: Do not update status on unpopulated CR when Get fails
body: ## Issue Fixes #3190 ## Description When .Get fails with a non-404 error (such as transient API server connection issues, context timeouts, or client rate limiting), ClusterPolicyReconciler and NVIDIADriverReconciler previously called .conditionUpdater.SetConditionsError on an unpopulated custom resource object whose .metadata.name is empty (""). Because SetConditionsError attempts to fetch the CR by name ( ypes.NamespacedName{Name: cr.Name}), this triggered a secondary error: ` failed to get instance for status update: resource name may not be empty ` which obscured the original Get failure and polluted controller logs. This PR aligns both reconcilers with the pattern already established in GPUClusterReconciler: when .Get fails on an unpopulated instance, log the error and surface it directly for requeue without attempting to set conditions on an empty CR. ## Checklist - [x] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes - [x] Lint checks passing (make lint) - [x] Generated assets in-sync (make validate-generated-assets) - [x] Go mod artifacts in-sync (make validate-modules) - [x] Test cases are added for new code paths ## Testing - Added unit tests in controllers/clusterpolicy_controller_test.go (TestClusterPolicyReconcileGetFailureDoesNotUpdateCondition) and controllers/nvidiadriver_controller_test.go (TestNVIDIADriverReconcileGetFailureDoesNotUpdateCondition) asserting that non-404 .Get errors are returned directly without invoking SetConditionsError. - Executed all controller unit tests (go test ./controllers/...) in WSL and confirmed they pass. - Verified linting via golangci-lint run ./controllers/.... ---

title: Add make target to deploy Mokka
body: ## Issue This PR is part of this [issue](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cloud-native-team/issues/600) to Add mokka to gpu-operator repo for testing. The goal of this PR is to integrate mokka into the gpu-operator repo so that we can run tests with a simulated gpu setup. Fixes # https://github.com/NVIDIA/cloud-native-team/issues/600 The earlier PR #3089 ported the bash e2e to Ginkgo. For now, this PR will run 16 of the 29 tests (9 tests require a driver and 4 tests require CUDA which is not supported with Mokka at the moment). For the clusterpolicy the e2e tests (11) brings up every operand; no repeated restarts; device plugin env vars; MIG strategy; standalone DCGM; time-slicing; remove and restore GFD; remove and restore DCGM exporter; operator restart; node opt-out and opt-in; and in the sandbox-workloads group, operand readiness with sandbox support enabled for container workloads (it does not run a sandboxed GPU workload). For the nvidia-driver (5) the tests renders the default NVIDIADriver (3 specs); brings up every operand; no repeated restarts. ## Description **tests/e2e/Makefile**: We will create two targets, _mokka-e2e_ which will run the script /scripts/run-mokka.sh and mokka-clean which will delete the mokka cluster. **tests/scripts/run-mokka.sh**: We will include the following Settings options: "${MOKKA_CHART:=oci://ghcr.io/nvidia/k8s-test-infra/chart/nvml-mock}" "${MOKKA_VERSION:=0.6.0}" "${MOKKA_GPU_PROFILE:=t4}" "${MOKKA_LABEL_FILTER:=(clusterpolicy || nvidia-driver) && !cuda-workload && !driver-container}" ...we will then verify prerequisites, create the cluster, build the operator and load it via make build-image, and install Mokka helm chart. We will then run the tests. It calls the existing e2e-test target in tests/e2e/Makefile. For the Ginkgo suite, each test group installs the operator with Helm, checks it, and uninstalls it. When it finishes, the cluster is left running so a rerun is faster. make -C tests/e2e mokka-clean deletes it. Because of set -euo pipefail on line 2, the script stops at the first failing step. **tests/e2e/mokka/gpu-operator-values.yaml**: The following operands will be disabled: driver.enabled: false, toolkit.enabled: false, migManager.enabled: false. GFD_MACHINE_TYPE_FILE=/etc/nvml-mock/machine-type, Mokka writes its own machine-type file, which is mounted through its CDI config, and this setting points GPU feature discovery at it. For the validator: validator.driver DISABLE_DEV_CHAR_SYMLINK_CREATION=true: the driver check normally creates symlinks under /dev/char but with a fake driver those device files aren't real, so the setting skips just that step. validator.cuda WITH_WORKLOAD=false: the CUDA check runs a small CUDA program, vectorAdd, by default, as Mokka can't run GPU code, so this switches the check to configuration only. **tests/e2e/nvidiadriver/nvidiadriver.go, tests/e2e/clusterpolicy/sandbox_workloads.go, tests/e2e/clusterpolicy/clusterpolicy.go**: We will need to switch from _DefaultOperandSelectors_ to _EnabledOperandSelectors_ in order to exclude the driver and toolkit which Mokka turns off. We will need to add ginkgo.Label("cuda-workload") and ginkgo.Label("driver-container") to corresponding tests. ## Checklist - [ ] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes - [ ] Lint checks passing (`make lint`) - [ ] Generated assets in-sync (`make validate-generated-assets`) - [ ] Go mod artifacts in-sync (`make validate-modules`) - [ ] Test cases are added for new code paths ## Testing ``` local-agadiyar@ipp2-2271:~/gpu-operator$ MOKKA_SKIP_BUILD=true make -C tests/e2e mokka-e2e make: Entering directory '/localhome/local-agadiyar/gpu-operator/tests/e2e' MOKKA_CLUSTER_NAME=gpu-operator-mokka /localhome/local-agadiyar/gpu-operator/tests/e2e/../scripts/run-mokka.sh Reusing kind cluster gpu-operator-mokka Set kubectl context to "kind-gpu-operator-mokka" Image: "localhost/gpu-operator:mokka-dev" with ID "sha256:50167a5b8073ef7772ab752920328c601e49a73181f4684ab42388a8d3b3aacc" not yet present on node "gpu-operator-mokka-control-plane", loading... NAME: nvml-mock LAST DEPLOYED: Tue Nov 24 00:39:46 2026 NAMESPACE: mokka STATUS: deployed REVISION: 3 TEST SUITE: None NOTES: .................... .................... === RUN TestE2E I1124 00:39:49.405210 2677410 e2e_test.go:65] Starting e2e run "99e9090d-3adb-4ac4-a016-e61b1f8070d2" on Ginkgo node 1 Running Suite: GPU Operator e2e suite - /localhome/local-agadiyar/gpu-operator/tests/e2e ======================================================================================== Random Seed: 1795480789 Will run 16 of 29 specs •••••••••••••••• Ran 16 of 29 Specs in 368.657 seconds SUCCESS! -- 16 Passed | 0 Failed | 0 Pending | 13 Skipped --- PASS: TestE2E (368.66s) PASS ok github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/tests/e2e 368.676s make[1]: Leaving directory '/localhome/local-agadiyar/gpu-operator/tests/e2e' make: Leaving directory '/localhome/local-agadiyar/gpu-operator/tests/e2e' ``` ---

title: [Bug]: Self-certification restore turns NVIDIADriver autoUpgrade: false into true
body:
**Motivation**
The self-certification suite should leave the ClusterPolicy and NVIDIADriver CRs as it found them. It changes the driver upgrade policy instead.

- [x] I would like to work on this issue.

**Describe the bug**
`OriginalSettings` (`internal/certification/original_settings.go`) captures the CRs as typed structs and restores each one with a JSON patch that replaces `/spec` with `json.Marshal(spec)`. Fields that have `omitempty` and a CRD default lose an explicit zero value in that round trip, and the API server applies the default instead:

- NVIDIADriver `upgradePolicy.autoUpgrade: false` becomes `true`.
- `upgradePolicy.maxParallelUpgrades: 0` becomes `1`, in both CRs.
- ClusterPolicy `driver.upgradePolicy.drain.timeoutSeconds` and `podDeletion.timeoutSeconds` of `0` become `300`.

So a cluster that had automatic driver upgrades turned off has them turned on once the suite has run. The restored spec also never equals the captured one, so every later `Restore` patches the CRs again and deletes all driver pods, even after a TestSet that didn't touch the driver.

**To Reproduce**
kind v0.33.0 (Kubernetes v1.37.0) with only the CRDs from `config/crd/bases` (main at 877c9860), no operator and no GPU needed:

1. Create the ClusterPolicy from `config/samples/v1_clusterpolicy.yaml` with `driver.upgradePolicy.maxParallelUpgrades: 0`, and the NVIDIADriver from `config/samples/nvidia_v1alpha1_nvidiadriver.yaml` with `upgradePolicy.autoUpgrade: false` and `maxParallelUpgrades: 0`.
2. Call `CaptureOriginalSettings`, change the driver version in both CRs like a TestSet does, then call `restoreClusterPolicy` and `restoreNVIDIADrivers` twice.

```
captured         NVIDIADriver: autoUpgrade=false maxParallelUpgrades=0 version=620.70.06 | ClusterPolicy: maxParallelUpgrades=0 version=
test set ran     NVIDIADriver: autoUpgrade=false maxParallelUpgrades=0 version=999.0.0 | ClusterPolicy: maxParallelUpgrades=0 version=999.0.0
restore 1: restoreClusterPolicy=true restoreNVIDIADrivers=true
after restore 1  NVIDIADriver: autoUpgrade=true maxParallelUpgrades=1 version=620.70.06 | ClusterPolicy: maxParallelUpgrades=1 version=
restore 2 (no change in between): restoreClusterPolicy=true restoreNVIDIADrivers=true
```

**Expected behavior**
The restore puts back the specs it captured, explicit `false` and `0` values included, and does nothing when nothing changed since. I'd keep the CRs as the API server returned them (unstructured) and send that spec back; I have the change and a unit test ready.

**Environment (please provide the following information):**
 - GPU Operator Version: main (877c9860)
 - OS: kind node image (kindest/node:v1.37.0)
 - Kernel Version: not relevant, no GPU involved
 - Container Runtime Version: containerd (kind)
 - Kubernetes Distro and Version: kind v0.33.0, Kubernetes v1.37.0

The pod, DaemonSet and log attachments don't apply: the reproduction only needs the CRDs.

title: [Bug]: Self-certification GDRCopy test can bind its pod to a node without a GPU
body:
**Motivation**
The GDRCopy TestSet of the self-certification suite can fail on clusters that run the driver through NVIDIADriver CRs, depending on which node it picks.

- [x] I would like to work on this issue.

**Describe the bug**
In NVIDIADriver mode, `GDRCopyEligibleNodes` (`internal/certification/k8s/driver.go`) lists the nodes that match each non-precompiled NVIDIADriver's `nodeSelector`. With an empty `nodeSelector`, which the OLM example and the sample use, that is every node in the cluster, control-plane and CPU-only nodes included. A non-empty `nodeSelector` can still match nodes without a GPU, and GPU nodes the operator assigned to another NVIDIADriver, such as a precompiled one.

The GDRCopy test then picks one of these nodes for its workload pod, sets `nodeName` and requests `nvidia.com/gpu: 1`. When the pick is a node without a GPU, the kubelet rejects the pod and the test fails. The ClusterPolicy branch of the same function already uses `GetGPUNodes`.

**To Reproduce**
kind v0.33.0 (Kubernetes v1.37.0), one node without any GPU label, the CRDs from `config/crd/bases` (main at 877c9860) and the NVIDIADriver from `config/samples/nvidia_v1alpha1_nvidiadriver.yaml` (`nodeSelector: {}`, `usePrecompiled: false`). Calling `GDRCopyEligibleNodes` returns the control-plane node:

```
GDRCopyEligibleNodes = map[gpuop-cert-control-plane:true], err = <nil>
```

**Expected behavior**
The eligible nodes are the ones whose driver pods the NVIDIADriver manages: its `nodeSelector` plus `nvidia.com/gpu.present=true` and `nvidia.com/gpu-operator.driver.owner=<name>`, which is how `getNodePools` selects the nodes for the CR's driver DaemonSets. I have the change and a unit test ready.

**Environment (please provide the following information):**
 - GPU Operator Version: main (877c9860)
 - OS: kind node image (kindest/node:v1.37.0)
 - Kernel Version: not relevant, no GPU involved
 - Container Runtime Version: containerd (kind)
 - Kubernetes Distro and Version: kind v0.33.0, Kubernetes v1.37.0

The pod, DaemonSet and log attachments don't apply: the reproduction only needs the CRDs and the node labels.

title: Select GDRCopy test nodes like the operator selects driver nodes
body: ## Issue Fixes #3290 ## Description In NVIDIADriver mode, `GDRCopyEligibleNodes` listed the nodes that match each non-precompiled CR's `nodeSelector`, which includes nodes without a GPU (all nodes when the `nodeSelector` is empty) and GPU nodes the operator assigned to another NVIDIADriver. The GDRCopy test binds its workload pod to one of them with `nodeName`, so the pod could land on a node without a GPU and be rejected by the kubelet. This selects the nodes the way `getNodePools` does for the CR's driver DaemonSets: the `nodeSelector` plus `nvidia.com/gpu.present=true` and the `nvidia.com/gpu-operator.driver.owner` label set to the CR's name. The ClusterPolicy branch is unchanged. ## Checklist - [x] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes - [x] Lint checks passing (`make lint`) - [x] Generated assets in-sync (`make validate-generated-assets`) - [x] Go mod artifacts in-sync (`make validate-modules`) - [x] Test cases are added for new code paths ## Testing `TestDriverNodeSelector` checks which node labels the selector matches. On main it also matches a node without a GPU, a node without a GPU that is in the `nodeSelector`, and a GPU node owned by another NVIDIADriver. On kind with the sample NVIDIADriver, `GDRCopyEligibleNodes` now returns nothing for a node without GPU labels, returns the node once it has `nvidia.com/gpu.present=true` and the owner label for the CR, and returns nothing when the owner label names another NVIDIADriver. No API, manifest or dependency changes. ---

title: Restore certification CRs from the specs the API server returned
body: ## Issue Fixes #3289 ## Description `OriginalSettings` restored the ClusterPolicy and NVIDIADriver CRs by marshaling their typed specs. Fields that have `omitempty` and a CRD default lose an explicit zero value that way, and the API server applies the default instead, so an NVIDIADriver `upgradePolicy.autoUpgrade: false` came back as `true` and `maxParallelUpgrades: 0` as `1`. The restored spec then never matched the captured one, so every later `Restore` patched the CRs again and deleted all driver pods. This keeps the CRs as the API server returned them and sends that spec back. `k8s.Clients` gets `GetClusterPolicyUnstructured` and `ListNVIDIADriversUnstructured`, and `GetClusterPolicy` and `ListNVIDIADrivers` now use them. The capture and restore code takes a small `crClient` interface, which `*k8s.Clients` implements, so the test can use an in-memory fake. Change detection compares the unstructured specs, and a driver restart is still triggered by changes under `driver`, `gdrcopy` and `gds`. ## Checklist - [x] No secrets, sensitive information, or unrelated changes - [x] Lint checks passing (`make lint`) - [x] Generated assets in-sync (`make validate-generated-assets`) - [x] Go mod artifacts in-sync (`make validate-modules`) - [x] Test cases are added for new code paths ## Testing `TestRestoreKeepsExplicitZeroValues` captures CRs that have `autoUpgrade: false`, `maxParallelUpgrades: 0` and `drain.timeoutSeconds: 0`, changes the driver version, restores, and checks that those values are still in the restored specs and that a second restore patches nothing. It fails on main with `[spec upgradePolicy autoUpgrade] is missing from the restored spec` (and the same for the other three fields). On kind with the CRDs from this branch, the reproduction from the issue now gives: ``` after restore 1 NVIDIADriver: autoUpgrade=false maxParallelUpgrades=0 version=620.70.06 | ClusterPolicy: maxParallelUpgrades=0 version= restore 2 (no change in between): restoreClusterPolicy=false restoreNVIDIADrivers=false ``` No API, manifest or dependency changes. ---
